  • I. Project Summary
    • What it is
    • Repository Structure
    • What each tool does
      • tools/summarize/ —— AI Conversation Daily / Weekly / Monthly Reports
      • tools/research/ —— Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis
      • tools/benchmark/ —— Performance Benchmarking SuiteCross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarking tool, measuring floating-point performance uniformly across different hardware vendors and precision levels. Supports actual GPU execution for NVIDIA(CUDA), Apple Silicon(MPS), and Intel(XPU) (OpenCL may only appear in --info detection), covering precisions such as FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8(experimental). Measurement uses Warm-up + Formal Measurement + Statistical Analysis (median, IQR outlier removal), and explicitly performs GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy. Results are accumulated in CSV in append mode (never overwrites, naturally supports multi-hardware cumulative leaderboards), can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards with Plotly charts, and supports deployment to Hugo websites and submission to public leaderboards.
      • tools/website/ —— Hugo Blog
      • tools/translator/ —— Gradio Document Translator
      • common/ —— Shared Infrastructure Package
      • scripts/ —— Ops and Maintenance Scripts
      • ../ai-companion/ —— Independent Repository
      • outputs/ —— Output Directory

What is it?Gadgets (repository directory name gadget) is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development, covering five major directions: AI Daily Report Generation, Paper Discovery, Performance Benchmarking, Blog Automation, and Document Translation, open-sourced under the GPL-3 license.

      • ④ Website (tools/website/) —— Hugo Blog

    • Reproducing

The gadget README.md (20,768 characters) handed verbatim to 58 models, asking for a project summary and then a usage tutorial in Chinese. Grouped by the tool that called them.

下面是开源项目 gadget 的 README。请你完成两件事：
1. 先用中文总结这个项目：它是什么、仓库结构、每个工具分别做什么。
2. 然后写一份详细的中文使用教程，面向第一次接触这个项目的人，覆盖环境准备、安装、配置，以及每个工具的典型用法（给出可以直接复制的命令）。
只依据 README 里写到的内容，不要编造 README 中没有出现的命令或参数。

===== README.md =====
<README.md 全文，20 768 字符>

Summarize the project in Chinese, then write a detailed Chinese tutorial for a first-time user with copy-pasteable commands. Use only what the README says; do not invent commands or flags.

Conditions: one run per model, no system prompt — read the numbers as orders of magnitude. Cloud models ran serially through their agent CLIs (codex exec / claude -p / cursor-agent --print) in an empty directory, prompt on stdin, so time includes CLI startup. Local models ran cold on an RTX 5090 and their speed is pure decode, so the two speeds are not comparable. Fable 5.1 had --effort high pinned; the other Claude models used the default effort.

Metrics (all regex): “Commands” counts code-block lines starting with pip, python, cd, bash and similar; “Not in README” counts those that, comments stripped and whitespace collapsed, cannot be found in the README; “Facts” is how many of 16 word-for-word README facts the output mentions, and “Missed” lists the rest.

Part One: Project Summary

What are Gadgets

Gadgets (repository directory named gadget/) is a set of daily development tools covering five types of needs: AI conversation summarization, paper research, performance testing, blog publishing, and document translation.

The five tools under tools/ can be used independently. They share the common/ package in the repository root, which provides capabilities such as LLM calls, caching, file writing, translation, and Hugo deployment.

The development workflow and Claude Code skills are placed in another repository, ai-companion, located in the sibling directory ../ai-companion/, and integrated via hooks from this repository.

Repository Structure

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报、周报、月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图分析
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客、媒体压缩、构建和发布
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 工具共用的基础能力
├── scripts/            # 同步、机器配置、检查等维护脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、计划、审计报告、历史归档
├── outputs/            # 可重新生成的输出，已被 Git 忽略
├── AGENTS.md           # AI agent 工作协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 打包与安装配置

Enter tools/<工具名>/ to modify tool logic; enter common/ to modify common capabilities; check scripts/sync.py to modify synchronization logic; enter the independent ai-companion repository to modify development workflows or skills.

What the Five Tools Do

Tool Main Function Key Features
Summarize Generates daily, weekly, and monthly reports from AI conversations Supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, and general JSON; supports merging after multi-device export; statistics for token usage and costs
Research Discovers papers, analyzes papers and researchers, and analyzes citation relationships Searches sources like arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, etc.; provides three-stage LLM evaluation, full paper analysis, OpenReview comment analysis, and researcher profiling
Benchmark Measures CPU/GPU floating-point performance Actual GPU testing supports CUDA, Apple MPS, Intel XPU; covers multiple precisions; results appended to CSV, can generate interactive HTML reports
Website Builds and publishes Hugo blogs Uses PaperMod theme; incremental compression of images and videos; bilingual translation with local models; pushes to GitHub Pages after building
Translator Translates text and files in the browser Based on Gradio; supports .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, and images; protects content like code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc., in Markdown

common/ also includes JSON parsing and repair, SHA-256 disk caching with namespaces and TTL, atomic writes, and content hashing. scripts/ is responsible for operations; ai-companion is responsible for code change tracking, testing and HTML reports, as well as development processes like /idea → /ccplan → /ccedit.

Part Two: Beginner’s Tutorial

All following commands are from the provided README. Except for Benchmark and commands explicitly containing cd, they are executed in the gadget/ repository root by default.

**2. Install Python Packages and Tool Dependencies**

Note: all does not include Translator. If a translator is needed, install it separately:

Value Meaning

Translation functionality uses local inference. Special attention is needed as the README’s description of the default translation model varies:

  • The Environment Requirements and Notes sections describe Ollama defaulting to gemma4:26b, while other in-process backends use tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B.

Therefore, based solely on this README, one cannot assert that all translation paths default to the same model.

4. Optional: Machine Initialization and Basic Checks

If you wish to configure a new machine, the README provides two paths:

  • Repository-level initialization: Run scripts/onboard.py after filling in tokens/onboard.yaml. It will configure SSH, Claude/Codex installation and authentication, pip extras, ai-companion, tool settings, and rclone bootstrap. The README does not provide the full execution command or YAML examples.
  • Ubuntu server-level initialization: The script is located in the ai-companion repository and supports Ubuntu 22.04/24.04. You can view its help first:
bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

The --companion-repo of the server script should point to the ai-companion repository git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git; after splitting, --companion-ref is no longer required. The README does not provide the full installation command.

After installation, a read-only smoke test can be run:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

It checks the --help, --info, and imports of each tool, without calling LLMs, accessing the network, or writing files.

5. Summarize: Generate AI Conversation Reports

The typical workflow is: export conversation logs from each device → sync via cloud drive or manual aggregation → merge daily to generate daily reports → generate weekly and monthly reports after daily reports have accumulated.

Phase one, export all dates that have not yet been exported:

python -m summarize daily export

In multi-device scenarios, each device exports separately, then records are aggregated. Phase two, sync all dates and merge them daily:

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Generate a weekly report for a specified week based on existing daily reports, and deploy:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

Generate a monthly report for a specified month based on existing daily reports, and deploy:

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

2026-W12 and 2026-02 are example values from the README; replace them with the target week or month when in use.

You can also run the full automated process:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

It executes export, merge, weekly report, monthly report, and deployment.

This tool uses the source-specific namespace command of ccusage 20.x to count tokens and costs for each agent CLI. The README does not provide the installation command for ccusage, conversation source paths, or exported data formats.

The old daily_summary.py, weekly_summary.py, and monthly_summary.py entry points are still compatible, but using the above python -m summarize format is recommended.

6. Research: Discover Papers, Analyze Researchers, and Citation Relationships

Research uses a single entry point tools/research/research_scout.py.

Run a complete paper research workflow for a project:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

It executes search, three-stage evaluation, and report generation. The three stages are rapid screening, in-depth evaluation, and citation impact analysis.

my-project is an example project name. The README does not explain how projects are defined or provide the project configuration format, so project configuration cannot be completed based solely on this README.

Search using natural language:

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

This command will automatically select the search source.

Generate researcher profiles:

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

The profiling feature combines arXiv, Semantic Scholar, and LLM to analyze research trajectories, calculate hierarchy scores, and discover mentor-student relationships through homepage information and co-authorship patterns. It also supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup.

Analyze paper citation graphs:

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Input supports arXiv ID or DOI; analysis includes forward citations, backward references, and LLM impact interpretation.

Deploy research reports to Hugo:

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

The README also introduces --insight in-depth paper analysis: downloading full texts, analyzing writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable knowledge, matching OpenReview comments, and synthesizing cross-paper writing guides. However, it does not provide a complete invocation example, so speculative commands are not concatenated here.

7. Benchmark: Test CPU/GPU Performance

Benchmark commands have special directory requirements: enter tools/benchmark/ first.

cd tools/benchmark

Run all tests:

python -m benchmark.cli

Test CPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Test GPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

Run tests and generate an HTML report:

python -m benchmark.cli --report

The /benchmark/ to run tests, generate reports, and publish to Hugo:

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

These are different running methods; choose according to your needs.

Testing uses warm-up, formal measurement, median statistics, and IQR outlier removal, and explicitly synchronizes the GPU. Results are saved to a CSV in an append mode, making it easy to accumulate scores for various hardware.

Actual GPU testing supports NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Silicon MPS, and Intel XPU. OpenCL may appear in the detection results of --info, but it is not listed as an actual GPU testing backend in the README. Precision includes FP64, FP32, FP16, BF16, and experimental FP8.

The README mentions a public leaderboard submission feature but does not provide the submission command, nor does it give specific hardware driver installation steps.

After execution, subsequent tool commands must be run after returning to the gadget/ root directory in the terminal.

8. Website: Preview and Publish Hugo Blog

If Website extras are not yet installed, execute in the root directory:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Local preview:

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

-D indicates including drafts during preview.

Build and publish on macOS/Linux:

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

On Windows, execute in the repository root:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

The Windows script will enter its own directory automatically.

The publish script performs incremental media compression, Hugo builds, and pushes to Pages. Incremental compression is based on .last_build: images use pngquant, and videos use HandBrakeCLI.

These update scripts will publish the website, not just generate a local preview. The corresponding site in the README is https://tzj2006.github.io/, and the deployment repository is tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io; the README does not explain how to change to your own site or configure push authentication.

Automatically generated content is written directly to:

  • tools/website/content
  • tools/website/static

These files carry a gadget_generated marker; handwritten files without this marker will not be overwritten.

tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository that is automatically committed and pushed by the build script; do not commit directly to it.

9. Translator: Translate Documents in the Browser

Install dependencies in the repository root:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Start the interface:

python -m translator

It will open the Gradio GUI in your browser. You can translate text, .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, or image files through the interface, and switch models via the interface’s model management.

Language selection behavior:

  • When the source language is set to auto, it detects based on the proportion of CJK characters in the text.
  • When the target language is set to auto, it toggles between Chinese and English.

The translator reuses common.engine.create_engine() to automatically select the backend: if the model tag has been pulled, it prioritizes Ollama; the fallback for Windows is transformers, Linux prioritizes vLLM, and low-VRAM scenarios provide llamacpp/GGUF options.Models will reside in memory; models are lazy-loaded on demand when switching. Discrepancies between the default model and environment requirements have been explained in the configuration section. The README does not provide commands for manually pulling models, specifying ports, or translating command-line files.

10. Data Synchronization and Output Management

Synchronization is centrally managed by scripts/sync.py, which requires pre-configuring rclone. The configuration is located in the sync section of the root directory config.json.

The basic entry point provided in the README is:

python scripts/sync.py

Cross-device push and pull:

python scripts/sync.py push

python scripts/sync.py pull

The script also supports status, bootstrap, and config operations, covering categories such as summarize, website, research, benchmark, and backups; a special dag category is used to generate and deploy DAG sites. The README does not provide the complete command syntax for these categories.

For Summarize, the local Ollama auxiliary script also provides the following environment loading command:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

This script is used to create an Ollama variant suitable for Summarize and output environment settings; it is not the Ollama installation command provided in the README.

Regular generated artifacts are concentrated in:

outputs/
├── logs/         # 导出日志、运行日志等中间产物
├── reports/      # Markdown、JSON、HTML 报告
├── cache/        # LLM 缓存、搜索缓存
├── data/         # CSV、JSON 画像等结构化数据
├── images/       # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/      # 强制覆盖操作的备份

Website content is a clear exception: it is written directly to tools/website/content|static, with no separate outputs/site staging directory.

Do not include auto-generated content, rclone sync data, build/, gadget.egg-info/, or the deployment and theme repositories under Website in the repository commits.

python scripts/sync.py pull

Before use, you need to configure rclone and the sync section of the root directory config.json. Synchronization overwrites summarize, website, research, benchmark, backups, and includes the special dag category used for generating and deploying DAG sites. The README also lists status, bootstrap, and config functions, but does not provide detailed parameters.

Run a read-only smoke check:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

This check covers help information, detection information, and imports; it does not call LLMs, access the network, or write files. It can be used for basic checks but cannot prove that API, synchronization, or publishing processes have been successfully configured.

Load environment settings from the local LLM auxiliary script output in Bash:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

The README states that this script is used to create Ollama variants optimized for Summarize and output environment settings, but does not expand on the full service preparation steps.

There are two paths for new machine initialization:

  • Repository-level initialization: Fill in tokens/onboard.yaml, then run scripts/onboard.py, used for SSH, Claude/Codex installation authentication, pip extras, ai-companion, tool configuration, and rclone initialization. The README does not provide YAML fields or complete execution commands.
  • Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 system-level installation: The script is located in the independent ai-companion repository; you can view its help first:
bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

ai-companion should be at the same level as ../ai-companion/ and requires Node.js 18+. The README provides the repository address git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git, but does not provide complete installation commands; installation instructions point to its scripts/install.ts.

XI. Where to Find Results After Running

Generated results are usually concentrated in:

outputs/
├── logs/       # 导出日志、运行日志等中间产物
├── reports/    # Markdown、JSON、HTML 最终报告
├── cache/      # LLM 和搜索缓存
├── data/       # CSV、JSON profiles 等结构化数据
├── images/     # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/    # 强制覆盖时的备份

Website content follows explicit special paths: written directly to tools/website/content and tools/website/static, with no outputs/site temporary directory.

Do not include automatically generated content, rclone synchronized data, build artifacts, or the deployment and theme repositories under tools/website/ in the gadget’s Git commits.

This README is sufficient to provide installation entry points and typical running commands, but complete configuration still requires the TUTORIAL.md it points to, configuration examples, and documentation for each tool; the above does not supplement these unprovided contents.

II. Getting Started from Scratch#

The following commands are all from the provided README. Unless otherwise noted, run them in the Gadgets repository root.

1. Environment Preparation and Installation#

Python 3.10 or higher is required. The README recommends using a conda environment named AI:

conda activate AI

If using the independent ai-companion repository, Node.js 18 or higher is also required. For specific dependencies of each tool, see the requirements.txt in its directory.

Install the shared package and dependencies for summarize, research, benchmark, and website:

all does not include translator. When translation tools are needed, install separately:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

When preparing only blog-related dependencies, the command given by the README is:

pip install -e ".[website]"

2. Configuration#

Tool configurations are located in config.json at the repository root: create this file using config.example.json as a template. The README does not list specific fields and values; check the template before modifying. GADGET_CONFIG can be used to specify other configuration file paths.

LLM functionality uses local Ollama by default; other backends listed in the README include claude_cli, anthropic, and openai, which can be selected via the --api parameter of each tool, or specified globally using GADGET_LLM_BACKEND. claude_cli reuses the login status of the Claude Code CLI; anthropic and openai involve respective API credentials. The README does not provide steps for filling in credentials.Translation uses local inference. The README lists GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND to select the translation backend and GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL to override the default translation model. Models may be downloaded upon first use. tokens/ stores API keys and new machine configuration tables; it is Git-ignored, so do not commit its contents.

For cross-device synchronization, rclone must be configured first. The one-time configuration entry for a new machine is to fill in tokens/onboard.yaml and then run scripts/onboard.py; the README does not provide the exact execution command or YAML fields for this script, so they are not supplemented here.

3. Summarize: Generate AI Conversation Reports#

First, export unexported conversation dates from each device, then synchronize and merge them day by day:

python -m summarize daily export
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Once sufficient daily reports are available, you can generate and publish reports for a specified week or month:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

You can also run the complete workflow provided in the README to sequentially complete export, merge, weekly report, monthly report, and publishing:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

When using multiple devices, conversation logs can be synchronized via cloud drives or manually copied and aggregated. For specific data formats and step-by-step configuration, refer to TUTORIAL.md and tools/summarize/tutorial.md pointed out in the README.

4. Research: Retrieve Papers and Analyze Researchers#

Run the complete project report workflow, which includes retrieval, three-stage evaluation, and report generation:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

Ask questions in natural language to let the tool select retrieval sources:

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

Generate researcher profiles or analyze citation relationships by arXiv ID/DOI:

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Publish reports to Hugo:

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

This tool also supports capabilities such as deep full-text paper analysis and OpenReview comment analysis; the README only mentions --insight without providing complete example commands. For project settings and detailed operations of these functions, refer to TUTORIAL.md and tools/research/TUTORIAL.md.

5. Benchmark: Test CPU/GPU Performance#

First enter tools/benchmark/; the README explicitly requires the following commands to be executed in this directory:

cd tools/benchmark

Select one running method as needed:

python -m benchmark.cli
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --report
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

They represent respectively: run all tests, test CPU only, test GPU only, test and generate HTML report, and test, generate report, and publish to Hugo via /benchmark/. Results are written to CSV in an append mode. Actual GPU testing supports CUDA, Apple MPS, and Intel XPU; OpenCL may only appear in detection information.

6. Website: Preview, Build, and Publish Blog#

The blog is based on Hugo. The README provides the local preview command; run from the repository root:

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

-D will include drafts in the development server. The publishing script incrementally compresses images and videos that have changed since the last build, then translates, builds, and pushes the site. Select the corresponding command from the README based on your operating system:

macOS/Linux

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

Windows PowerShell

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

The publishing script will automatically handle the separate tools/website/public/ deployment repository; you should not commit directly to it. Generated content carries the gadget_generated tag; handwritten files without this tag will not be overwritten.

7. Translator: Open Document Translation Page#

After installing the translator dependencies, start from the repository root:

python -m translator

It will open a Gradio page. Inputs listed in the README include text, .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, and images; Markdown snippets such as code blocks, URLs, and Hugo shortcodes will be protected during translation. When the source language is set to auto and the target language is set to auto, it will switch between Chinese and English. Models are loaded on demand and may be downloaded upon first use.

8. Common Maintenance Commands and Output Locations#

The entry point for data synchronization scripts, and the cross-device push/pull forms provided in the README:

python scripts/sync.py
python scripts/sync.py push/pull

The second line is the README’s combined representation of the two operations; in actual use, choose one from push and pull. Synchronization requires pre-configuring rclone, with settings located in the sync section of config.json.

Perform cross-tool smoke tests without calling LLMs, accessing the network, or writing files:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

View the environment settings output from the local Ollama service script:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Generated artifacts are concentrated in outputs/: logs/ for intermediate logs, reports/ for final reports, cache/ for cache, data/ for structured data, images/ for charts and images, and backups/ for backups of overwrite operations. This directory is Git-ignored. For finer configuration values, data formats, and troubleshooting, the README explicitly points to the repository’s TUTORIAL.md and each tool’s own documentation; this tutorial does not fabricate those unshown steps.

I. Project Summary#

1. What is Gadget#

Gadget is a set of practical tools accumulated from daily development, primarily covering five types of tasks:

  • Generation of daily, weekly, and monthly reports for AI conversation logs
  • Academic paper discovery, deep paper analysis, and researcher profiling
  • CPU/GPU floating-point performance testing
  • Hugo blog building, translation, media compression, and automatic publishing
  • Local document translation

The five tools under tools/ are independent of each other and can be used separately. They collectively depend on the common/ package in the repository root. common/ provides general capabilities such as LLM invocation, JSON repair, disk caching, atomic writes, local translation, and Hugo deployment.

The project’s development workflow and Claude Code skills are not in this repository, but in an adjacent independent repository ../ai-companion/, integrated into Gadget via hooks under .claude/ and .codex/.

The project uses the GPL-3 license.

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报、周报、月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客构建和发布
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 所有工具共享的基础设施
├── scripts/            # 同步、初始化、维护脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划、审计和历史文档
├── outputs/            # 自动生成的输出，已被 gitignore
├── AGENTS.md           # AI agent 工作协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 包及 extras 配置

When modifying different types of functions, the corresponding locations are as follows:

Target Location
Modify a specific tool tools/<tool>/
Modify common capabilities like LLM, cache, translation, Hugo deployment, etc. common/
Modify data synchronization scripts/sync.py
One-time configuration for a new machine scripts/onboard.py
Modify development workflow or skill ../ai-companion/
View design and execution plans docs/、docs/ecl/

3. What Each Tool Does#

Summarize#

Reads AI conversation logs from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, or general JSON formats to generate structured daily, weekly, and monthly reports.

It employs a multi-device, two-stage process:

  1. Export conversation logs on each device.
  2. Aggregate them via cloud drive synchronization or manual copying, then generate reports on a daily basis.

Once daily reports accumulate to a certain amount, weekly and monthly trend summaries can be further generated.

It uses the source-specific commands of ccusage 20.x to statistics token usage and costs for different agent CLIs, such as ccusage claude, ccusage codex, and ccusage gemini.

It supports four LLM backends:

  • ollama: Default, runs locally, no API key required
  • claude_cli: Reuses Claude Code CLI login status, no API key required
  • anthropic
  • openai

Research#

A unified academic research tool, entry point:

tools/research/research_scout.py

It has four main capabilities:

  • Paper Discovery: Searches for papers from arXiv, bioRxiv, and PubMed; generates research weekly reports through a three-stage LLM process (“Quick Screening → Deep Evaluation → Citation Impact”) and can publish them to Hugo.
  • Deep Paper Insights: Downloads full paper texts, analyzes writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable knowledge; matches OpenReview comments to analyze reviewer consensus and controversies; finally synthesizes cross-paper writing guides.
  • Researcher Profiling: Retrieves paper and citation data from ArXiv and Semantic Scholar to generate research trajectory analysis and stratified scoring, and infers mentor-student relationships through personal homepages and co-authorship patterns.
  • Citation Mapping: Utilizes the Semantic Scholar API to analyze forward citations and backward references, then uses an LLM to interpret the paper’s impact.

It also supports four LLM backends: ollama, claude_cli, anthropic and openai.

Benchmark#

A cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS floating-point performance testing tool, supporting:

  • NVIDIA CUDA
  • Apple Silicon MPS
  • Intel XPU

OpenCL may appear in --info detection results, but the README does not state that it can perform actual GPU tests.

Supported precisions include:

  • FP64
  • FP32
  • FP16
  • BF16
  • FP8, experimental support

The testing process includes warmup, formal measurement, median statistics, IQR outlier removal, and explicit GPU synchronization.

Results are written to a CSV in an append mode and will not overwrite existing results, allowing for the accumulation of data from multiple hardware units to form leaderboards. The tool can also use Plotly to generate interactive HTML reports and publish them to the Hugo website or submit them to public leaderboards.

Website#

A Hugo static blog named “TzJ’s Net”, using the PaperMod theme, with the target site being https://tzj2006.github.io/.

Main capabilities include:

  • Only compressing media files that have changed after .last_build
  • Compressing images using pngquant
  • Compressing videos using HandBrakeCLI
  • Generating bilingual content using local models
  • Automatically building the Hugo website
  • Automatically committing and pushing the GitHub Pages deployment repository

Daily, weekly, and monthly reports, research reports, benchmark pages, and images are written directly by the deployment process:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

Automatically generated files carry the gadget_generated tag. Hand-written files without this tag will not be overwritten.

tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository corresponding to tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io; files should not be manually committed to it.

Translator#

A Gradio-based local document translation web application with an interface similar to Google Translate.

Supports translating:

  • Plain text
  • .md
  • .txt
  • .pdf
  • .docx
  • Images

It attempts to preserve Markdown formatting and protects snippets like code blocks, URLs, and Hugo shortcodes.

Translation is performed entirely via local inference without using cloud LLM APIs. It automatically selects the backend via common.engine.create_engine():

  • Prioritizes Ollama if the corresponding model has been pulled
  • Falls back to transformers on Windows
  • Prioritizes vLLM on Linux
  • Uses llama.cpp/GGUF for low VRAM scenarios

The default model is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

The GGUF version is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF

Models are automatically downloaded upon first use. Once loaded, models remain in memory, with lazy loading applied when switching models as needed.

When the source language is set to auto, it automatically detects based on the proportion of CJK characters in the text; when the target language is set to auto, it automatically switches between Chinese-to-English and English-to-Chinese.

4. Common Modules and Operations Scripts#

common/#

A common Python package providing:

  • A unified two-layer LLM API
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • SHA-256 disk caching with namespaces and TTL
  • Atomic writes and content hashing
  • Local translation engine
  • Bilingual content generation
  • Cross-platform Hugo deployment

scripts/#

Main scripts include:- sync.py：Syncs summarize, website, research, benchmark, and backups data via rclone, and also supports generating and deploying DAG sites.

  • onboard.py：One-time initialization for new machines, responsible for SSH, Claude/Codex CLI, authentication, Python extras, AI Companion, tool configuration, and rclone bootstrap.
  • smoke.sh：Read-only smoke test, checks help, hardware info, and imports without calling LLMs, network, or performing writes.
  • serve_local_llm.sh：Creates Ollama model variants suitable for summarize and outputs environment variables.
  • language.py：Hugo bilingual content audit and summarize report renaming.
  • profile_translation.py：Translation engine GPU profiler.

AI Companion#

../ai-companion/ is a standalone Node.js/TypeScript repository providing:

  • Function-level code change logs
  • Test and HTML report generation
  • /idea → /ccplan → /ccedit planning and execution workflow
  • Claude Code and Codex integration
  • Skills such as optimization, debugging, auditing, cleaning, paper writing, etc.

Node.js 18+ is only required when using this standalone repository.

tokens/onboard.yaml

README note: After filling in tokens/onboard.yaml and running scripts/onboard.py, the repository-level one-time machine configuration will be completed, including:

  • SSH configuration
  • Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication
  • Python extras installation
  • AI Companion installation
  • Configuration for each tool
  • rclone bootstrap

The README does not provide a full invocation example for onboard.py in the command block, so its parameters are not expanded here.

4. Summarize Usage Tutorial#

Summarize recommends using a unified entry point:

python -m summarize

Step 1: Export conversation records on the current device#

python -m summarize daily export

This command executes the first stage of the multi-device workflow, exporting all dates that have not yet been exported.

This stage should be executed on every device containing AI conversation records.

Step 2: Sync and merge by day#

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

This command syncs data for all dates and merges them day by day to generate daily reports.

Generate a weekly report for a specific week#

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

Where:

  • 2026-W12 represents Week 12 of 2026.
  • --deploy means generate and then deploy.

Generate a monthly report for a specific month#

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

Where:

  • 2026-02 represents February 2026.
  • --deploy means generate and then deploy.

Run the full workflow with one click#

python -m summarize auto --deploy

It will sequentially complete:

export → merge → weekly → monthly → deploy

Old Entry Point#

The following old scripts are still compatible:

python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ...
python tools/summarize/weekly_summary.py ...
python tools/summarize/monthly_summary.py ...

But the README recommends using:

python -m summarize

The README does not list specific parameters for the old entry point, so one should not assume the new entry point parameters are identical to the old ones.

5. Research Usage Tutorial#

The unified entry point for Research is:

python tools/research/research_scout.py

Full Paper Search and Report Workflow#

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

This command executes:

搜索 → 三阶段评估 → 生成报告

my-project is the project name used in the README example.

Search for papers using natural language#

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

The tool will automatically select search sources based on the question.

Generate researcher profiles#

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

Researcher profiles may include:

  • Paper data from ArXiv and Semantic Scholar
  • Citation data
  • Research trajectory analysis
  • tier score
  • Advisor-student relationship discovery
  • Name disambiguation
  • Reverse lookup

Specific output fields are not detailed in the README.

Analyze paper citation graphs#

Using arXiv ID:

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

The README indicates that this position also supports DOI, but does not provide a DOI example format, so no extra examples are fabricated here.

Analysis content includes:

  • Forward citations
  • Backward references
  • LLM-driven impact interpretation

Deploy reports to Hugo#

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

Deep Paper Insights#

The README states that Research supports --insight, which can:

  • Download full paper text
  • Analyze writing structure
  • Analyze publication strategies
  • Extract reusable core knowledge
  • Match OpenReview
  • Analyze review consensus and controversies
  • Synthesize research writing guides

However, the README does not provide the complete --insight command combination, so it should not be guessed which subcommand it follows. Refer to tools/research/TUTORIAL.md when using it.

6. Benchmark Usage Tutorial#

All Benchmark commands must first enter their respective directories:

cd tools/benchmark

Execute all benchmarks#

python -m benchmark.cli

Results will be appended to the CSV and will not overwrite existing results.

Test CPU only#

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Test GPU only#

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

The tool will automatically detect:

  • CUDA
  • Apple MPS
  • Intel XPU

Execute tests and generate HTML report#

python -m benchmark.cli --report

Reports use Plotly to generate interactive charts.

Execute tests, generate reports, and deploy#

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

Reports will be published to the Hugo website at:

/benchmark/

Testing employs warmup, formal measurement, median statistics, IQR outlier removal, and GPU synchronization. Since the CSV uses append mode, it can be run repeatedly on different hardware to accumulate leaderboard data.

7. Website Usage Tutorial#

Install website dependencies#

Run in the repository root:

pip install -e ".[website]"

macOS/Linux: Build and Publish#

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

This workflow will execute:

  • Incremental compression of modified images and videos
  • Local model bilingual translation
  • Hugo build
  • Commit and push to the GitHub Pages deployment repository

Windows: Build and Publish#

Run in the repository root:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

The Windows script will automatically switch to its own directory, so there is no need to execute cd tools/website beforehand.

Local Preview#

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

-D will allow the local development server to include draft content.

Website File Notes#

Automatically generated content is written directly to:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

Files marked with gadget_generated may be automatically updated; handwritten files without this mark will not be overwritten.Do not manually submit or directly modify deployment repositories:

tools/website/public/

They are automatically committed and pushed by build scripts.

8. Translator Tutorial#

Install Dependencies#

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Start Translation Interface#

python -m translator

After starting, a Gradio GUI will open in your browser.

In the interface, you can:

  • Input text for translation
  • Upload .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx or images
  • Select source and target languages
  • Manage or switch translation models

On the first run, the default model will be downloaded automatically.

When the source language is set to auto, the tool detects the language via CJK character ratio; when the target language is set to auto, it will automatically perform reverse translation between Chinese and English.

9. Data Synchronization#

Synchronization is driven by rclone, with configuration located in the sync section of the root directory config.json.

To view the synchronization tool entry:

python scripts/sync.py

Cross-device pushing and pulling are used via:

python scripts/sync.py push

python scripts/sync.py pull

The README also specifies that sync.py supports:

status
bootstrap
config

as well as summarize, website, research, benchmark, backups, and special dag categories, but does not provide the full command combinations for these operations, so parameters are not expanded here.

10. Local Summarize Ollama Environment#

The startup and environment variable loading command provided in the README is:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

This script creates an Ollama variant suitable for Summarize and outputs the environment settings.

Long-term configuration items should be written to the summarize section of the root directory config.json, or you can use GADGET_CONFIG to point to other configuration files.

11. Run Read-only Smoke Test#

bash scripts/smoke.sh

This check only performs:

  • --help
  • --info
  • Python import checks

It does not call LLMs, access the network, or write files, making it suitable for basic verification after installation.

12. Where are the output files#

All reconstructible artifacts are unified in:

outputs/

The structure is as follows:

outputs/
├── logs/         # 导出日志、运行日志等中间产物
├── reports/      # Markdown、JSON、HTML 最终报告
├── cache/        # LLM 和搜索缓存
├── data/         # CSV、JSON profile 等结构化数据
├── images/       # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/      # 强制覆盖前的备份

Hugo content is not staged via outputs/site but is written directly to:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

13. Important Notes for Use#

  • Do not commit API keys or onboarding configurations in tokens/.
  • Do not commit auto-generated files in outputs/.
  • Do not commit build/ and gadget.egg-info/.
  • Do not commit data synchronized via rclone.
  • Do not directly commit deployment repositories or theme repositories under tools/website/.
  • config.json is a local configuration file and should be created from config.example.json.
  • Translator is not included in .[all]; you need to install .[translator] separately.
  • The website and translation functions use local inference models; downloading tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B may be required on the first run.
  • For more detailed configuration fields, data formats, troubleshooting, and incomplete usage details such as --insight, please refer to the TUTORIAL.md and tool tutorials in the repository; this README alone cannot reliably supplement them.

Project Overview#

Gadgets is a collection of daily developer tools covering five categories of tasks:

  • Generation of daily, weekly, and monthly reports for AI conversation logs
  • Academic paper retrieval, researcher profiling, and citation mapping
  • CPU/GPU performance benchmarking
  • Automated Hugo blog building, media compression, and publishing
  • Local model-driven document translation

Each directory under tools/ is an independently usable tool; the common/ in the root directory provides shared capabilities such as LLM calls, caching, JSON parsing, atomic writes, translation engines, and Hugo deployment. The development workflow and Claude Code skills are not in this repository but in the sibling independent repository ../ai-companion/.

Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/   # AI 对话日报 / 周报 / 月报
│   ├── research/    # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/   # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/     # Hugo 博客及自动发布
│   └── translator/  # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/          # 所有工具共享的基础能力
├── scripts/         # 同步、初始化、检查等运维脚本
├── docs/            # 设计文档、ECL 计划、审计与历史资料
├── outputs/         # 可重新生成的输出文件（已忽略 Git）
├── AGENTS.md        # AI Agent 工作流程协议
├── CLAUDE.md        # Claude Code 仓库说明
└── pyproject.toml   # Python 打包与依赖配置

Generated results are unified in outputs/:

outputs/
├── logs/      # 导出及运行日志
├── reports/   # Markdown、JSON、HTML 报告
├── cache/     # LLM 与搜索缓存
├── data/      # CSV、JSON 等结构化数据
├── images/    # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/   # 强制覆盖时的备份

Hugo website content is written directly to tools/website/content and tools/website/static.

Tool Purposes#

Tool Purpose
summarize Reads conversation logs from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, or general JSON to generate daily, weekly, and monthly reports, and statistics for token usage and costs of various Agent CLIs.
research Discovers papers from sources like arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, etc.; can perform deep paper insights, researcher profiling, mentor-student relationship inference, and forward/backward citation analysis.
benchmark Cross-platform testing of CPU/GPU floating-point performance, supporting CUDA, Apple MPS, Intel XPU, and generating HTML charts, leaderboards, and publishing to Hugo.
website Hugo static blog with capabilities for incremental image/video compression, automatic translation, building, and pushing to GitHub Pages.
translator Gradio-based local document translation web interface, capable of translating text, Markdown, TXT, PDF, DOCX, and images while preserving Markdown formatting as much as possible.

Tutorial#

1. Environment Preparation#

The base environment specified in the README is:

  • Python 3.10+
  • Recommended to use Conda environment AI
  • Node.js 18+: Only required if using the sibling ../ai-companion/ repository
  • Website and translation functions require a local inference engine: Ollama is preferred; Linux can use vLLM, Windows can fall back to transformers
  • Translation model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B will be downloaded automatically upon first use

If using Conda:

conda activate AI

Tool settings are located in the root directory config.json, and README instructions should be copied from config.example.json. This configuration file allows overriding paths via environment variables:

GADGET_CONFIG

Do not commit the following to Git:

  • API keys and initialization tables within tokens/
  • outputs/
  • build/
  • gadget.egg-info/
  • Deployment repositories and theme repositories under tools/website/
  • Auto-generated content and data synchronized via rclone

2. Install Dependencies#

First, install shared packages and common tool dependencies in the repository root:

pip install -e ".[all]"

Note: all does not include the translator. If the translator is needed, install it separately:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

If only using website functions:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Each tool directory also has its corresponding requirements.txt, which can be consulted when needed.

3. LLM and Translation Backend Configuration#

Supported unified LLM backends include:

  • ollama: Default, local Ollama, no API Key required
  • claude_cli: Reuses Claude Code CLI login status, no API Key required
  • anthropic
  • openai

Switching is supported via the --api parameter of each tool, or it can be set globally:

GADGET_LLM_BACKEND

Translation functions use a local inference backend, which can be selected via the following environment variables:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND

The default selection order provided in the README is:

ollama → llamacpp / vllm / transformers

The default model is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

The translation model can be replaced via the following environment variables:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL

4. Using the Conversation Summary Tool: Summarize#

This tool adopts a two-stage, multi-device workflow:

  1. Export conversation logs from each device.
  2. Aggregate data via cloud drive synchronization or manual copying, and merge by date.
  3. Generate daily reports first, then generate weekly and monthly reports.

Export all dates that have not yet been exported:

python -m summarize daily export

Sync all dates and merge them day by day:

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Generate weekly reports and deploy:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

Generate monthly reports and deploy:

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

Execute the complete one-click workflow from export and merge to weekly/monthly reports and deployment:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

The old entry point remains compatible, but the modular form above is recommended:

python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py
python tools/summarize/weekly_summary.py
python tools/summarize/monthly_summary.py

This tool automatically discovers and summarizes token usage and costs for various Agent CLIs through the source-specific commands of ccusage 20.x. Optional LLM backends are ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, and openai.

5. Using the Paper Research Tool: Research#

The unified entry point is:

python tools/research/research_scout.py

Execute a complete paper discovery process for a specific project: search, three-stage evaluation, and report generation:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

Search for papers using natural language; the tool will automatically route to the appropriate data source:

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

Generate a profile for a researcher:

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

Analyze citation maps based on arXiv ID or DOI:

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Deploy research reports to Hugo:

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

The research tool includes four types of capabilities:

  • Paper Discovery: From arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, through a three-stage process of rapid screening, deep evaluation, and citation impact analysis.
  • Deep Paper Insights: Downloads full texts via --insight to analyze writing structure, publication strategy, and reusable knowledge, and also matches OpenReview peer reviews.
  • Researcher Profiling: Generates research trajectories, scores, and relationship inferences by combining papers and citation data from ArXiv and Semantic Scholar.
  • Citation Mapping: Performs forward citation and reference analysis based on the Semantic Scholar API, with impact interpreted by LLM.

Its LLM backend can also be switched via --api.

6. Using the Performance Testing Tool: Benchmark#

All commands require entering the tool directory first:

cd tools/benchmark

Run all benchmarks:

python -m benchmark.cli

Test CPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Test GPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

Run tests and generate an HTML report:```bash python -m benchmark.cli –report


Generate reports and publish to Hugo's `/benchmark/` :

```bash
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

This tool supports actual GPU testing for NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Silicon MPS, and Intel XPU; OpenCL may only appear in --info detection. Results are written to CSV in append mode and will not overwrite existing results, making it suitable for aggregating scores from multiple machines.

7. Using Website Tool: Website#

Install website-related dependencies:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Execute incremental compression, Hugo build, and Pages push on macOS or Linux:

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

Execute the corresponding script on Windows:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

Start the local Hugo preview server, including draft content:

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

The website automatically handles the following:

  • Compresses only media files that have changed since .last_build.
  • Uses pngquant for images and HandBrakeCLI for videos.
  • Automatically generated daily reports, research reports, Benchmark pages, etc., are written directly to the Hugo content root directory.
  • Generated files will carry the gadget_generated tag; handwritten files without this tag will not be overwritten.
  • The build script will automatically commit and push to the independent GitHub Pages deployment repository in tools/website/public/.

Do not commit content directly to tools/website/public/.

8. Using Document Translator: Translator#

Install the translator:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Start the Gradio GUI:

python -m translator

After starting, the local translation page will open in your browser.

Supported translations:

  • Plain text
  • .md
  • .txt
  • .pdf
  • .docx
  • Images

The translator will protect code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc., in Markdown to preserve the original format as much as possible. The source language can be set to auto, which identifies based on the proportion of CJK characters in the text; when the target language is set to auto, it will automatically switch between Chinese and English.

9. Operations and Sync Scripts#

View or execute centralized rclone data synchronization:

python scripts/sync.py

The README explicitly lists the push and pull forms for cross-device synchronization:

python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

The sync configuration is located in the config.json section of the root directory sync, and other configuration files can also be specified via GADGET_CONFIG.

One-time initialization process for new machines:

  1. Fill out tokens/onboard.yaml.
  2. Execute:
python scripts/onboard.py

It will complete SSH, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras, ai-companion, configuration for various tools, and rclone initialization.

Execute a read-only smoke test that produces no network, LLM calls, or writes:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

Create an Ollama variant optimized for summarize and output environment configurations:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

For system-level installation of SSH public keys, Claude Code, Codex, Superpowers, Ponytail, and AI Companion on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 servers, refer to the scripts in the sibling repository for help:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

I. Project Summary#

1. What is Gadget#

Gadget is a collection of practical development tools composed of multiple independent tools, covering:

  • AI conversation daily, weekly, and monthly report generation
  • Academic paper discovery and researcher analysis
  • CPU/GPU performance benchmarking
  • Hugo blog automatic building and publishing
  • Local model-driven document translation

Each tools/ subdirectory is a tool that can be used independently. The common/ in the repository root provides shared capabilities, including:

  • LLM calls
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • Disk caching
  • Atomic writes
  • Local model translation
  • Hugo deployment

Development workflows, code change tracking, and Claude Code skills are provided by ../ai-companion/ outside the repository.

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报、周报、月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施
├── scripts/            # 同步、初始化、维护脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、计划和历史资料
├── outputs/            # 生成的报告、缓存、数据和图片
├── AGENTS.md           # AI Agent 工作流协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 使用说明
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 打包配置

When modifications are needed:

Target Directory
Modify a specific tool tools/<tool>/
Modify shared capabilities common/
Modify data synchronization scripts/sync.py
Initialize a new machine scripts/onboard.py
Modify development workflow or skills ../ai-companion/

3. Functions of Each Tool#

summarize#

Reads AI conversation logs from sources such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, etc., and calls LLMs to generate:

  • Daily reports
  • Weekly reports
  • Monthly reports and trend summaries

It uses a multi-device two-stage process:

  1. Each device exports conversation logs
  2. Aggregates data and generates reports by day

It also uses ccusage to statistics token usage and costs for different Agent CLIs.

Supports four LLM backends:

  • ollama: Default, local Ollama, no API Key required
  • claude_cli: Reuses Claude Code login status
  • anthropic
  • openai

research#

An academic research tool containing four types of capabilities:

  • Paper Discovery: Searches arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, and performs a three-stage LLM evaluation
  • Deep Paper Insights: Analyzes paper writing structure, publication strategies, core knowledge, and OpenReview reviews
  • Researcher Profiling: Combines ArXiv and Semantic Scholar data to analyze research trajectories, citations, and advisor-student relationships
  • Citation Mapping: Analyzes forward citations and backward references of papers

benchmark#

A cross-platform CPU/GPU floating-point performance testing tool.

Supports:

  • NVIDIA CUDA
  • Apple Silicon MPS
  • Intel XPU

Supports multiple precisions, including FP64, FP32, FP16, BF16, and experimental FP8.

Results are appended to CSV and will not overwrite historical data; it can also generate Plotly interactive HTML reports and leaderboards.

website#

A Hugo-based blog site using the PaperMod theme, published to GitHub Pages.

Main features:

  • Incremental compression of images and videos
  • Automatic translation of bilingual content
  • Automatic building of the Hugo website
  • Automatic commit and push of the deployment repository
  • Receives automatically generated content such as daily reports, weekly reports, research reports, and benchmark pages

Website content writing:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository and should not be committed directly to the current project.

translator#

A Gradio-based local document translator, supporting:

  • Text
  • Markdown
  • TXT
  • PDF
  • DOCX
  • Images

It protects Markdown code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, and other content. It uses the local model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B by default, and also supports GGUF versions.

The translation backend is automatically selected by the shared translation engine:

  • Ollama
  • vLLM
  • transformers
  • llama.cpp/GGUF

4. common/, scripts/ and outputs/#

common/#

A shared Python package used by various tools after installation, containing LLM, cache, IO, translation, and Hugo deployment functionalities.

scripts/#

Main scripts include:

  • sync.py: Uses rclone to synchronize data
  • onboard.py: New machine initialization
  • smoke.sh: Performs read-only smoke tests on all tools
  • serve_local_llm.sh: Creates Ollama model variants suitable for summarize
  • language.py: Checks Hugo bilingual content
  • profile_translation.py : Analyzes translation engine GPU performance

outputs/#

All generated artifacts are concentrated here:

outputs/
├── logs/
├── reports/
├── cache/
├── data/
├── images/
└── backups/

This directory is ignored by Git and can be automatically regenerated.

openai

The specific backend is switched via the --api parameter.

2. Research: Paper Search and Researcher Analysis#

Generate Research Project Report#

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

This workflow performs paper searching, three-stage evaluation, and report generation.

Search for Papers Using Natural Language#

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

The tool automatically selects data sources based on the question.

Generate Researcher Profiles#

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

It retrieves paper and citation data and generates research trajectory analysis.

Analyze Paper Citation Networks#

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Parameters can be an arXiv ID or a DOI.

Deploy Research Reports#

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

The LLM backend for Research also supports:

ollama
claude_cli
anthropic
openai

Switched uniformly via --api.

3. Benchmark: Run CPU/GPU Performance Tests#

README special note: All Benchmark commands require entering the directory first:

cd tools/benchmark

Run all benchmarks:

python -m benchmark.cli

Results will be appended to the CSV.

Run only CPU tests:

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Run only GPU tests:

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

Run tests and generate an HTML report:

python -m benchmark.cli --report

Run tests, generate reports, and deploy to Hugo:

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

The tool automatically detects CUDA, Apple MPS, and Intel XPU. OpenCL may only appear in the --info detection results and does not mean an OpenCL benchmark will be executed.

4. Website: Build and Preview Hugo Website#

Install website dependencies:

pip install -e ".[website]"

macOS/Linux: Build and Publish#

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

This workflow includes:

  1. Incremental compression of media files
  2. Executing Hugo build
  3. Pushing to GitHub Pages

Images are compressed using pngquant, and videos are processed using HandBrakeCLI.

Windows: Build and Publish#

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

This script will automatically switch to its own directory.

Local Preview#

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

-D indicates including drafts during preview.

Automatically generated content in the website is written directly to:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

Automatically generated files with the gadget_generated tag can be updated by the deployment process; handwritten files without this tag will not be overwritten.

5. Translator: Start Local Document Translator#

Install translator dependencies:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Start the Gradio GUI:

python -m translator

A browser will open after starting.

The translator supports text and the following file types:

.md
.txt
.pdf
.docx
图片

The default model is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

The GGUF version is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF

The model will be downloaded automatically upon first use. The translator prioritizes local Ollama by default; on Linux, vLLM can be used; on Windows, it can fall back to transformers, and it also supports the low-VRAM GGUF/llama.cpp path.

When the source language is set to auto and the target language is set to auto, it will automatically switch between Chinese and English.

IV. Common Notes#

  • Files in outputs/ are automatically generated and should not be committed.
  • tokens/ contains keys and initialization information and cannot be committed.
  • build/ and gadget.egg-info/ are build files produced by installation.
  • Do not directly commit tools/website/public/ or the website theme/deployment repository.
  • Cross-device synchronization requires configuring rclone first.
  • Website and translation functions depend on local inference engines, defaulting to Ollama.
  • ../ai-companion/ is an independent repository responsible for development workflows and skills.
  • The project uses the GPL-3 license.

The following content is based solely on the README you provided; the summary and tutorial will not supplement commands or parameters not appearing in the README.

I. Project Summary

Gadget is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development, covering scenarios such as AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly report generation, paper discovery and researcher analysis, performance benchmarking, Hugo blog automation, document translation, etc.

Its core design is: each directory under tools/ is a tool that can be used independently; the common/ in the repository root is a shared infrastructure package, installed via pip install -e ., providing common capabilities like LLM calling, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writing, translation, Hugo deployment, etc., to various tools. The development workflow and Claude Code skills are not within this repository but are provided by the independent repository in the adjacent directory ../ai-companion/ and integrated via hooks.

Repository Structure

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报 / 周报 / 月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客，媒体压缩，自动构建发布
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包
├── scripts/            # 运维与维护脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划、审计报告、历史归档
├── outputs/            # 所有生成产物，gitignored，可重新生成
├── AGENTS.md           # AI agent 工作流协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # common 和各工具的 Python packaging 配置

outputs/ is used for centralized storage of generation results:

outputs/
├── logs/         # 中间日志和运行日志
├── reports/      # 最终报告，Markdown / JSON / HTML
├── cache/        # LLM 缓存、搜索缓存
├── data/         # CSV、JSON profiles 等结构化数据
├── images/       # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/      # 强制覆盖备份

Hugo website content is not written to outputs/site first, but is written directly to tools/website/content|static by the deployment process.

Roles of Each Tool

tools/summarize/：AI conversation report generation tool.
Automatically reads AI conversation records from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, general JSON, etc., and calls LLMs to generate daily, weekly, and monthly trend summaries. Supports multi-device workflows: each device exports conversation logs, aggregates them via cloud drive synchronization or manual copying, and then generates the final report. Uses ccusage 20.x to statistics token usage and costs for each agent CLI. The LLM backend can be switched uniformly via --api, including ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, and openai.

tools/research/：Academic research tool.
The unified entry point is tools/research/research_scout.py, providing four types of capabilities: paper discovery, deep paper insights, researcher profiles, and citation network analysis. Supports arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and uses LLMs to complete filtering, evaluation, impact analysis, writing structure analysis, research trajectory analysis, etc.

tools/benchmark/：CPU/GPU performance benchmarking tool.
Measures floating-point performance across different hardware and precision levels on multiple platforms, supporting actual GPU execution for NVIDIA CUDA, Apple Silicon MPS, and Intel XPU. Results are appended to a CSV, and it can generate Plotly interactive HTML reports and leaderboards, as well as support deployment to Hugo websites.

tools/website/：Hugo blog site.
This is the Hugo static blog “TzJ’s Net”, using the PaperMod theme, deployed to GitHub Pages. It features an incremental image/video compression workflow, using pngquant for images and HandBrakeCLI for videos. Automatically generated content is written to tools/website/content|static with a gadget_generated tag; handwritten files without this tag will not be overwritten. tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository and should not be committed directly.

tools/translator/：Gradio document translator.
Based on the common translation engine, it provides a local translation web page similar to Google Translate. It supports translating text and files such as .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, and images, while attempting to preserve Markdown formatting and protecting code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc. The default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, with a GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF.

common/：Shared infrastructure.
Provides capabilities such as unified LLM calling, JSON parsing and repair, SHA-256 disk caching, atomic writing, content hashing, local inference translation engine, bilingual content generation, and cross-platform Hugo deployment.

scripts/：Operations and maintenance scripts.
Includes sync.py data synchronization, onboard.py new machine initialization, smoke.sh read-only smoke checks, serve_local_llm.sh local Ollama variant configuration, language.py Hugo bilingual auditing and report renaming, profile_translation.py translation engine GPU profiling, etc.

../ai-companion/：Independent repository.
Does not belong to the gadget repository itself. It is responsible for function-level code change records, testing and HTML report generation, the /idea→/ccplan→/ccedit planning and execution workflow, and Claude Code skills.

All tools share the common/ package in the repository root, which provides capabilities such as LLM invocation, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation, and Hugo deployment, installed via pip install -e ..

The development workflow (planning, execution, change tracking) and all Claude Code skills are not in this repository; they are provided by another repository, ai-companion. It is located in the sibling directory ../ai-companion/ and connects to this repository through hooks under .claude/ and .codex/.

II. Usage Tutorial#

Note: The following commands are taken directly from the README. Where the README does not specify exact command lines, I will mark them; please refer to TUTORIAL.md or the original documentation of each tool as the standard.

Step 1: Environment Preparation#

Required Environment:

  • Python 3.10+, recommended to use the conda environment named AI
  • Node.js 18+, only required for the ../ai-companion/ repository
  • Local Inference Engine: Default is Ollama, which is used for both conversation and translation via gemma4:26b. Alternatives are vLLM on Linux and transformers on Windows, which use tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B and will be automatically downloaded upon first run
  • External Programs (installed as needed):
    • website requires Hugo, pngquant, and HandBrakeCLI
    • data synchronization requires rclone
conda activate AI

Step 2: Installation#

Execute in the repository root:

# common 包 + summarize / research / benchmark / website 的依赖
pip install -e ".[all]"

# translator 不包含在 all 里，需要单独安装
pip install -e ".[translator]"

# 只需要 website 时（包含翻译用的 torch 和 transformers）
pip install -e ".[website]"

After installation, build/ and gadget.egg-info/ will be generated in the repository root. They are already gitignored; do not commit them. For specific dependencies of each tool, see requirements.txt in their respective directories.

Optional: Install ai-companion. Only install if you need development workflows and skills.

  • Checkout git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git to the sibling directory ../ai-companion/
  • For installation methods, see ../ai-companion/scripts/install.ts

Step 3: Configuration#

1. Configuration Files

  • Manually copy config.example.json from the repository root to config.json]. This file is gitignored.
  • If you need to use other paths, specify them using the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.
  • Purpose of each section:
    • sync section: configuration for sync.py
    • summarize section: persistent parameters for local LLM

2. Keys

API keys and onboarding forms are located in the tokens/ directory. This directory is gitignored; absolutely do not commit it.

3. Selecting LLM Backend

All features involving LLM can switch backends using --api, or set globally via the environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND.

Backend Description
ollama Default. Local Ollama, no key required, uses Gemma4-26B
claude_cli Reuses the login status of Claude Code CLI, no API key required
anthropic Anthropic API
openai OpenAI API

Global setting example:

export GADGET_LLM_BACKEND=claude_cli

4. Translation-related Environment Variables

  • GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: Values can be ollama (default), llamacpp, vllm or transformers
  • GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL: Overrides the default translation model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

5. Optional: Generate Ollama variants optimized for summarize and export environment variables

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

6. One-click Configuration for New Machines

First, fill in tokens/onboard.yaml, then run scripts/onboard.py once. It will automatically complete:

  • SSH configuration
  • Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication
  • pip extras and ai-companion installation
  • Configuration for each tool
  • rclone bootstrap

The README only mentions “run the script once” without providing the full command line arguments.

If you are using an Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 server and require system-level installation, please use the scripts in the ai-companion repository; check the help first:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

7. Verifying Installation

The smoke test is read-only: it only checks if --help, --info and various modules can be imported; it does not call LLM, connect to the internet, or write files.

bash scripts/smoke.sh

Step 4: Tool Usage#

4.1 Summarize: AI Conversation Daily / Weekly / Monthly Reports#

The workflow is divided into two stages:

  1. Export conversation logs from each device
  2. Aggregate the logs to one place via cloud drive synchronization or manual copying, then merge them day by day to generate daily reports

Once enough daily reports have accumulated, you can generate weekly and monthly reports.

# 阶段 1：导出所有尚未导出的日期
python -m summarize daily export

# 阶段 2：同步所有日期并逐日合并
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

# 生成指定周的周报并部署
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

# 生成指定月的月报并部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

# 一键跑完整流程：导出 → 合并 → 周报 → 月报 + 部署
python -m summarize auto --deploy
  • Token usage and costs are automatically tracked by ccusage 20.x, which categorizes commands by source: ccusage claude, ccusage codex, ccusage gemini, etc.
  • Old entry points python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py, weekly_summary.py, monthly_summary.py are still available, but using python -m summarize is recommended.
  • For detailed instructions, see tools/summarize/tutorial.md.

4.2 Research: Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis#

# 完整流程：搜索 → 三阶段评估 → 报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

# 自然语言搜索，自动路由到合适的数据源
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

# 研究者画像
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

# 引用图谱，参数可以是 arXiv ID 或 DOI
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

# 把报告部署到 Hugo
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy
  • Deep paper insights are enabled via --insight. The README does not specify which subcommand it is attached to.
  • Both conference paper search and author search are supported, but the README does not provide specific commands.
  • Please refer to tools/research/TUTORIAL.md for the above two items.

4.3 Benchmark: Performance Benchmarking#

All commands must be executed within the tools/benchmark/ directory first:

cd tools/benchmark

# 运行全部测试，结果追加写入 CSV
python -m benchmark.cli

# 只测 CPU
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

# 只测 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

# 运行测试并生成 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report

# 生成报告并发布到 Hugo 的 /benchmark/
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy
  • GPU will be automatically detected (CUDA, MPS, or XPU).
  • OpenCL will only appear in the detection results of --info and cannot actually run tests.
  • CSV uses append mode and never overwrites, so results run on different machines will naturally accumulate into a leaderboard.

4.4 Website: Hugo Blog#

# 安装依赖
pip install -e ".[website]"

# macOS/Linux：增量压缩 + Hugo 构建 + 推送到 Pages
cd tools/website && bash update.sh

# Windows：脚本会自动 cd 到自己所在的目录
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

# 本地预览，启动开发服务器，包含草稿
cd tools/website && hugo server -D

Notes:

  • Content generated by various tools will be written directly to tools/website/content and tools/website/static and will carry the gadget_generated tag. Hand-written files without this tag will not be overwritten.
  • Compression only processes media files that have changed since .last_build.
  • tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), which is automatically committed and pushed by build scripts. Do not commit to it manually.
  • The translation model will be automatically downloaded upon the first run.

4.5 Translator: Gradio Document Translator#

# 安装 gradio 和 GGUF 翻译栈
pip install -e ".[translator]"

# 启动 GUI，会在浏览器中打开
python -m translator

Backend Selection: The translator will automatically select the inference backend.

  • If the corresponding model tag has been pulled, ollama is prioritized.
  • On Linux, vllm is prioritized.
  • On Windows, it falls back to transformers.
  • When VRAM is low, llamacpp (GGUF format) can be selected.

Models:

  • The default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, and the GGUF version is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF; it will be automatically downloaded upon first use.
  • You can switch models using GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or via model management in the GUI.
  • Models remain resident in memory after loading; they are loaded on demand when switching models.

Languages:

  • When the source language is set to auto, the language is determined by the proportion of CJK characters in the text.
  • When the target language is set to auto, it performs mutual translation between Chinese and English.

4.6 Cross-device Data Synchronization```bash#

python scripts/sync.py # 运行同步脚本 python scripts/sync.py push # 推送 python scripts/sync.py pull # 拉取


- Supported operations: push, pull, status, bootstrap, config.
- Synchronized data categories: summarize, website, research, benchmark, backups. There is also a special category `dag` used for generating and deploying DAG sites.
- Before use, rclone must be configured; synchronization settings are written in the `sync` section of `config.json`.

## Step 5: Where is the output

All artifacts are under `outputs/`. This directory is gitignored and can be deleted and rebuilt at any time.

```text
outputs/
├── logs/      # 中间产物（导出日志、运行日志）

├── images/    # 图表和生成的图片
└── backups/   # 强制覆盖前的备份

Hugo site content is an exception: it is written directly to tools/website/content and tools/website/static.

Common Notes#

  • Do NOT git add the following:
    • Automatically generated content
    • Data synchronized via rclone
    • build/ and gadget.egg-info/
    • Deployment repositories and theme repositories under tools/website/
    • The tokens/ directory
  • For step-by-step operations, data formats, and FAQ for each tool, please refer to TUTORIAL.md in the root directory. The Chinese version of the README is in docs/README.zh.md.
  • The project uses the GPL-3 license.
