Cursor#

Grok 4.7 High — 13,143 chars · 16/16 facts

This is a Chinese explanation organized solely based on the README you pasted, without adding any commands or parameters not mentioned in the README.

I. Project Summary#

Gadgets is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development, covering five areas: AI conversation daily report generation, paper discovery, performance benchmarking, blog automation, and document translation.

Each directory under tools/ is an independent tool that can be used separately. The common/ in the repository root is the shared infrastructure, installed via pip install -e ., providing LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation, and Hugo deployment. The development workflow (planning / execution / change tracking) and all Claude Code skills are not in this repository, but in the independent repository ai-companion (git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git), checked out to the sibling directory ../ai-companion/, and connected to this repository via hooks.

This README is an overview. Step-by-step operations, configurations, data formats, and FAQs for each tool are in TUTORIAL.md as well as in the source code documentation of each tool. The Chinese version of the README is at docs/README.zh.md.

Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具（改某个工具就进这里）
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日 / 周 / 月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现 + 研究者分析 + 引用图
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客（增量媒体压缩 + 自动构建发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译
├── common/             # 共享包（LLM / 缓存 / IO / 翻译 / Hugo），所有工具都依赖它
├── scripts/            # 运维与维护脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划（docs/ecl/）、审计报告、历史归档（docs/archive/）
├── outputs/            # 全部生成物（已 gitignore，可自动重建）
├── AGENTS.md           # 所有 AI agent 的工作流协议（动手前先读）
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 的仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # common/ 与各工具的打包配置（pip install -e .）

build/ and gadget.egg-info/ are generated by pip install -e ., are gitignored, and are always in the repository root. Synchronized data uses python scripts/sync.py.

What do you want to change Where to go
Logic of a specific tool tools/<tool>/
Shared capabilities (LLM / cache / translation / Hugo deployment) common/
Data synchronization scripts/sync.py
One-time configuration for a new machine scripts/onboard.py
Development workflow / skill ai-companion (sibling directory ../ai-companion/)
Plan / Design documents docs/ecl/, docs/

What Each Tool Does#

Directory Function Key Technologies
tools/summarize/ AI conversation daily / weekly / monthly summaries (multi-device two-stage architecture) Claude/OpenAI API, ccusage 20.x, matplotlib
tools/research/ Paper discovery + researcher analysis + citation graphs arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed, Semantic Scholar, LLM
tools/benchmark/ Cross-platform CPU/GPU performance benchmarks PyTorch, NumPy, Plotly
tools/website/ Hugo blog (incremental media compression + automatic build and publish) Hugo, pngquant, HandBrakeCLI
tools/translator/ Gradio document translation based on common translation engine Gradio, GGUF/transformers
common/ Shared infrastructure pip install -e .
scripts/ Operations scripts (rclone sync, machine configuration, etc.) rclone, Python
../ai-companion/ AI code change tracking + planning/execution skill pipeline + all skills Node.js, TypeScript

Summarize: Reads daily AI conversation logs (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON) and calls LLMs to generate structured daily, weekly, and monthly summaries. The multi-device process is: each device exports conversation logs, which are aggregated via cloud drive synchronization or manual copying, and then the final daily report is generated; once enough daily reports are collected, weekly and monthly trends can be generated. Through ccusage 20.x source-based commands (ccusage claude, ccusage codex, ccusage gemini…), it automatically discovers and statistics the token usage and costs of various agent CLIs. The four AI summary backends are switched uniformly via --api: ollama (default, local Ollama, no key required, Gemma4-26B), claude_cli (reuses Claude Code CLI login state, no API key required), anthropic, openai.

Research: A single entry point tools/research/research_scout.py with four capabilities:

  • Paper Discovery: Searches arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed using a three-stage LLM pipeline (fast screening → deep evaluation → citation impact), generating research weekly reports and deploying them to Hugo. Supports conference paper search and author search.
  • Deep Paper Insights (--insight): Downloads full texts, analyzes writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable core knowledge; automatically matches OpenReview to obtain reviewer comments and analyze consensus and divergence; synthesizes these into research writing guides across papers.
  • Researcher Profiling: Retrieves paper and citation data from ArXiv + Semantic Scholar to generate research trajectory analysis and calculate hierarchical scores; automatically discovers mentor–student relationships through homepage extraction + co-authorship patterns. Supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup.
  • Citation Graphs: Performs forward citation / backward reference analysis based on the Semantic Scholar API, supplemented by LLM impact interpretation.

LLMs are also switched via --api: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai.

Benchmark: Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarks, measuring floating-point performance uniformly across different hardware vendors and precision levels. Actual GPU execution supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU); OpenCL may only appear in --info detection. Precision includes FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental). The measurement process consists of warmup + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR outlier removal), and explicitly performs GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy. Results are appended to a CSV (not overwritten, allowing for natural accumulation of multi-hardware leaderboards), can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards with Plotly charts, and supports deployment to Hugo websites or submission to public leaderboards. All commands must first run cd tools/benchmark.

Website: A Hugo static blog (“TzJ’s Net”, PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages (https://tzj2006.github.io/). Built-in incremental image/video compression: only compresses media that has changed since .last_build (images via pngquant, videos via HandBrakeCLI). Bilingual translation uses local models (default Ollama; falls back to vLLM on Linux, and transformers on Windows; model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded upon first run, without using cloud LLM APIs). Automatically generated content (daily/weekly/monthly reports, research reports, benchmark pages, images) is written directly by the deployment pipeline into tools/website/content|static (the unique Hugo content root; files marked with gadget_generated will be written, while handwritten files without this mark will not be overwritten), then translated, compressed, built, and pushed. tools/website/public/ is another deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), which is automatically committed + pushed by the build script; do not commit directly to it.

Translator: A Gradio page based on the common translation engine, with a style similar to Google Translate. Translates text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images) while preserving Markdown formatting (code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc., are protected). Local inference, not a cloud API. Automatically selects the backend via common.engine.create_engine(): if the model tag is already pulled, prioritize ollama; falls back to transformers on Windows, prioritizes vllm on Linux, and offers llamacpp (GGUF) for low VRAM. Models stay in memory (warm), with lazy loading on demand when switching models. Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF), which is automatically downloaded upon first use; can be overridden by GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or the model management in the interface. Source language can be set to auto (detected by CJK ratio in text); when the target is auto, it performs bidirectional translation between Chinese and English.

common/: The shared layer that all tools depend on.

  • LLM calls (unified two-layer API, four backends: ollama default / claude_cli / anthropic / openai)
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • SHA-256 disk caching (namespace + TTL)
  • Atomic writes and content hashing
  • Local inference translation engine (Ollama / vLLM / transformers / GGUF) and bilingual content generation
  • Cross-platform Hugo deployment

scripts/:- sync.py: Centralized rclone data synchronization (push / pull / status / bootstrap / config), covering summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups; there is also a special category dag used for generating and deploying DAG sites. Configuration is in the sync section of the repository root config.json (paths can be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG).

  • onboard.py: Repository-level one-time machine onboarding. Fill out a YAML file (tokens/onboard.yaml), run the script once, and it automatically completes SSH, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras and ai-companion installation, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.
  • smoke.sh: Read-only smoke test (--help / --info / imports; does not call LLM, does not connect to the internet, does not write files).
  • serve_local_llm.sh: Creates an Ollama variant tuned for summarize and prints environment variables. Persistent switches are written in the summarize section of the repository root config.json (paths can be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG).
  • Others: language.py (Hugo bilingual audit + summarize report renaming), profile_translation.py (translation engine GPU analysis).

ai-companion: An independent Node.js repository, checked out in ../ai-companion/. It records function-level code changes, generates tests and HTML reports, provides a /idea → /ccplan → /ccedit plan–execute pipeline, and hosts all Claude Code skills. This repository integrates via hooks under .claude/ and .codex/. It serves as both a standard Claude Code plugin and an equivalent Codex integration, ready to use upon installation without building (the change tracking hook is a pre-built single-file artifact submitted with the repository). Methodology skills: ccplan planning, optimize optimization, cchypothesis debugging, repo-audit auditing, repo-tidy tidying. Domain skills: summarize code overview, slurm-gpu cluster detection, nature-benchmark / NIPS-2025-paper paper writing advisor. This repository no longer contains the skills/ directory. For installation, see ../ai-companion/scripts/install.ts.

New Server Onboarding has two complementary paths: this repository uses scripts/onboard.py; system-level one-click installation for Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 (SSH public key, Claude Code, Codex, Superpowers, Ponytail, AI Companion) has moved to ai-companion: ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh. After the repository split, --companion-repo is passed directly to the ai-companion repository (git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git), and --companion-ref is no longer required. For usage, see bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help.

Output Directory outputs/ (gitignored, can be automatically rebuilt):

outputs/
├── logs/         # 中间产物（导出日志、运行日志）
├── reports/      # 最终报告（Markdown、JSON、HTML）
├── cache/        # LLM 缓存、搜索缓存
├── data/         # 结构化数据（CSV、JSON 画像）
├── images/       # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/      # 强制覆盖备份（website-force 等）

Hugo site content is written directly to tools/website/content|static, without a separate outputs/site staging tree.

II. First-time Use Tutorial#

Detailed step-by-step operations, configurations, data formats, and FAQs can be found in TUTORIAL.md and the documentation of each tool. Below are only the steps and commands mentioned in the README.

1. Environment Preparation#

  • Python 3.10+. Recommended conda environment AI: conda activate AI
  • Node.js 18+. Only the independent repository ../ai-companion/ requires it.
  • Specific dependencies for each tool can be found in the corresponding requirements.txt within their directories.
  • Website / translation functions default to local inference: Ollama, reusing the same chat model gemma4:26b during translation; falls back to vLLM on Linux and transformers on Windows; these two paths use tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, which is automatically downloaded upon first run.

2. Installation#

Install the common package, along with extras for summarize / research / benchmark / website. all does not include the translator; the translator must be installed separately:

pip install -e ".[all]"
pip install -e ".[translator]"

If only installing the website (including torch + transformers for translation):

pip install -e ".[website]"

If only installing the translator (gradio + GGUF translation stack):

pip install -e ".[translator]"

pip install -e . will generate build/ and gadget.egg-info/ in the repository root, both of which are gitignored.

3. Configuration#

Tool settings are located in config.json at the repository root (gitignored). Copy one from the example:

# README 写的是：copy from config.example.json

That is, copy config.example.json to config.json in the repository root. Use environment variable GADGET_CONFIG to change the configuration file path.

Environment variables related to configuration (mentioned in the README):

Variable Purpose
GADGET_CONFIG Overrides the path of config.json
GADGET_LLM_BACKEND Globally switches the LLM backend
GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND Selects the translation backend
GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL Overrides the translation model

LLM backends are switched uniformly using --api: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai. You can also use GADGET_LLM_BACKEND for global settings.

The translation path is selected by GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama (default, local Ollama, reuses the existing serviced chat tag gemma4:26b) → llamacpp / vllm / transformers (in-process, model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B).

tokens/ stores API keys and access tables; it is gitignored, so do not commit its contents.

One-time machine onboarding: first fill out tokens/onboard.yaml, then run scripts/onboard.py (the README provides the script name and this workflow, but not the full command-line arguments). It will configure SSH, Claude/Codex authentication, pip extras, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.

System-level installation for Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 servers is in the sibling repository. Check the help first:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

After the repository split, --companion-repo is passed directly to git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git, and --companion-ref is no longer needed. Installation instructions for ai-companion itself are in ../ai-companion/scripts/install.ts.

Cross-device data synchronization requires a configured rclone:

python scripts/sync.py
python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

The README also lists sub-capabilities of the same script: status, bootstrap, config. Configuration is in the sync section of config.json. Overridden categories are summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups, with a special category dag (generating and deploying DAG sites).

Read-only smoke test (does not call LLM, does not connect to the internet, does not write files):

bash scripts/smoke.sh

Prepare a local Ollama variant for summarize, and eval its printed environment variables into the current shell:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Persistent switches are written in the summarize section of config.json.

4. Summarize: Daily / Weekly / Monthly Reports#

The recommended entry point is python -m summarize. Old entry points python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ..., weekly_summary.py, and monthly_summary.py are still available (backward-compatible re-exports), but the new format is recommended.

python -m summarize daily export                                   # 阶段 1：导出所有尚未导出的日期
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all                         # 阶段 2：同步所有日期并按天合并
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy       # 周报并部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy      # 月报并部署
python -m summarize auto --deploy                                  # 一键全流程：export → merge → weekly → monthly + deploy

Multi-device usage (workflow described in README): Export chat logs on each device, aggregate them using cloud drives or manual copying, and then generate the final daily report; once enough daily reports are accumulated, generate weekly and monthly trends. Token usage can be statistically analyzed via ccusage 20.x by source command, e.g., ccusage claude, ccusage codex, ccusage gemini.

Backend switching examples (the four values for --api are in the README; below, the default and the other three are appended to existing subcommands according to the documentation):

python -m summarize daily export --api ollama
python -m summarize daily export --api claude_cli
python -m summarize daily export --api anthropic
python -m summarize daily export --api openai

For step-by-step instructions, see the Summarize section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/summarize/tutorial.md.

5. Research: Papers and Researchers#

The entry point is tools/research/research_scout.py:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project        # 全流程：搜索 → 三阶段评估 → 报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"  # 自然语言搜索（自动路由来源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"             # 研究者画像
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597               # 引用图（arXiv ID 或 DOI）
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy                              # 把报告部署到 Hugo

For deep insights, use --insight (the README explains the purpose of this switch: download full text, analyze writing and publication strategies, match OpenReview, and synthesize writing guides). The LLM backend is also --api: ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, openai.

For step-by-step instructions, see the Research section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/research/TUTORIAL.md.

6. Benchmark: Performance Benchmarking#

README note: All commands below must first enter tools/benchmark/.

cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli                # 跑全部基准（结果追加到 CSV）
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only     # 只测 CPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only     # 只测 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --report       # 跑基准并生成 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy  # 生成报告并发布到 Hugo /benchmark/

GPU will automatically detect CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU. OpenCL may only appear in the --info detection output (this is mentioned in the README, but no separate --info command-line example is provided). Precision levels: FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental). Results are appended to the CSV without overwriting history.

For step-by-step instructions, see the Benchmark section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/benchmark/tutorial.md.

7. Website: Hugo Blog```bash#

pip install -e “.[website]” # 安装依赖（含翻译用的 torch + transformers） cd tools/website && bash update.sh # macOS/Linux：增量压缩 + Hugo 构建 + 推送 Pages powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1 # Windows（脚本会 cd 到自己的目录） cd tools/website && hugo server -D # 本地预览（开发服务器，包含草稿）


The site address is `https://tzj2006.github.io/`. Automatic content writing goes to `tools/website/content` and `tools/website/static`]. Files marked with `gadget_generated` are generated files; handwritten files without this mark will not be overwritten. `tools/website/public/` is the independently deployed repository `tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io`}, which is committed and pushed by build scripts; do not `git commit` directly inside it.

For step-by-step instructions, see the Website section in `TUTORIAL.md`}, as well as `tools/website/CLAUDE.md`}.

### 8. Translator: Document Translation Webpage

```bash
pip install -e ".[translator]"   # 安装依赖（gradio + GGUF 翻译栈）
python -m translator             # 启动 Gradio 界面（在浏览器中打开）

Translatable text and files: .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, and images. When the source language is set to auto}, it detects based on CJK ratio; when the target is set to auto}, it performs bidirectional translation between Chinese and English. Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B}, GGUF variant is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF}, which is automatically downloaded upon first use. To change models, use the environment variable GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or perform model management within the interface.

The backend is automatically selected by common.engine.create_engine(): if the model tag has been pulled, ollama is prioritized; Windows falls back to transformers; Linux prioritizes vllm; low VRAM uses llamacpp. You can also specify using GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama, llamacpp, vllm, or transformers.

Interface wiring is in tools/translator/app.py}, translation and file logic are in tools/translator/core.py}, and the shared engine is in common/engine.py and common/translation.py}. For step-by-step instructions, see the Translator section in TUTORIAL.md}.

9. Where outputs are located and what NOT to commit#

All generated items are in outputs/: logs/, reports/, cache/, data/, images/, and backups/}. This directory is already gitignored.

Do NOT git add these things:

  • Automatically generated content
  • Data synced via rclone
  • Build artifacts build/, gadget.egg-info/
  • Deployment repositories and theme repositories under tools/website/
  • Keys and access tables in tokens/

The license is GPL-3, see LICENSE}.

1. Project Summary#

What it is#

Gadgets is a collection of useful tools accumulated during daily development, covering five categories of capabilities:

  • AI conversation daily / weekly / monthly report generation
  • Paper discovery and researcher analysis
  • Performance benchmarking
  • Blog automation
  • Document translation

Every directory under tools/ is an independently usable tool. Common capabilities are concentrated in the common/ package in the repository root (installed via pip install -e .), including LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writing, translation, and Hugo deployment.

The development workflow (planning / execution / change tracking) and all Claude Code skills are not in this repository, but in the independent repository ai-companion (git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git), which should be placed in the sibling directory ../ai-companion/ and accessed via the hooks of this repository.

This README is an overview; step-by-step operations, configuration, data formats, and FAQ can be found in TUTORIAL.md and the source documentation of each tool. The Chinese version of the README is at docs/README.zh.md.

Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具（改某个工具就进这里）
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日/周/月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现 + 研究者分析 + 引用图
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客（增量媒体压缩 + 自动构建发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施（LLM / cache / IO / translation / Hugo）
├── scripts/            # 运维脚本（sync.py、onboard.py、language.py、profile_translation.py …）
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划（docs/ecl/）、审计报告、历史归档（docs/archive/）

├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # common/ + 各工具的打包配置（pip install -e .）

Supplementary notes (original README):

  • Workflow engine and skills are in ../ai-companion/}, accessed via hooks under .claude/ and .codex/}.
  • build/ and gadget.egg-info/ are generated by pip install -e .}, are gitignored, and always reside in the repository root.
  • Synced data: python scripts/sync.py}.
What do you want to change Where to go

What each tool does#

tools/summarize/
Automatically reads daily AI conversation logs (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON) and calls an LLM to generate structured daily/weekly/monthly reports. Multi-device two-stage process: each device first exports, then aggregates via cloud drive sync or manual copy to produce daily reports; once enough daily reports are accumulated, weekly and monthly trends are produced. Automatically discovers and statistics token usage and costs for various agent CLIs via ccusage 20.x source commands (ccusage claude, ccusage codex, ccusage gemini…). Four summary backends can be switched uniformly using --api: ollama (default, local, keyless, Qwen3.8-27B), claude_cli (reuses Claude Code CLI login state, no API key required), anthropic, and openai.

tools/research/
A unified academic research toolbox with a single entry point tools/research/research_scout.py}, offering four capabilities:

  1. Paper Discovery: Retrieves from arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed using a three-stage LLM pipeline (fast screening → deep evaluation → citation impact analysis), generates research weekly reports, and deploys them to Hugo; supports conference paper and author searches.
  2. Deep Paper Insights (--insight): Downloads full texts, analyzes writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable core knowledge; automatically matches OpenReview peer review comments; synthesizes research writing guides across papers.
  3. Researcher Profiling: Pulls papers and citations from ArXiv + Semantic Scholar; LLM generates research trajectory analysis and calculates graded scores; automatically discovers mentor-student relationships via homepage extraction + co-authorship patterns; supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup.
  4. Citation Graph Analysis: Performs forward citation / backward reference analysis based on the Semantic Scholar API, combined with LLM for impact interpretation.

LLM switching also uses --api}, with the same four backends as summarize.

tools/benchmark/
Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmark, unifying floating-point performance measurements across different hardware vendors and precision levels. Actual GPU execution supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU) (OpenCL may only appear in --info detection). Precision coverage includes FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental). Measurement process: warm-up + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR for outlier removal), with explicit GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy. Results are written to CSV in append mode (does not overwrite, naturally supporting multi-hardware cumulative leaderboards); can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards with Plotly charts, and can be deployed to Hugo or submitted to public leaderboards.

tools/website/
Hugo static blog site (“TzJ’s Net”, PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages (https://tzj2006.github.io/). Includes built-in incremental image/video compression (only compresses media changed since .last_build: images via pngquant, videos via HandBrakeCLI), as well as local model bilingual translation (default Ollama; falls back to vLLM on Linux, transformers on Windows; model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded upon first run, without using cloud LLM APIs). Each tool’s deploy pipeline writes automatically generated content directly to tools/website/content|static (the unique Hugo content root; marked with gadget_generated]; handwritten files without this mark are never overwritten), then translates, compresses, builds, and pushes. tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), which is automatically committed and pushed by build scripts—do not commit directly to it.

tools/translator/
A Gradio-based document translator using the common translation engine: a Google Translate-like local webpage that translates text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images) while preserving Markdown formatting (code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc., are protected). Local inference, no cloud APIs used. Automatically selects the backend via common.engine.create_engine() (prioritizes ollama if the model tag is pulled; falls back to transformers on Windows; prioritizes vllm on Linux; uses GGUF via llamacpp for low VRAM), with models kept in memory (warm) and lazy-loaded on demand when switching. Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF); automatically downloaded upon first use; can be overridden via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or in-GUI model management. Source language can be set to auto (detects based on text CJK ratio); when the target is auto}, it flips between zh↔en.

common/
The shared layer relied upon by all tools: unified two-layer LLM API (four backends), JSON parsing and repair, SHA-256 disk caching (namespace + TTL), atomic writing and content hashing, local inference translation engine and bilingual content generation, and cross-platform Hugo deployment.scripts/
Ops scripts: rclone data synchronization, new machine onboarding, read-only smoke tests, local LLM environment, Hugo bilingual audit, translation engine GPU profiler, etc.

../ai-companion/ (standalone repository)
Records function-level code changes, generates tests and HTML reports, provides the /idea→/ccplan→/ccedit planning-execution pipeline, and hosts all Claude Code skills. It is also packaged as a standard Claude Code plugin and an equivalent Codex integration, ready to use upon installation. This repository no longer contains the skills/ directory.

outputs/
All artifacts are centralized here (gitignored, can be automatically rebuilt): logs/, reports/, cache/, data/, images/, backups/. Hugo site content is written directly to tools/website/content|static, with no separate outputs/site staging tree.

2. Usage Tutorial for First-Timers#

2.1 Environment Preparation#

Requirements provided in README:

  • Python 3.10+ (recommended conda environment AI)
  • Node.js 18+ (only required by the standalone repository ../ai-companion/)
  • Specific dependencies for each tool can be found in the corresponding directory’s requirements.txt
  • Website/translation functions use a local inference engine (default Ollama; fallback to vLLM on Linux, fallback to transformers on Windows); model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded upon first run.

Activate the recommended environment:

conda activate AI

Additionally, please read AGENTS.md (workflow protocols for all AI agents before they take action) and CLAUDE.md (Claude Code repository guide) in the repository root. For more detailed step-by-step instructions, see TUTORIAL.md.

2.2 Installation#

Install the shared package common/ and tool extras in the repository root.

Install common + summarize / research / benchmark / website extras (excluding translator):

pip install -e ".[all]"

Install translator separately (all does not include translator):

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Install only website-related dependencies (includes torch + transformers for translation):

pip install -e ".[website]"

pip install -e . will generate build/ and gadget.egg-info/ in the repository root (already gitignored).

For ai-companion installation, see ../ai-companion/scripts/install.ts. It serves as both a Claude Code plugin and a Codex integration; it is ready to use upon installation without needing to build.

2.3 Configuration#

Repository-level Configuration

  • Tool settings are located in config.json at the repository root (already gitignored).
  • Copy from config.example.json before making changes.
  • Paths can be overridden using the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.

Keys and Onboarding Tables

  • tokens/ stores API keys and onboarding tables and is gitignored—never commit its contents.

One-time Configuration for New Machines (this repository)

  1. Fill out a YAML file: tokens/onboard.yaml
  2. Run scripts/onboard.py once.

It will automatically complete: SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras and ai-companion installation, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.

System-level Installation for New Servers (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04)

Scripts have been migrated to ai-companion: ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh. After the repository split, --companion-repo is passed directly to the ai-companion repository (git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git), and --companion-ref is no longer required. Usage:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

LLM Backend (Global)

Use --api to switch uniformly: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai. You can also specify it globally via the environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND.

Translation Backend / Models

  • The backend is selected by GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama (default if the model has been pulled, using local Ollama service) → llamacpp / vllm / transformers (in-process).
  • Models: tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B; the translator can also be overridden by GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or model management within the GUI.

Cross-device Data Synchronization

rclone must be configured first. Configuration is in the sync section of the repository root’s config.json (paths can also be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG).

python scripts/sync.py
python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

The README specifies that sync.py overrides categories such as summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups, as well as a special dag category (for generating and deploying DAG sites); subcommands also include status / bootstrap / config.

What Not to Commit

Do not git add: auto-generated content, rclone sync data, build artifacts (build/, gadget.egg-info/), or deployment/theme repositories under tools/website/. All generated files are in outputs/ (already gitignored). Licensed under GPL-3 (see LICENSE).

Post-installation Read-only Smoke Check (does not call LLM, does not connect to the internet, does not write files):

bash scripts/smoke.sh

Local Ollama variant for summarize (prints environment variables for eval):

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Persistence knobs are written in the summarize section of the repository root’s config.json (paths can be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG).

Other ops scripts: language.py (Hugo bilingual audit + summarize report renaming), profile_translation.py (translation engine GPU profiler).

2.4 Typical Usage for Each Tool#

Summarize: AI Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

Multi-device workflow: each device first exports unexported dates → sync and merge by day → generate weekly/monthly reports once enough daily reports are accumulated. The recommended new entry point is python -m summarize (old entry points python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ... / weekly_summary.py / monthly_summary.py are still available but act as compatibility shims for re-exporting).

python -m summarize daily export                                   # 阶段 1：导出所有未导出日期
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all                         # 阶段 2：同步全部日期并按天合并
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy       # 周报 + 部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy      # 月报 + 部署
python -m summarize auto --deploy                                  # 一键全流水线：export → merge → weekly → monthly + deploy

Switch the LLM backend using --api (ollama / claude_cli / anthropic / openai). For more detailed steps, see the Summarize section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/summarize/tutorial.md.

Research: Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis#

The unified entry point is tools/research/research_scout.py.

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project        # 全流水线：检索 → 三阶段评估 → 报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"  # 自然语言搜索（自动路由数据源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"             # 研究者画像
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597               # 引用图（按 arXiv ID / DOI）
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy                              # 把报告部署到 Hugo

Deep paper insight capabilities are marked in the README as --insight, but no full copy-pasteable command line is provided. The LLM also uses --api to switch between four backends. For more detailed steps, see the Research section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/research/TUTORIAL.md.

Benchmark: Performance Benchmark Suite#

Note: All commands must first cd into tools/benchmark/. GPU will automatically detect CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU. Results are written to CSV in append mode and will not be overwritten.

cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli                # 跑全部基准（结果追加到 CSV）
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only     # 只测 CPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only     # 只测 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --report       # 跑基准 + 生成 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy  # 生成报告并发布到 Hugo /benchmark/

--info will perform detection (OpenCL may only appear in detection results). For more detailed steps, see the Benchmark section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/benchmark/tutorial.md.

Website: Hugo Blog#

Automatically generated content is written to tools/website/content|static by each tool’s deploy pipeline, then translated, compressed, built, and pushed. tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository, which is automatically committed and pushed by build scripts; do not commit directly to it.

pip install -e ".[website]"                          # 安装依赖（含翻译用的 torch + transformers）
cd tools/website && bash update.sh                   # macOS/Linux：增量压缩 + Hugo 构建 + 推送 Pages
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1  # Windows（脚本会自己 cd 到所在目录）
cd tools/website && hugo server -D                   # 本地预览（开发服务器，含草稿）

For more detailed steps, see the Website section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/website/CLAUDE.md.

Translator: Gradio Document Translator#

Local inference; the default model is automatically downloaded upon first use. The source language can be set to auto]; when the target is auto, it flips between Chinese and English.

pip install -e ".[translator]"   # 安装依赖（gradio + GGUF 翻译栈）
python -m translator             # 启动 Gradio GUI（在浏览器打开）

For more detailed steps, see the Translator section in TUTORIAL.md. UI wiring is in tools/translator/app.py, translation and file logic is in tools/translator/core.py, and the shared engine is in common/engine.py and common/translation.py.

2.5 Suggested Order for First-time Onboarding#

Follow the path that can be connected strictly according to the README:

  1. conda activate AI, confirm Python 3.10+. If using ai-companion, prepare Node.js 18+ as well.
  2. Copy config.json from config.example.json; when keys are needed, place them only in tokens/ and do not commit.
  3. New machine: fill tokens/onboard.yaml, run scripts/onboard.py. For new Ubuntu servers, you can also refer to bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help.
  4. pip install -e ".[all]"; if using the translation GUI, then pip install -e ".[translator]".
  5. Use bash scripts/smoke.sh for a read-only smoke test.
  6. Use individual tools according to the commands in each section above; use python scripts/sync.py push / pull (requires rclone) for cross-device data.
  7. To change tool logic, go to tools/<tool>/; to change shared capabilities, go to common/; to change workflows/skills, go to ../ai-companion/.For more step-by-step operations, configurations, data formats, and FAQ, the README explicitly points to TUTORIAL.md and the source documentation of each tool; this tutorial does not use extra commands found in those files.

Gadget Project Summary and Usage Tutorial#

The following content is based solely on the README you provided, without adding any commands or parameters not present in the README.

I. Project Summary#

1. What is this?#

Gadgets is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development, covering:

  • AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly report generation
  • Paper discovery and research analysis
  • Performance benchmarking
  • Blog automation
  • Document translation

Features:

  • Every directory under tools/ is a standalone usable tool
  • Shared capabilities are centralized in the common/ package in the repository root (installed via pip install -e . ), including LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation, Hugo deployment, etc.
  • Development workflows (planning/execution/change tracking) and all Claude Code skills are provided by the independent repository ai-companion (located in the sibling directory ../ai-companion/ ), integrated into this repository via hooks

For more detailed step-by-step operations, configurations, data formats, and FAQ, see TUTORIAL.md and the documentation of each tool.

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具（改工具逻辑来这里）
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报/周报/月报

│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准测试

Goal Location
Change logic of a specific tool tools/<tool>/

3. Tool Overview#

Directory Function Key Technologies
tools/summarize/ AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly reports (multi-device two-stage architecture) Claude/OpenAI API, ccusage 20.x, matplotlib
tools/research/ Paper discovery + researcher analysis + citation graphs arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed, Semantic Scholar, LLM
tools/benchmark/ Cross-platform CPU/GPU performance benchmarking PyTorch, NumPy, Plotly
tools/website/ Hugo blog (incremental media compression + automatic build & publish) Hugo, pngquant, HandBrakeCLI
tools/translator/ Gradio document translator Gradio, GGUF/transformers
common/ Shared infrastructure package pip install -e .
scripts/ Operations scripts (sync, onboard, etc.) rclone, Python
../ai-companion/ AI change tracking + planning/execution skill pipeline Node.js, TypeScript

4. What does each tool do?#

Summarize — AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly reports#

  • Automatically reads daily AI conversation logs (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON)
  • Calls LLM to generate structured daily, weekly, and monthly reports
  • Multi-device workflow: Export conversations from each device → sync via cloud drive or manual copy → merge to generate daily reports → accumulate to generate weekly/monthly reports
  • Automatically discovers and statistics token usage and costs for various agent CLIs via ccusage 20.x
  • LLM backends (--api ): ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai

Research — Paper discovery and research analysis#

Unified entry point tools/research/research_scout.py with four major capabilities:

  1. Paper Discovery: arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed search, three-stage LLM pipeline (fast screening → deep review → citation impact), generates research weekly reports and deploys to Hugo; supports conference paper search and author search
  2. Deep Paper Insights (--insight ): Downloads full text, analyzes writing structure/publication strategy/reusable knowledge; matches OpenReview to obtain reviewer comments; synthesizes cross-paper writing guides
  3. Researcher Profiling: Uses ArXiv + Semantic Scholar data, LLM generates research trajectory analysis and hierarchical scoring; extracts mentor-student relationships via homepage and co-authorship patterns; supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup
  4. Citation Graph Analysis: Based on Semantic Scholar for forward citation/backward reference analysis + LLM impact interpretation

Benchmark — Performance benchmarking suite#

  • Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarking
  • Supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), Intel (XPU)
  • Precision: FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental)
  • Warm-up + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR outlier removal)
  • Results appended to CSV; can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards; can be deployed to Hugo or submitted to public leaderboards

Website — Hugo blog#

  • Static blog “TzJ’s Net” (PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages: https://tzj2006.github.io/
  • Incremental image/video compression (pngquant, HandBrakeCLI)
  • Local model bilingual translation (default Ollama; Linux fallback vLLM, Windows fallback transformers; model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded on first run)
  • Automatically generates content written to tools/website/content|static (with gadget_generated markers, so handwritten files will not be overwritten)
  • tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io ), automatically committed and pushed by build scripts; do not commit directly to it

Translator — Gradio document translator#

  • Local inference Web interface based on the common translation engine
  • Supports text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images), preserving Markdown format
  • Automatic backend selection: prioritizes ollama , falls back to transformers on Windows, prioritizes vllm on Linux, and offers llamacpp for low VRAM
  • Default model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B ; can be overridden by GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or GUI
  • Source language auto is detected by CJK ratio; target auto toggles between zh↔en

5. common / scripts / ai-companion#

common/: LLM calls, JSON parsing repair, SHA-256 disk caching, atomic writes, local translation engine, cross-platform Hugo deployment.

Main scripts/:

Script Function
sync.py rclone data synchronization (push/pull/status/bootstrap/config)
onboard.py One-time configuration for a new machine
smoke.sh Read-only smoke test (--help / --info / imports)
serve_local_llm.sh Creates an Ollama variant optimized for summarize and prints environment variables
language.py Hugo bilingual audit + summarize report renaming
profile_translation.py Translation engine GPU performance analysis

ai-companion: An independent Node.js repository providing code change tracking, planning/execution pipelines, and all Claude Code skills; see ../ai-companion/scripts/install.ts for installation.

conda activate AI
  • Node.js Environment: Node.js 18+ (only required if using the peer independent repository ../ai-companion/).
  • Local Translation/Model Environment: Translation and blog functions default to relying on the tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B model running via local Ollama (automatically downloaded upon first use; Linux alternative is vLLM, Windows alternative is transformers).

2. Installation and Initialization#

The project uses editable mode to install the base package and various tool dependencies:

2.1 Install Common Base Package and Most Tool Dependencies#

Install common/ and all tool dependencies except for translator (summarize, research, benchmark, website):

pip install -e ".[all]"

2.2 Install Specific Tool Dependencies#

  • Install Translator independent dependencies (Note: translator is not included in .[all], must be installed separately): 
    pip install -e ".[translator]"
  • Install Website dependencies separately (includes torch + transformers etc. required for local translation): 
    pip install -e ".[website]"

2.3 Run Read-only Smoke Test#

Verify if the environment and imports for all tools are normal (does not initiate network requests, LLM calls, or write operations):

bash scripts/smoke.sh

3. Configuration Instructions#

  1. Global Configuration File:
    • Copy the template file from the root directory to generate config.json (this file is gitignored): 
      cp config.example.json config.json
    • It contains running settings for various tools such as sync (rclone sync configuration) and summarize.
    • The configuration file path can be overridden via the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.
  2. API Keys and Credentials Directory:
    • The tokens/ directory is used to store API Keys and the new machine initialization manifest tokens/onboard.yaml (this directory is gitignored, do not commit).
  3. Global Environment Variable Adjustments:
    • GADGET_LLM_BACKEND: Globally specify the LLM backend (ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, openai).
    • GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: Specify the translation backend (ollama, llamacpp, vllm, transformers).
    • GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL: Override the default translation model name.

4. Typical Usage Methods for Each Tool (Directly Runnable Commands)#

4.1 Summarize —— AI Conversation Report Generation#

Unified entry point via python -m summarize. The LLM backend can be specified via --api (optional ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai).

  • Phase 1: Export unexported conversation records 
    python -m summarize daily export
  • Phase 2: Sync and merge daily to generate daily reports 
    python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all
  • Generate a specific weekly report and deploy to the blog 
    python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy
  • Generate a specific monthly report and deploy to the blog 
    python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy
  • One-click full workflow execution (Export → Merge → Weekly Report → Monthly Report + Deploy) 
    python -m summarize auto --deploy

4.2 Research —— Academic Paper and Scholar Research#

Unified entry point is tools/research/research_scout.py.

  • Run full paper research workflow (Search → Three-stage evaluation → Report generation) 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project
  • Natural language retrieval of papers (Automatic data source routing) 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "Find recent robot manipulation papers by Pieter Abbeel"
  • Scholar academic profile analysis (Input scholar name) 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"
  • Citation graph analysis (Based on arXiv ID or DOI) 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597
  • Deploy research reports to Hugo blog 
    python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

4.3 Benchmark —— Performance Benchmarking#

Note: Before executing benchmark commands, you must cd enter the tools/benchmark directory.

cd tools/benchmark
  • Run full benchmark (CPU + GPU, results appended to CSV) 
    python -m benchmark.cli
  • Run CPU benchmark only 
    python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only
  • Run GPU benchmark only 
    python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only
  • Run tests and generate interactive HTML reports 
    python -m benchmark.cli --report
  • Generate test reports and publish to the /benchmark/ path of the Hugo blog 
    python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

4.4 Website —— Hugo Blog Construction and Publishing#

  • Start local preview server (including drafts) 
    cd tools/website && hugo server -D
  • macOS / Linux environment: Incremental media compression + Hugo build + Auto-push to GitHub Pages 
    cd tools/website && bash update.sh
  • Windows environment: Update and build for release 
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

4.5 Translator —— Local Document Translation Web Interface#

  • Start Gradio Web GUI (automatically opens in browser after starting) 
    python -m translator

4.6 Operations and Scripting Tools#

  • Cross-device data synchronization (based on rclone) 
    python scripts/sync.py
    (or use python scripts/sync.py push / python scripts/sync.py pull)
  • One-click configuration and initialization for new machines (execute after filling in tokens/onboard.yaml): 
    python scripts/onboard.py
  • Create local Ollama models optimized for Summarize and export environment variables: 
    eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"
  • View help for server-level system initialization scripts (from peer ai-companion repository): 
    bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

5. Output Artifacts and Data Flow#

All generated files are centrally stored in the outputs/ directory (added to .gitignore):

  • outputs/logs/: Intermediate export logs and runtime logs
  • outputs/reports/: Final generated Markdown, JSON, and HTML reports
  • outputs/cache/: LLM call and search result caches
  • outputs/data/: Structured data (CSV benchmark data, scholar profile JSON)
  • outputs/images/: Charts and generated images
  • outputs/backups/: Backup files
