gpt-5.6-sol-high — 7,638 chars · 16/16 facts

I. Project Summary#

1. What is Gadget#

Gadget is a collection of daily development tools, mainly covering:

  • AI conversation daily, weekly, and monthly report generation
  • Academic paper discovery, paper analysis, and researcher profiling
  • CPU/GPU performance benchmarking
  • Hugo blog building, translation, and automatic deployment
  • Local document translation

The five tools under tools/ are independent and can be used separately; common capabilities are concentrated in the common/ package in the root directory, including:

  • LLM calls
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • Disk caching
  • Atomic writing and content hashing
  • Local translation
  • Hugo deployment

The project uses the GPL-3 license.

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报、周报、月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者画像、引用网络
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客构建与发布
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 本地文档翻译器
├── common/             # 所有工具共享的基础能力
├── scripts/            # 同步、机器初始化、检查等运维脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、计划、审计报告和历史归档
├── outputs/            # 自动生成的输出，已被 Git 忽略
├── AGENTS.md           # AI Agent 工作协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 包及可选依赖配置

Modification locations:

Requirement Directory or File
Modify a specific tool tools/<tool>/
Modify common capabilities like LLM, cache, translation, deployment, etc. common/
Modify data synchronization logic scripts/sync.py
New machine initialization scripts/onboard.py
Modify AI workflows or skills Adjacent ../ai-companion/ repository
View design and plans docs/, docs/ecl/

3. What the Five Tools Do Individually#

Summarize#

Reads conversation logs from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, or general JSON formats to generate:

  • Daily reports
  • Weekly reports
  • Monthly trend summaries
  • Token and cost statistics

It uses a multi-device two-stage process:

  1. Each device exports conversations.
  2. Data is aggregated and synchronized, then reports are generated.

Supports four LLM backends:

  • ollama: Default, runs locally, no API Key required
  • claude_cli: Reuses Claude Code login status
  • anthropic
  • openai

Research#

A unified academic research command-line tool containing four types of capabilities:

  • Search for papers from arXiv, bioRxiv, and PubMed
  • Download full texts and analyze paper structures, submission strategies, and OpenReview reviews
  • Generate researcher profiles, research trajectories, and advisor-student relationships
  • Analyze papers’ forward citations and backward references

It also supports ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, and openai backends.

Benchmark#

A cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS performance testing tool, supporting:

  • NVIDIA CUDA
  • Apple MPS
  • Intel XPU
  • FP64, FP32, FP16, BF16, and experimental FP8

Testing employs warmup, formal measurement, median statistics, and IQR outlier removal. Results are appended to a CSV without overwriting old records; it can also generate Plotly HTML reports and leaderboards.

OpenCL may appear in hardware detection info, but the README does not state it can be used for actual GPU testing.

Website#

A Hugo blog using the PaperMod theme, including:

  • Incremental image compression
  • Incremental video compression
  • Bilingual translation via local models
  • Hugo build
  • Automatic GitHub Pages commit and push

Images use pngquant, and videos use HandBrakeCLI. The deployment repository is located at tools/website/public/; it is an independent repository and files should not be committed to it manually.

Automatically generated articles will carry the gadget_generated tag; handwritten files without this tag will not be overwritten.

Translator#

A Gradio-based local document translation web interface, supporting:

  • Plain text
  • Markdown
  • TXT
  • PDF
  • DOCX
  • Images

During translation, Markdown snippets such as code blocks, URLs, and Hugo shortcodes are protected. Supports Ollama, transformers, vLLM, and low-VRAM GGUF/llama.cpp paths.

When the source language is set to auto, it detects based on CJK character ratios; when the target language is set to auto, it automatically switches between Chinese and English.

II. First-Time Use Tutorial#

1. Environment Preparation#

Minimum requirements:

  • Python 3.10+
  • Node.js 18+: Only required when using optional Companion graph and DAG publishing features
  • Website media processing requires Hugo, pngquant, and HandBrakeCLI
  • Cross-device synchronization requires rclone

The README recommends using a Conda environment named AI:

conda activate AI

All subsequent commands are executed in the Gadget repository root by default; except for the Benchmark section, which requires entering its own directory first.

2. Installing Common Packages and Main Tools#

Install the common common package:

pip install -e .

Install Summarize, Research, Benchmark, Website, and their optional dependencies:

pip install -e ".[all]"

all does not include Translator. Translator must be installed separately:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

If only using Website, you can install Website dependencies:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Each tool also has its own requirements.txt, but the README does not provide corresponding installation commands, so no speculation is made here.

3. Basic Configuration#

Root Configuration File#

Tool settings are located at the repository root in:

config.json

It is Git-ignored. You should copy and modify it using the following file as a template:

config.example.json

Other configuration files can also be specified via environment variables:

GADGET_CONFIG

The README does not list the specific fields of config.json, so you should refer to the template and each tool’s documentation.

LLM Backends#

Summarize, Research, and common LLM capabilities support:

  • ollama
  • claude_cli
  • anthropic
  • openai

The default is ollama. You can select the backend via the tool’s --api parameter or use a global environment variable:

GADGET_LLM_BACKEND

The README does not show the exact placement of --api in each subcommand, nor does it list the variable names for Anthropic/OpenAI API Keys, so you should not guess; consult TUTORIAL.md or the tool’s own tutorials.

Translation Configuration#

Translation models can be overridden via the following environment variables:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL

Translation backends can be selected via the following variable:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND

The translation backends described in the README include:

  • ollama
  • llamacpp
  • vllm
  • transformers

Local inference models will be automatically downloaded upon first use. Models mentioned in the README include:

  • The Ollama path uses local gemma4:26b
  • In-process translation uses tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B
  • The GGUF version is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF

Key Security#

API Keys and machine initialization tables are placed in:

tokens/

This directory is Git-ignored; never commit its contents.

4. Summarize Usage Tutorial#

Step 1: Export all dates not yet exported#

Execute on each device where AI conversation logs are saved:

python -m summarize daily export

Step 2: Synchronize and merge daily#

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Generate and deploy a weekly report for a specific week#

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

Where 2026-W12 is the ISO week format example provided in the README.

Generate and deploy a monthly report for a specific month#

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

The month format is YYYY-MM.

Run the full process with one click#

python -m summarize auto --deploy

This command executes the following in order:

  1. Export
  2. Merge
  3. Generate weekly report
  4. Generate monthly report
  5. Deploy

Old daily_summary.py, weekly_summary.py, and monthly_summary.py entry points are still compatible, but the README recommends using python -m summarize.

5. Research Usage Tutorial#

The unified entry point for Research is:

tools/research/research_scout.py

Full paper discovery and reporting process#

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

This process includes searching, three-stage evaluation, and report generation.

Search for papers using natural language#

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

The tool will automatically select the search source.

Generate researcher profiles#

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

Profiles may include papers, citation data, research trajectories, hierarchical scores, and automatically discovered advisor-student relationships.

Analyze citation networks#

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

This uses arXiv IDs. The README states that DOI is also supported, but no DOI examples are provided.

Deploy research reports to Hugo#

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

6. Benchmark Usage Tutorial#

All Benchmark commands require entering its directory first:

cd tools/benchmark

Run all tests#

python -m benchmark.cli

Results will be appended to the CSV without overwriting existing data.

Test CPU only#

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Test GPU only#

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

The tool will automatically detect CUDA, Apple MPS, or Intel XPU.

Run tests and generate an HTML report#

python -m benchmark.cli --report

Generate report and deploy to Hugo#

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

The deployment page is located at /benchmark/ of the Hugo website.

7. Website Usage Tutorial#

Install website-related dependencies#

pip install -e ".[website]"

macOS/Linux: Build and publish#

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

This script performs incremental media compression, Hugo build, and Pages push.

Windows: Build and publishExecute in the repository root:#

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

The script will automatically switch to the website directory.

Start Local Preview#

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

-D will include drafts in the preview.

Note:

  • Do not commit tools/website/public/ directly
  • Do not manually commit the deployment repository or the theme repository
  • Automatically generated content will be written directly to tools/website/content or tools/website/static
  • Files written by hand without the gadget_generated tag will not be automatically overwritten

8. Translator Usage Tutorial#

Install Dependencies#

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Start Translation Webpage#

python -m translator

After starting, the Gradio GUI will open in your browser. Models will be loaded on demand and kept in memory; models may be automatically downloaded upon first use.

Supported file types for translation include:

.md
.txt
.pdf
.docx
图片

Models can be managed via the GUI or by using GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL to override default settings.

9. Data Synchronization and Maintenance#

Open Sync Tool#

python scripts/sync.py

Sync configuration is located in the sync section of the root config.json.

Push Data Across Devices#

python scripts/sync.py push

Pull Data Across Devices#

python scripts/sync.py pull

These operations require rclone to be configured in advance.

Run Read-only Smoke Test#

bash scripts/smoke.sh

It checks the --help, --info, and import status of various tools without calling LLM, accessing the network, or writing files.

Start or Configure Local Summarize Model Environment#

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Persistent settings are placed in the summarize section of the root config.json.

View Server-level Initialization Script Help#

This script has been migrated to the adjacent ai-companion repository:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

Repository-level machine initialization uses tokens/onboard.yaml and scripts/onboard.py, but the README does not provide the exact execution command; therefore, you should check TUTORIAL.md or the script help before running.

10. Output File Locations#

Automatically generated results are unified in:

outputs/
├── logs/       # 导出日志、运行日志等中间产物
├── reports/    # Markdown、JSON、HTML 最终报告
├── cache/      # LLM 和搜索缓存
├── data/       # CSV、JSON 画像等结构化数据
├── images/     # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/    # 强制覆盖前的备份

outputs/ is ignored by Git, and its content should be regeneratable. Hugo content is an exception: it is written directly to tools/website/content and tools/website/static.

Finally, the following should NOT be executed: git add includes:

  • Automatically generated files in outputs/
  • rclone data synchronization
  • build/
  • gadget.egg-info/
  • Deployment and theme repositories under tools/website/
  • Keys and configuration tables in tokens/
grok-4.5-high — 7,678 chars · 16/16 facts

1. Project Summary#

Gadgets is a set of practical tools accumulated from daily development, covering: AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly reports, paper discovery and researcher analysis, performance benchmarking, Hugo blog automation, and document translation.

Each directory under tools/ is an independently usable tool; shared capabilities are concentrated in the common/ package in the repository root (installed via pip install -e . ), providing LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation, Hugo deployment, etc. Optional Companion graphs and planning capabilities are available locally; the sibling repository ../ai-companion/ provides DAG publishing. Coding agents follow AGENTS.md and are not intercepted by Companion.

Repository Structure#

Path Role
tools/ Five independent tool products
tools/summarize/ AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly reports
tools/research/ Paper discovery + researcher analysis + citation graphs
tools/benchmark/ CPU/GPU performance benchmarks
tools/website/ Hugo blog (incremental media compression + automatic build & publish)
tools/translator/ Gradio document translator
common/ Shared infrastructure (LLM / Cache / IO / Translation / Hugo)
scripts/ Operations scripts (sync.py, onboard.py, etc.)
docs/ Design docs, ECL plans, audit reports, historical archives
outputs/ All generated artifacts (gitignore, regeneratable)
AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md Agent workflows / Claude Code guide
pyproject.toml Packaging configuration (pip install -e .)

To change logic, see tools/<tool>/; to change shared capabilities, see common/]; to change sync, see scripts/sync.py]; for one-time new machine configuration, see scripts/onboard.py]; to change development workflow/skill, see the sibling repository ../ai-companion/.

What Each Tool Does#

  • Summarize: Reads conversation logs from Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON, etc., and uses LLMs to generate structured daily/weekly/monthly reports; multi-device two-stage process (export from each device → sync and merge); statistics for multi-source tokens and costs via ccusage 20.x; --api can switch between ollama (default) / claude_cli / anthropic / openai.
  • Research: Unified CLI research_scout.py, including paper discovery (three-stage LLM for arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed), deep paper insights (--insight), researcher profiling, and citation graph analysis; also supports four LLM backends.
  • Benchmark: Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS testing (CUDA / MPS / XPU, etc.), multi-precision, results appended to CSV, can generate Plotly HTML reports and deploy to Hugo.
  • Website: Hugo static blog (PaperMod, GitHub Pages); incremental compression of images/videos; local model bilingual translation; deploy artifacts from each tool are written to content|static then translated, compressed, built, and pushed.
  • Translator: A Gradio-based local translation webpage based on the common translation engine, supporting text and various file types, with tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B as the default model.

common: LLM, JSON, SHA-256 cache, atomic writes, local translation engine, cross-platform Hugo deployment.
scripts: sync.py (rclone sync), onboard.py (new machine config), smoke.sh, serve_local_llm.sh, etc.
ai-companion: Independent repository providing optional capabilities like DAG publishing.

2. Beginner Tutorial (Based only on README)#

2.1 Environment Preparation#

  • Python 3.10+ (Recommended conda environment AI: conda activate AI )
  • Node.js 18+ (Only required for optional Companion graphs and DAG publishing)
  • Specific dependencies for each tool can be found in the corresponding directory’s requirements.txt
  • Translation/Website: Local inference (default Ollama, chat model gemma4:26b; Linux can fallback to vLLM, Windows can fallback to transformers, using tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, automatically downloaded on first use)
  • tokens/ contains API keys and onboarding forms; it is gitignored, do not commit
  • Tool configurations are in the repository root config.json (gitignore; copy from config.example.json ); paths can be overridden using environment variables GADGET_CONFIG

2.2 Installation#

In the repository root:

# 安装 common + summarize / research / benchmark / website 等 extras
# 注意：all 不包含 translator
pip install -e ".[all]"

# 若要用文档翻译器，需单独安装
pip install -e ".[translator]"

# 仅网站相关依赖（含 torch + transformers 用于翻译）
pip install -e ".[website]"

pip install -e . will generate build/ and gadget.egg-info/ (already gitignored) in the repository root.

2.3 Configuration and Getting Started on a New Machine#

Configuration Files#

  1. Copy example configuration: Get the root directory config.json from config.example.json
  2. Optional: Use GADGET_CONFIG to specify a different configuration path
  3. LLM backends are globally available via GADGET_LLM_BACKEND or via command line --api: ollama (default) / claude_cli / anthropic / openai
  4. Translation backend uses GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama (default, reuses gemma4:26b ) → llamacpp / vllm / transformers (in-process, model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B )
  5. Translation models can be overridden: GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL (can also be managed within the Translator GUI)

One-click New Machine Configuration (This Repository)#

  1. Fill out tokens/onboard.yaml
  2. Run:
python scripts/onboard.py

It will automatically complete: SSH, Claude/Codex CLI installation and login, pip extras, configuration for each tool, and rclone bootstrap.
Note: onboarding will not install Companion; old fields install.ai_companion will be ignored.

Server-level System Installation (Optional, in ai-companion repository)#

The script for Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 one-click installation of SSH public keys, Claude Code, Codex, Superpowers, Ponytail, and AI Companion has been moved to:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

After the repository split, --companion-repo is directly transferred to the ai-companion repository (git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git ), and --companion-ref is no longer required.

Local LLM (Related to Summarize, Optional)#

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Persistent knobs are written in the summarize section of the root directory config.json (paths can be overridden using GADGET_CONFIG ).### Data Synchronization (Cross-device)Configuration: config.json section of sync (or GADGET_CONFIG).

python scripts/sync.py

The README specifies support for push / pull / status / bootstrap / config, covering summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups, as well as the special category dag (generating and deploying DAG sites). A cross-device example expression is:

python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

(Requires rclone to be configured first.)

Read-only Smoke Test#

bash scripts/smoke.sh

(Each tool --help / --info / import; no LLM calls, no internet connection, no disk writing.)

2.4 Typical Usage of Each Tool#

Summarize — Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

Multi-device workflow: Export conversations from each device → Sync or manually copy and aggregate to cloud storage → Generate daily reports → Accumulate to generate weekly and monthly reports. The new entry point python -m summarize is recommended (the old python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py etc. are still available).

python -m summarize daily export                                   # 阶段1：导出所有未导出日期
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all                         # 阶段2：同步所有日期并逐日合并
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy       # 周报 + 部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy      # 月报 + 部署
python -m summarize auto --deploy                                  # 一键：导出→合并→周报→月报+部署

LLM backend uses --api : ollama / claude_cli / anthropic / openai.

For more detailed steps, see TUTORIAL.md#summarize and tools/summarize/tutorial.md within the repository (referenced in the README; details are not expanded in this README body).

Research — Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis#

Unified entry point: tools/research/research_scout.py.

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project        # 全流程：搜索→三阶段评估→报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"  # 自然语言搜索（自动路由源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"             # 研究者画像
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597               # 引用图（arXiv ID / DOI）
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy                              # 报告部署到 Hugo

LLM also uses --api : ollama (default) / claude_cli / anthropic / openai.
Deep insight capabilities are noted in the README as --insight (described alongside full-text analysis, OpenReview capabilities, etc.); see TUTORIAL.md#research for specific sub-command combinations.

Benchmark — Performance Benchmarking#

Note: All commands must first enter tools/benchmark/.

cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli                # 跑全部基准（结果追加到 CSV）
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only     # 仅 CPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only     # 仅 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --report       # 跑基准 + 生成 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy  # 生成报告并发布到 Hugo /benchmark/

GPU will automatically detect CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU. Result CSVs are in append mode and will not be overwritten.

Website — Hugo Blog#

Automatically generated content is written to tools/website/content|static by various tools (marked with gadget_generated tags; un-tagged handwritten files will not be overwritten). tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), where build scripts automatically commit + push; do not commit directly to it.

pip install -e ".[website]"                          # 安装依赖（含 torch + transformers）
cd tools/website && bash update.sh                   # macOS/Linux：增量压缩 + Hugo 构建 + 推送 Pages
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1  # Windows（脚本会自行 cd 到自身目录）
cd tools/website && hugo server -D                   # 本地预览（含草稿）

Incremental compression: Media changed since .last_build — images via pngquant, videos via HandBrakeCLI. Translation defaults to local Ollama; the first run may download tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B.

Translator — Gradio Document Translation#

pip install -e ".[translator]"   # Gradio + GGUF 翻译栈
python -m translator             # 启动 Gradio GUI（浏览器打开）

Supports text and .md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images; protects code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc. Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF), which can be overridden by GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or the GUI. Source language can be set to auto (detected by CJK ratio); when the target is auto, it flips between zh↔en.

2.5 Outputs and Notes#

Generated items are unified in outputs/ (gitignore):

outputs/
├── logs/         # 中间产物
├── reports/      # 最终报告
├── cache/        # LLM / 搜索缓存
├── data/         # CSV、JSON 画像等
├── images/       # 图表
└── backups/      # 强制覆盖备份等

Hugo content is written directly to tools/website/content|static, with no separate outputs/site.

Notes (README Notes):

  • Do not git add: automatically generated content, rclone synced data, build/ / gadget.egg-info/, deployment/theme repositories under tools/website/
  • License: GPL-3 (see LICENSE)
  • For more detailed step-by-step operations, configuration, data formats, and FAQ: see TUTORIAL.md and the respective tool documentation; for the Chinese README, see docs/README.zh.md

All commands and parameters above are taken directly from the provided README; no options not mentioned in the README have been added.

gpt-5.6-luna-high — 9,263 chars · 15/16 facts

I. Project Summary#

1. What is Gadget#

Gadget is a development toolkit composed of multiple independent tools, primarily covering:

  • AI conversation daily, weekly, and monthly report generation
  • Academic paper discovery, researcher analysis, and citation mapping
  • CPU/GPU performance benchmarking
  • Hugo blog automatic construction, media compression, and publishing
  • Local document translation based on Gradio

Each tools/ subdirectory is an independently usable tool. The common/ in the repository root provides shared capabilities, including:

  • LLM invocation
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • Disk caching
  • Atomic writing
  • Local translation engine
  • Hugo deployment

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报、周报、月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 所有工具共享的基础设施
├── scripts/            # 同步、初始化、维护脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、计划和历史资料
├── outputs/            # 自动生成的文件，已被 Git 忽略
├── AGENTS.md           # AI Agent 工作流规范
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 使用说明
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 打包配置

Key directories:

  • Tool logic: tools/<tool>/
  • Shared capabilities: common/
  • Data synchronization: scripts/sync.py
  • New machine initialization: scripts/onboard.py
  • Configuration files: config.json in the repository root
  • Configuration templates: config.example.json
  • Sensitive information: tokens/
  • Generated results: outputs/

There is also an optional sibling repository, ../ai-companion/, responsible for DAG publishing and other Companion tools. Gadget itself does not automatically intercept Agent operations.

3. Tool Functions#

summarize#

Reads AI conversation logs from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, or general JSON formats, and calls LLMs to generate:

  • Daily reports
  • Weekly reports
  • Monthly trend summaries

It uses a multi-device two-stage workflow:

  1. Each device exports conversation dates that have not yet been exported
  2. Syncs and merges data, then generates reports

It also tracks token usage and costs for different Agent CLIs via ccusage.

Supports four LLM backends:

  • ollama: default, local Ollama, no API Key required
  • claude_cli: reuses Claude Code CLI login status
  • anthropic
  • openai

research#

Provides four types of capabilities through the unified entry point tools/research/research_scout.py:

  • Paper Discovery: Searches arXiv, bioRxiv, PubMed, followed by a three-stage LLM evaluation
  • Deep Paper Insights: Analyzes paper writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable knowledge, and analyzes OpenReview comments
  • Researcher Profiling: Analyzes papers, citation data, research trajectories, and advisor-student relationships
  • Citation Mapping: Analyzes forward citations and backward references of papers

Also supports ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, and openai.

benchmark#

A cross-platform CPU/GPU floating-point performance testing tool, supporting:

  • NVIDIA CUDA
  • Apple Silicon MPS
  • Intel XPU

Supports multiple precisions, including FP64, FP32, FP16, BF16, and experimental FP8.

Tests include warmup, formal measurement, GPU synchronization, and statistical analysis. Results are appended to CSVs (not overwriting old results) and can generate Plotly HTML reports and leaderboards.

website#

A Hugo-based static blog site deployed to GitHub Pages.

Main features:

  • Incremental compression of images and videos
  • Automatic construction and publishing of the Hugo website
  • Bilingual translation using local models
  • Receives daily reports, weekly reports, research reports, and Benchmark pages
  • Automatic generation of images and site content

Website-generated content is written directly to:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository and should not be submitted to directly.

translator#

A Gradio-based local document translator, supporting:

  • Text translation
  • Markdown
  • TXT
  • PDF
  • DOCX
  • Images

During translation, it protects Markdown code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc.

The default model is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

The corresponding GGUF model is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF

Supported local inference backends include:

  • Ollama
  • vLLM
  • transformers
  • llamacpp

4. common/, scripts/ and Companion#

common/#

A shared infrastructure package, installed via the following command:

pip install -e .

Provides:

  • Unified LLM API
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • SHA-256 disk caching
  • Atomic writing
  • Local translation engine
  • Hugo deployment capabilities

scripts/#

Main scripts include:

  • sync.py: syncs data using rclone
  • onboard.py: new machine initialization
  • smoke.sh: read-only smoke test
  • serve_local_llm.sh: creates Ollama variants for summarization
  • language.py: Hugo bilingual audit and report renaming
  • profile_translation.py: translation engine GPU profiling

ai-companion#

An optional sibling repository, primarily providing DAG publishing tools as well as planning and execution capabilities.

5. Output Directories#

Generated files are concentrated in outputs/:

outputs/
├── logs/         # 导出日志和运行日志
├── reports/      # Markdown、JSON、HTML 报告
├── cache/        # LLM 缓存和搜索缓存
├── data/         # CSV、JSON 等结构化数据
├── images/       # 图表和生成图片
└── backups/      # 强制覆盖时的备份

Hugo website content is not placed in outputs/site, but written directly to tools/website/content and tools/website/static.

II. Chinese User Tutorial#

1. Environment Preparation#

README requirements:- Python 3.10+

  • Node.js 18+, only required when using optional Companion graph and DAG publishing features
  • Recommended to use the conda environment named AI
  • Additional dependencies for each tool are recorded in the corresponding directory’s requirements.txt

Activate the recommended conda environment:

conda activate AI

Install public packages and dependencies related to Summary, Research, Benchmark, and Website:

pip install -e ".[all]"

Note: all does not include Translator. To install translator dependencies, you need to execute extra:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

If you only need to install the shared base packages, you can execute:

pip install -e .

2. Configuration Files#

Tool configurations are located at the repository root:

config.json

You can refer to:

config.example.json

README notes that config.json is ignored by Git. If you need to change the configuration file location, you can set:

GADGET_CONFIG

Sensitive information is placed in:

tokens/

This directory is ignored by Git and its contents cannot be committed.

LLM Backend Configuration#

Each tool supporting LLM can select a backend via --api:

  • ollama
  • claude_cli
  • anthropic
  • openai

Global environment variables can also be used:

GADGET_LLM_BACKEND

The default backend is ollama.

Translation Backend Configuration#

Translation functionality can use:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND

The selection order and backends listed in the README include:

  • ollama
  • llamacpp
  • vllm
  • transformers

The translation model can also be overridden via the following variable:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL

3. Using Summarize#

3.1 Export Chat Records#

Export all dates that have not yet been exported:

python -m summarize daily export

This is the first stage of the multi-device workflow.

3.2 Sync and Merge Daily Reports#

Sync all dates and merge them day by day:

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

3.3 Generate Weekly Reports#

Generate a weekly report for a specified week and deploy it:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

3.4 Generate Monthly Reports#

Generate a monthly report for a specified month and deploy it:

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

3.5 Execute Full Workflow#

Complete export, merging, weekly reports, monthly reports, and deployment in one go:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

3.6 Select LLM Backend#

For example, using local Ollama:

python -m summarize auto --api ollama

README explicitly states that the old entry point is still compatible:

python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py
python tools/summarize/weekly_summary.py
python tools/summarize/monthly_summary.py

It is recommended to use the new one:

python -m summarize

4. Using Research#

The unified entry point for Research is:

tools/research/research_scout.py

4.1 Generate Research Reports#

Execute the full workflow, including searching, three-stage evaluation, and report generation:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

4.2 Natural Language Paper Retrieval#

For example, searching for recent robotics manipulation papers by Pieter Abbeel:

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

This command will automatically select the appropriate data source.

4.3 Generate Researcher Profiles#

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

4.4 Analyze Citation Graphs#

You can use arXiv ID or DOI:

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

4.5 Deploy Reports to Hugo#

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

4.6 Select LLM Backend#

Research also supports:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project --api ollama

README only explicitly states that the backends supported by --api are ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, and openai.

5. Using Benchmark#

README specifically requires: all Benchmark commands must first enter tools/benchmark/.

cd tools/benchmark

5.1 Run All Benchmarks#

python -m benchmark.cli

Results will be appended to the CSV.

5.2 Test CPU Only#

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

5.3 Test GPU Only#

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

5.4 Test and Generate HTML Reports#

python -m benchmark.cli --report

5.5 Generate Reports and Deploy to Hugo#

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

The tool will automatically detect CUDA, Apple MPS, and Intel XPU. OpenCL might appear in the --info detection, but README states it is not used for actual GPU execution.

6. Using Website#

6.1 Install Website Dependencies#

If full dependencies are not yet installed, you can execute:

pip install -e ".[website]"

This installation includes Website-related dependencies, including torch and transformers required for translation.

6.2 Build and Publish on macOS/Linux#

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

This workflow will perform:

  • Incremental media compression
  • Hugo build
  • Push to GitHub Pages

Images use pngquant, and videos use HandBrakeCLI.

6.3 Build and Publish on Windows#

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

README states that this script will automatically switch to its own directory.

6.4 Local Preview#

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

Where -D indicates that the development server includes draft content.

6.5 Website Translation Behavior#

Website uses local inference for bilingual translation:

  • Defaults to using Ollama
  • vLLM can be used on Linux
  • transformers can be used on Windows
  • Model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B will be automatically downloaded upon first run

Automatically generated content carries the gadget_generated tag. Hand-written content without this tag will not be automatically overwritten.

7. Using Translator#

7.1 Install Translator Dependencies#

pip install -e ".[translator]"

README describes it as the Gradio and GGUF translation stack dependency.

7.2 Start Gradio Interface#

python -m translator

A browser will open after starting.

7.3 Translate Text and Files#

The interface supports:

  • Direct text input
  • .md
  • .txt
  • .pdf
  • .docx
  • Images

During translation, it will attempt to maintain Markdown format and protect:

  • Code blocks
  • URL
  • Hugo shortcode

7.4 Model and Language Settings#

Default model:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

GGUF version:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF

The model will be automatically downloaded when used for the first time, or it can be overridden via:

GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL

or set in the model management function of the GUI.

The source language can be set to auto. README states it will detect through the CJK ratio of the text; when the target language is set to auto, it will automatically switch between Chinese and English.

8. Using Sync and Maintenance Scripts#

8.1 Data Synchronization#

sync.py uses rclone to handle cross-device data synchronization, supporting the push, pull, status, bootstrap, and config operations listed in the README.

Sync script:

python scripts/sync.py

Cross-device push and pull usage:

python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

Sync configuration is located in the sync section of the root directory config.json, and the configuration path can also be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG.

The sync categories covered by this script include:

  • summarize
  • website
  • research
  • benchmark
  • backups
  • dag

DAG categories can be processed via:

python scripts/sync.py --category dag

Generate and deploy the DAG website.

8.2 New Machine Initialization#

First, fill in:

tokens/onboard.yaml

Then run:

python scripts/onboard.py

This script will automatically complete the initialization tasks listed in the README:

  • SSH configuration
  • Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication
  • pip extras installation
  • Tool configurations
  • rclone initialization

8.3 Run Read-only Smoke Test#

bash scripts/smoke.sh

This check only performs:

  • --help
  • --info
  • Import checks

It will not call LLMs, access the network, or perform write operations.

8.4 Start Local Summary Model#

Generate and use an Ollama variant dedicated to summarization:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Persistent configuration is placed in the summarize section of the root directory config.json.

9. Optional Server-level Initialization#

The server-level installation script has been migrated to the sibling repository ../ai-companion/.

View help:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

This script is intended for Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, and README states it can one-click install or configure:

  • SSH public keys
  • Claude Code
  • Codex
  • Superpowers
  • Ponytail
  • AI Companion

10. Important Notes When Using#

  • tokens/ contains API Keys and initialization information and must not be committed.
  • Content in outputs/ is automatically generated and is ignored by Git.
  • Do not commit build/ and gadget.egg-info/.
  • Do not directly commit the deployment repositories or theme repositories under tools/website/.
  • Hugo content is written directly to tools/website/content and tools/website/static.
  • LLM backends can be switched via --api or GADGET_LLM_BACKEND.
  • Translation backends can be switched via GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND.
  • Website and Translator use local inference and do not depend on cloud LLM APIs.
  • Generated results can usually be rebuilt from outputs/.

The following is a project summary and beginner’s tutorial organized entirely based on the provided README.md content.

Part One: Project Summary#

1. What is it?Gadgets (repository directory name gadget) is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development, covering five major directions: AI Daily Report Generation, Paper Discovery, Performance Benchmarking, Blog Automation, and Document Translation, open-sourced under the GPL-3 license.#

The core architectural feature of the project is “Independent Tools + Shared Foundation”:

  • Each subdirectory under tools/ is a tool that can be used independently.
  • The common/ package under the repository root aggregates the infrastructure shared by all tools (installed via pip install -e .), providing unified capabilities such as LLM invocation, JSON parsing and repair, disk caching, atomic writing, local model translation, and Hugo deployment.
  • Locally provides optional Companion graph and planning tools; the peer directory ../ai-companion/ repository provides functions such as DAG publishing. Coding Agents follow AGENTS.md, with no Companion interception hooks.

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 5 个独立的工具产品（修改某个工具的逻辑去这里）
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日 / 周 / 月报生成
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现 + 学者分析 + 引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客（增量媒体压缩 + 自动构建与发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 所有工具依赖的共享基础设施包（LLM / 缓存 / IO / 翻译 / Hugo）
├── scripts/            # 运维与维护脚本（sync.py, onboard.py, language.py, profile_translation.py 等）
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划 (docs/ecl/)、审计报告、历史归档 (docs/archive/)
├── outputs/            # 所有生成的产物（已 gitignore，可自动重建：含 logs/reports/cache/data/images/backups）
├── AGENTS.md           # 所有 AI Agent 的工作流协议（行动前必读）
├── CLAUDE.md           # 面向 Claude Code 的仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # common/ 与各工具的打包配置（pip install -e .）

Additionally, the README mentions the following important directories and files:

  • config.json: Tool configuration file in the repository root (gitignored, copied from config.example.json).
  • tokens/: Stores API keys and machine initialization configuration table tokens/onboard.yaml (gitignored).
  • build/ and gadget.egg-info/: Executable packaged products generated by pip install -e . (gitignored, always located in the repository root).
  • ../ai-companion/ (independent peer repository): Responsible for AI code change tracking, planning/execution skill pipelines, and all skills (based on Node.js, TypeScript).

3. What does each tool and core module do?#

① Summarize (tools/summarize/) —— AI Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

  • Functionality: Automatically reads daily AI conversation logs (supporting Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON), calls LLM APIs to generate structured daily reports, weekly reports, and monthly trend summaries.
  • Multi-device Two-stage Workflow: Stage one exports conversation logs from various devices; stage two synchronizes logs via cloud drives or manual copying to aggregate them and generate the final daily report. Once enough daily reports are accumulated, weekly and monthly reports can be generated.
  • Usage and Cost Statistics: Through the source-namespace commands of ccusage 20.x (ccusage claude, ccusage codex, ccusage gemini, etc.), it automatically discovers and statistics the token usage and costs of all agent CLIs.
  • LLM Backend: Supports ollama (default, local no-key, Gemma4-26B), claude_cli (reuses Claude Code CLI login state, no API key required), anthropic, and openai.

② Research (tools/research/) —— Paper Discovery and Scholar Analysis#

Provides four major functions through the unified CLI entry tools/research/research_scout.py:

  1. Paper Discovery: Searches for papers from arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed, generates research weekly reports via a three-stage LLM pipeline (Fast Screening → Deep Evaluation → Citation Impact) and deploys them to Hugo; supports conference paper search and author search.
  2. Deep Paper Insights (--insight): Downloads full paper texts, uses LLMs to analyze writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable core knowledge; automatically matches OpenReview to obtain reviewer comments for analyzing consensus and controversy; comprehensively generates cross-paper research writing guides.
  3. Researcher Profiling: Retrieves paper and citation data from ArXiv + Semantic Scholar, uses LLMs to generate research trajectory analysis, calculates tier scores, and automatically discovers mentor-student relationships via homepage extraction + co-authorship patterns; supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup.
  4. Citation Graph Analysis: Performs forward citation/backward reference analysis based on the Semantic Scholar API, combined with LLM for impact interpretation.

③ Benchmark (tools/benchmark/) —— Performance Benchmarking Suite#

  • Functionality: A cross-platform CPU/GPU floating-point performance (FLOPS) benchmarking tool, based on PyTorch, NumPy, and Plotly.
  • Hardware and Precision: Actual GPU execution supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU) (OpenCL may only appear in --info detection); covers precisions such as FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental).
  • Measurement and Reporting: Employs a “Warm-up + Formal Measurement + Statistical Analysis (median, IQR outlier removal)” approach and explicit GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy. Results are written to CSV in append mode (does not overwrite, naturally supporting multi-hardware cumulative leaderboards), can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards with Plotly charts, and supports deployment to Hugo websites and submission to public leaderboards.

④ Website (tools/website/) —— Hugo Blog#

  • Functionality: A static blog site based on Hugo (“TzJ’s Net”, PaperMod theme), deployed on GitHub Pages (https://tzj2006.github.io/).
  • Incremental Media Compression: Only compresses media files that have changed since .last_build (images use pngquant, videos use HandBrakeCLI).
  • Local Model Bilingual Translation: Does not rely on cloud LLM APIs; defaults to Ollama (Linux falls back to vLLM, Windows falls back to transformers; fallback model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded upon first run).
  • Automatic Content Injection and Publishing: Reports, pages, and images automatically generated by other tools are written directly to tools/website/content|static (marked with gadget_generated, never overwriting unmarked handwritten articles), then automatically undergo translation, compression, building, and pushing to the independent deployment repository tools/website/public/ (corresponding to tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io).

⑤ Translator (tools/translator/) —— Gradio Document Translator#

  • Functionality: A local Google Translate-style web translation tool (Gradio GUI) built on the common translation engine. Supports translating text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images) while protecting Markdown formatting (such as code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc.).
  • Local Inference Engine: Reuses common.engine.create_engine() to automatically select the backend (prioritizes ollama when model tags are pulled; Windows falls back to transformers, Linux prioritizes vllm, and the low-VRAM GGUF option is llamacpp). Models remain in memory (warm), with lazy loading on demand when switching models. The default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF), which is automatically downloaded upon first use.
  • Language Identification: Source language can be set to auto (detected based on CJK ratio in text); when the target language is auto, it automatically translates between Chinese and English (zh↔en).

⑥ Shared Modules and Ops Scripts (common/ and scripts/)#

  • common/: Provides a unified two-layer LLM invocation API, JSON parsing and repair, SHA-256 disk caching (supporting namespace + TTL), atomic writing and content hashing, local inference translation engine and bilingual content generation, and cross-platform Hugo deployment.
  • scripts/:
    • sync.py: A centralized data synchronization script based on rclone (supports push / pull / status / bootstrap / config, covering summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups categories, as well as the dag category used for generating and deploying DAG sites).
    • onboard.py: A one-time initialization script for new machines at the repository level.
    • smoke.sh : Read-only smoke tests across all tools (checks --help / --info / imports, without triggering LLM, network, or writes).
    • serve_local_llm.sh: Creates an Ollama variant optimized for summarize and outputs environment variables.
    • language.py (Hugo bilingual audit + summarize report renaming), profile_translation.py (Translation engine GPU performance analysis).

Part 2: Detailed Beginner Tutorial#

1. Environment Preparation#

Before starting, please ensure the following basic environment requirements are met:

  • Python 3.10+ (Recommended to use the conda environment named AI): 
    conda activate AI
  • Node.js 18+ (Only required when using optional Companion graph and DAG publishing features).
  • For specific dependencies of each tool, please refer to requirements.txt in the corresponding tool directory.

2. Installation Guide#

In the repository root, select the corresponding pip command to install based on your needs:

Method A: Install Base Package + All Tools except Translator (Recommended for most users)#

Install the common package and all extended dependencies for summarize / research / benchmark / website (Note: [all] does not include translator):

pip install -e ".[all]"

Method B: Install Specific Modules on Demand1. Install only the common shared base package:#

pip install -e .
  1. Install website dependencies (includes torch + transformers for translation): 
    pip install -e ".[website]"
  2. Install translator dependencies separately (includes gradio + GGUF translation stack): 
    pip install -e ".[translator]"

Verify Installation (Read-only Smoke Test)#

After installation, you can run the read-only smoke test script to verify that all tool imports and basic commands are working correctly (it will not call LLM, connect to the internet, or write files):

bash scripts/smoke.sh

3. Configuration and Machine Initialization#

3.1 Configuration Files (config.json)#

  • Persistent configurations for each tool are stored in config.json in the repository root (already gitignored). For first-time use, please copy one from config.example.json in the root directory to generate config.json.
  • To customize the configuration file path, you can override it via the GADGET_CONFIG environment variable.

3.2 New Machine/New Server Initialization (Optional)#

  • One-click Machine-level Initialization for this repository: After filling in the configuration information in tokens/onboard.yaml, run scripts/onboard.py once to automatically complete SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras installation, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.
  • Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 Server System-level Installation (located in the sibling repository ../ai-companion, used for one-click installation of SSH public keys, Claude Code, Codex, Superpowers, Ponytail, and AI Companion): 
    bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

    Note: After the repository split, --companion-repo is passed directly to git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git, and --companion-ref is no longer required.

3.3 LLM and Translation Engine Backend Configuration#

  1. LLM Backend Switching:
    • Can be specified via the --api parameter when running commands, or set via the global environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND.
    • Supports 4 optional values:
      • ollama (Default, local Ollama, no API key required, uses Gemma4-26B)
      • claude_cli (Reuses Claude Code CLI login state, no API key required)
      • anthropic
      • openai
    • To create a local Ollama variant optimized for summarize and load environment variables, run: 
      eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"
  2. Translation Engine Configuration:
    • Select the local inference backend via the GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND environment variable: Default is ollama (reuses gemma4:26b from the local Ollama service), or can be set to llamacpp / vllm / transformers (runs in-process, using tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B automatically downloaded during the first run).
    • The default translation model for the Translator tool can be overridden via the GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL environment variable or the model management function within the GUI.

4. Typical Usage for Each Tool#

4.1 Summarize —— AI Chat Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

Recommended to use the python -m summarize entry point (old versions python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ... / weekly_summary.py / monthly_summary.py remain compatible). LLM backends can be switched via --api.

# 阶段 1：导出所有尚未导出的日期对话记录
python -m summarize daily export

# 阶段 2：同步所有日期并逐日合并生成日报
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

# 生成指定周（如 2026-W12）的周报并部署到 Hugo
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

# 生成指定月（如 2026-02）的月报并部署到 Hugo
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

# 一键全流程：export → merge → weekly → monthly + 部署
python -m summarize auto --deploy

4.2 Research —— Paper Discovery and Scholar Analysis#

All functions are called uniformly through tools/research/research_scout.py, supporting LLM backend switching via --api (ollama / claude_cli / anthropic / openai), and deep paper insights are supported via the --insight parameter.

# 完整论文发现流水线：搜索 → 三阶段 LLM 评估 → 生成报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

# 自然语言搜索论文（自动路由数据源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

# 生成指定学者的学术画像（论文、引用、研究轨迹、评级、师承关系）
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

# 引用图谱分析（支持传入 arXiv ID 或 DOI）
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

# 将生成的研究报告部署到 Hugo 站点
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

4.3 Benchmark —— CPU/GPU Performance Benchmarking#

Note: All benchmark commands must be executed after first cd entering the tools/benchmark/ directory.

# 1. 先进入 benchmark 工具目录
cd tools/benchmark

# 2. 运行全部基准测试（CPU + GPU，结果以追加模式写入 CSV）
python -m benchmark.cli

# 仅运行 CPU 基准测试
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

# 仅运行 GPU 基准测试（自动检测 CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU）
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

# 运行基准测试并生成交互式 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report

# 生成报告并发布到 Hugo 站点的 /benchmark/ 页面
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

4.4 Website —— Hugo Blog Building, Compression, and Publishing#

# 1. 确保已安装 website 依赖
pip install -e ".[website]"

# 2a. macOS / Linux：增量媒体压缩 + 本地双语翻译 + Hugo 构建 + 推送 GitHub Pages
cd tools/website && bash update.sh

# 2b. Windows（PowerShell）：增量压缩 + 构建 + 推送（脚本会自动切换到自身所在目录）
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

# 3. 本地启动开发服务器预览博客（包含草稿）
cd tools/website && hugo server -D

4.5 Translator —— Gradio Local Document Translator#

# 1. 确保已安装 translator 依赖
pip install -e ".[translator]"

# 2. 启动 Gradio 网页翻译界面（会在浏览器中打开）
python -m translator

4.6 Cross-device Data Synchronization (scripts/sync.py)#

Depends on rclone configuration, reading the sync section in the config.json of the repository root.

# 运行同步脚本（支持 push / pull / status / bootstrap / config，以及 --category dag）
python scripts/sync.py

# 推送或拉取跨设备数据
python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

5. Directory Artifacts and Important Notes#

  1. Output Directory (outputs/): All intermediate logs (logs/ ), final reports (reports/ ), caches (cache/ ), structured data (data/ ), charts (images/ ), and forced overwrite backups (backups/ ) generated by all tools are uniformly saved under outputs/.
  2. Hugo Content Writing Mechanism: Content deployed to the blog by each tool is written directly to tools/website/content|static (files are marked with gadget_generated ; handwritten articles without this mark will never be overwritten).
  3. Git Commit Taboos (NEVER manually git add or commit the following content):
    • API keys and onboard.yaml under the tokens/ directory
    • config.json configuration files
    • All auto-generated artifacts and rclone sync data under outputs/
    • Packaging products of build/ and gadget.egg-info/
    • tools/website/public/ (this is an independent tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io deployment repository, automatically committed and pushed by build scripts, do not commit to it manually) and the theme repository under tools/website/.

Gadget / Gadgets is a collection of practical tools accumulated by the author during daily development, covering five types of work:

  • Key technologies: Claude/OpenAI API, ccusage 20.x (unified multi-source), matplotlib.### 3.2 tools/research/ — Paper Findings and Researcher AnalysisA unified academic research toolbox that provides four major capabilities through a single CLI entry point tools/research/research_scout.py:

  • Paper Discovery: Search for papers from arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed using a three-stage LLM pipeline (Fast Screening → Deep Evaluation → Citation Impact), generate research weekly reports and deploy them to Hugo; supports conference paper search and author search.

  • Deep Paper Insights (--insight): Download full-text papers, let the LLM analyze their writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable core knowledge; automatically match OpenReview to obtain reviews and analyze consensus and controversies; synthesize cross-paper research writing guides.

  • Researcher Profiling: Obtain paper and citation data from ArXiv + Semantic Scholar, use LLM to generate research trajectory analysis, calculate tier scores, and automatically discover mentor–student relationships via homepage extraction + collaborator patterns; supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup.

  • Citation Graph Analysis: Forward citation / backward reference analysis based on Semantic Scholar API, combined with LLM-driven impact interpretation.

All LLM functions support switching backends using --api: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai.

3.3 tools/benchmark/ — Performance Benchmark Suite#

  • Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarking, unifying floating-point performance measurements across different hardware vendors and precision levels.
  • Actual GPU execution supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), Intel (XPU); OpenCL may only appear in --info detection results.
  • Covered precisions: FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental).
  • Measurement method: Warm-up + Formal Measurement + Statistical Analysis (median, IQR outlier removal), with explicit GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy.
  • Results are accumulated in CSV in append mode (never overwrites, naturally supports multi-hardware cumulative leaderboards); can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards with Plotly charts, supporting deployment to Hugo websites and submission to public leaderboards.
  • Key technologies: PyTorch, NumPy, Plotly.

3.4 tools/website/ — Hugo Blog#

  • Hugo static blog site (“TzJ’s Net”, PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages: https://tzj2006.github.io/.
  • Built-in incremental image/video compression pipeline: only compresses media changed since .last_build (images via pngquant, videos via HandBrakeCLI).
  • Local model bilingual translation: Ollama by default, with vLLM on Linux and transformers on Windows as fallbacks; model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded upon its first run, without using cloud LLM APIs.
  • Automatically generated content (daily/weekly/monthly reports, research reports, benchmark pages, images) is written directly to tools/website/content|static by various deployment pipelines (the unique Hugo content root directory, files are marked with gadget_generated; unmarked handwritten files will never be overwritten), then translated, compressed, built, and pushed.
  • tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), automatically committed + pushed by build scripts; do not commit directly into it.

3.5 tools/translator/ — Gradio Document Translator#

  • A Gradio document translator built on the common translation engine: a Google Translate-style local translation webpage that can translate text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images), while preserving Markdown formatting (snippets like code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc., are protected).
  • Local inference, no cloud APIs: reuses common.engine.create_engine() to automatically select backends (prioritizes ollama if the model tag is already pulled; transformers is the Windows fallback, vllm is prioritized on Linux, and llamacpp is the low-VRAM GGUF option); models remain in memory for warmth, with on-demand lazy loading when switching models.
  • Default model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF), automatically downloaded upon first use, can be overridden via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or the model management within the GUI.
  • Source language can be set to auto (detected by CJK ratio of the text); when the target language is auto, it flips between zh↔en.

3.6 common/ — Shared Infrastructure Package#

The shared layer that all tools depend on, installed as a Python package via pip install -e .:

  • LLM invocation (unified two-layer API, supporting four backends: ollama (default) / claude_cli / anthropic / openai)
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • SHA-256 disk caching (namespace + TTL)
  • Atomic writing and content hashing
  • Local inference translation engine (Ollama / vLLM / transformers / GGUF) and bilingual content generation
  • Cross-platform Hugo deployment

3.7 scripts/ — Ops & Maintenance Scripts#

  • sync.py — Centralized rclone data synchronization (push / pull / status / bootstrap / config, covering summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups categories; there is also a special dag category for generating + deploying DAG sites). Run python scripts/sync.py; configuration is in the sync section of the repository root config.json (paths can be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG).
  • onboard.py — Repository-level one-time initialization for new machines: fill out a YAML table (tokens/onboard.yaml), run the script once, and it automatically completes SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras installation, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.
  • smoke.sh — A read-only smoke test covering all tools (--help / --info / import checks; does not call LLMs, does not connect to the internet, does not write files). Run bash scripts/smoke.sh.
  • serve_local_llm.sh — Creates an Ollama variant optimized for summarize and prints environment variables (eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"). Persistence knobs are located in the summarize section of the repository root config.json (paths can be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG).
  • Others: language.py (Hugo bilingual audit + summarize report renaming), profile_translation.py (translation engine GPU performance analysis).

3.8 AI Companion (Optional Tool)#

The peer ../ai-companion/ repository provides the DAG publishing tool used by scripts/sync.py --category dag. Existing local idea graphs, manual graph commands, and skills remain available. This repository has no Companion interception hooks; onboarding will not install Companion. Original install.ai_companion settings (including those in the old version of the onboarding table) will be ignored.

Tool Overview:

Directory Function Key Technologies
tools/summarize/ AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly report summary (multi-device two-stage architecture) Claude/OpenAI API, ccusage 20.x, matplotlib
tools/research/ Paper discovery + researcher analysis + citation graph arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed, Semantic Scholar, LLM
tools/benchmark/ Cross-platform CPU/GPU performance benchmark PyTorch, NumPy, Plotly
tools/website/ Hugo blog site (incremental media compression + auto build & publish) Hugo, pngquant, HandBrakeCLI
tools/translator/ Gradio document translator (based on common translation engine) Gradio, GGUF/transformers
common/ Shared infrastructure package (LLM, cache, IO, translation, Hugo deployment) pip install -e .
scripts/ Ops & maintenance scripts (sync.py rclone sync, onboard.py machine config, etc.) rclone, Python
../ai-companion/ (Independent Repo) AI code change tracking + planning/execution skill pipeline + all skills Node.js, TypeScript

4. Output Directory#

All generated products are unified in outputs/ (already gitignored, can be automatically rebuilt):

outputs/
├── logs/         # 中间产物（导出日志、运行日志）
├── reports/      # 最终报告（Markdown、JSON、HTML）
├── cache/        # LLM 缓存、搜索缓存
├── data/         # 结构化数据（CSV、JSON 画像）
├── images/       # 图表与生成的图片
└── backups/      # 强制覆盖备份（website-force 等）

Hugo site content is written directly to tools/website/content|static (no separate outputs/site staging tree).

II. Chinese User Tutorial (For First-time Users)#

Note: This tutorial only uses commands and parameters that appear in the README. The README itself is an overview; for step-by-step details of each tool, please follow the instructions to see TUTORIAL.md and each tool’s own documentation (noted at the end of each section below).

1. Environment Preparation#

Environment requirements provided in the README:

  • Python 3.10+ (conda environment AI recommended, activate with conda activate AI)
  • Node.js 18+ (only required for optional Companion graphs and DAG publishing tools)
  • Dependencies for each tool can be found in the corresponding directory’s requirements.txt
  • Website/translation functions use local inference engines: Ollama by default (the same gemma4:26b chat model is used for translation); vLLM on Linux and transformers on Windows as fallbacks (using tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, automatically downloaded upon first run)

Two additional global conventions regarding backends, to give you a concept:- LLM backends are unified and switched using the --api parameter: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic or openai; you can also use the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable for global settings.

  • The translation path uses a local inference engine, selected by GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama (default, local Ollama service, reusing existing conversation tags gemma4:26b) → llamacpp / vllm / transformers (in-process, model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B).

2. Installation#

Execute in the repository root. Common installation methods for ```bash pip install -e “.[all]”

 shared packages + tool extras:

```bash
pip install -e ".[all]"

Note: all does not include translator; the translator must be installed separately:

pip install -e ".[translator]"   # 安装依赖（gradio + GGUF 翻译栈）

If you only care about the website (including torch + transformers required for translation), you can install website extras:

pip install -e ".[website]"                          # 安装依赖（含翻译用的 torch + transformers）

To install only the shared infrastructure package itself:

pip install -e .

3. Configuration#

The configuration locations mentioned in the README are as follows:

  • Tool settings are located in config.json at the repository root (gitignored, copied from config.example.json). The path can be overridden using the GADGET_CONFIG environment variable.
  • Data synchronization configuration is in the sync section of config.json (the path can also be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG); cross-device data synchronization uses python scripts/sync.py push/pull (requires rclone to be configured first).
  • The persistence knob for serve_local_llm.sh is placed in the summarize section of config.json (the path can be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG).
  • The tokens/ directory stores API keys and onboarding tables, which is gitignored—never commit its contents.
  • Translation models can be overridden via the GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL environment variable (default tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B), or managed within the translator’s GUI.
  • One-click initialization for new machines (machine configuration for this repo): Use scripts/onboard.py—run it once after filling in tokens/onboard.yaml to automatically complete SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras installation, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.
  • Server-level system installation (a script for one-click installation of SSH public keys, Claude Code, Codex, Superpowers, Ponytail, and AI Companion on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 servers) has been migrated to the ai-companion repository: ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh. After the repository split, --companion-repo is directly passed to the ai-companion repository (git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git), and --companion-ref is no longer needed. For usage, see:
bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

A few auxiliary scripts worth knowing when starting for the first time:

python scripts/sync.py                                # 数据同步入口（rclone）
bash scripts/smoke.sh                                 # 只读冒烟检查：各工具 --help / --info / 导入，不调用 LLM、不联网、不写文件
eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"         # 创建 summarize 调优的 Ollama 变体并加载其环境变量

4. Typical Usage of Each Tool#

4.1 summarize — AI Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

The recommended new entry point is python -m summarize. The daily two-stage process (export from each device first, then aggregate and merge) allows you to accumulate daily reports before generating weekly/monthly ones; or you can run the entire pipeline with a single command:

python -m summarize daily export                                   # 阶段 1：导出所有未导出的日期
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all                         # 阶段 2：同步所有日期并逐日合并
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy       # 周报 + 部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy      # 月报 + 部署
python -m summarize auto --deploy                                  # 一键全流水线：导出 → 合并 → 周报 → 月报 + 部署

Supplements:

  • Old entry points python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ... / weekly_summary.py / monthly_summary.py are still available (backward-compatible shims), but the above python -m summarize format is recommended.
  • The four summary backends are switched via --api: ollama (default, local, keyless, Gemma4-26B), claude_cli (reuses Claude Code CLI login status, no API key required), anthropic, or openai.
  • For detailed steps, see the Summarize section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/summarize/tutorial.md.

4.2 research — Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis#

The unified entry point is tools/research/research_scout.py, with four typical operations:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project        # 全流水线：搜索 → 三阶段评估 → 报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"  # 自然语言搜索（自动路由数据源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"             # 研究者画像
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597               # 引用图（按 arXiv ID / DOI）
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy                              # 把报告部署到 Hugo

Supplements:

  • All LLM features support switching backends via --api: ollama (default, local Ollama, keyless, Gemma4-26B), claude_cli (no API key required), anthropic, or openai.
  • For detailed steps, see the Research section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/research/TUTORIAL.md.

4.3 benchmark — Performance Benchmarking#

Note: All commands must first cd into tools/benchmark/:

# 注意：所有命令都需要先 cd 到 tools/benchmark/
cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli                # 运行全部基准测试（结果追加到 CSV）
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only     # 只测 CPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only     # 只测 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --report       # 运行基准测试 + 生成 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy  # 生成报告 + 发布到 Hugo 的 /benchmark/

Supplements:

  • GPU benchmarking automatically detects CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU.
  • Results are appended to the CSV and will not overwrite old results, so the same CSV can naturally accumulate scores from multiple hardware setups.
  • For detailed steps, see the Benchmark section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/benchmark/tutorial.md.

4.4 website — Hugo Blog#

First, install dependencies (if .[all] is already installed, you can skip this; all already includes website extras):

pip install -e ".[website]"                          # 安装依赖（含翻译用的 torch + transformers）

Build, publish, and local preview:

cd tools/website && bash update.sh                   # macOS/Linux：增量压缩 + Hugo 构建 + 推送 Pages
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1  # Windows（脚本会自己 cd 到所在目录）
cd tools/website && hugo server -D                   # 本地预览（开发服务器，包含草稿）

Note:

  • tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository, which is automatically committed and pushed by the build script; do not commit directly to it.
  • Automatically generated content is written to tools/website/content|static by various deployment pipelines, and will only overwrite files marked with gadget_generated; manually written files will not be affected.
  • For detailed steps, see the Website section in TUTORIAL.md and tools/website/CLAUDE.md.

4.5 translator — Gradio Document Translator#

pip install -e ".[translator]"   # 安装依赖（gradio + GGUF 翻译栈）
python -m translator             # 启动 Gradio GUI（在浏览器中打开）

Usage (as described in README): Translate text within the opened webpage, or upload .md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / image files for translation; Markdown formatting will be preserved, and snippets like code blocks, URLs, and Hugo shortcodes are protected from translation. The default model is automatically downloaded upon first use; the source language can be set to auto for auto-detection, and the target language auto will automatically flip between Chinese and English. For detailed steps, see the Translator section in TUTORIAL.md; to see the code wiring, refer to tools/translator/app.py (UI), tools/translator/core.py (translation and file logic), and common/engine.py & common/translation.py (shared engine).

5. Newcomer Notes (from README Notes)#

  • GPU benchmarking automatically detects CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU.
  • The tokens/ directory holds API keys and onboarding tables; it is gitignored, never commit it.
  • All generated files are output to the outputs/ directory (gitignored).
  • LLM backends are unified and switched via --api: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, or openai (or use GADGET_LLM_BACKEND for global settings).
  • The translation path uses a local inference engine, selected by GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama (default) → llamacpp/vllm/transformers.
  • Cross-device data synchronization uses python scripts/sync.py push/pull (requires rclone configuration).
  • Never git add automatically generated content, rclone synchronized data, build artifacts (build/, gadget.egg-info/), or the deployment/theme repositories under tools/website/.
  • Tool settings are in config.json at the repository root (gitignored, copied from config.example.json); use GADGET_CONFIG to override the path.
  • The license is GPL-3 (see LICENSE).

6. Suggested Learning Order#

  1. Prepare a Python 3.10+ environment according to Sections 1–2 and execute pip install -e ".[all]" (add pip install -e ".[translator]" if the translator is needed).
  2. When full configuration for a new machine is required, fill in tokens/onboard.yaml first, then use scripts/onboard.py to initialize everything at once; for old machines/server-level installations, follow ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh.
  3. Run bash scripts/smoke.sh first to perform a read-only smoke test, ensuring that the --help / --info / imports for each tool are working correctly.
  4. Pick the tool you need most, run its command once according to Section 4, and then read the corresponding TUTORIAL.md chapter and the source documentation within that tool’s directory for deeper understanding.

1. Project Chinese Summary#

gadget is a collection of daily development tools covering scenarios such as AI conversation summarization, paper discovery, performance benchmarking, blog automation, and document translation. Each directory under tools/ in the repository is an independently usable tool; general capabilities are placed in the common/ package at the root, which is reused by each tool after installation via pip install -e ..

Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报 / 周报 / 月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施：LLM、缓存、IO、翻译、Hugo 部署等
├── scripts/            # 运维和维护脚本
├── docs/               # 设计文档、计划、审计报告、历史归档
├── outputs/            # 所有生成产物，已 gitignore
├── AGENTS.md           # AI agent 工作协议
