What each tool doestools/summarize/：Automatically reads AI conversation logs from Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON, etc., to generate daily, weekly, and monthly reports. Supports multi-device export, synchronization, merging, and statistics for token usage and costs. LLM backends available: ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, openai.#

tools/research/：Academic research tool, with a unified entry point at tools/research/research_scout.py. Supports paper search, research weekly reports, deep paper analysis, OpenReview comment analysis, researcher profiling, citation graph analysis, and can deploy reports to Hugo.

tools/benchmark/：Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarking tool. Supports NVIDIA CUDA, Apple MPS, Intel XPU, covering precisions such as FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8. Results are appended to CSV, and can generate Plotly HTML reports and leaderboards, or be deployed to Hugo.

tools/website/：Hugo static blog, deployed to GitHub Pages. Includes incremental image/video compression, bilingual translation, build, and publishing workflows. Automatically generated content will be written to tools/website/content|static, while hand-written content will not be overwritten.

tools/translator/：Local document translator based on Gradio, supporting text and .md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / image files. Uses the translation engine of common, with tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B as the default model, which will be automatically downloaded upon first use.

common/：Shared infrastructure package, providing capabilities such as LLM calls, JSON repair, SHA-256 disk caching, atomic writes, local translation engine, Hugo deployment, etc.

scripts/：Collection of operations scripts, e.g., sync.py for rclone data synchronization, onboard.py for new machine initialization, smoke.sh for read-only smoke checks, and serve_local_llm.sh for configuring local Ollama variants.

../ai-companion/：An independent optional companion repository for DAG publishing, planning/execution skill pipelines, etc. This repository will not install Companion intercept hooks.

2. Chinese Usage Tutorial#

Environment Preparation#

README requirements:

  • Python 3.10+
  • Recommended conda environment AI
  • Node.js 18+, used only for optional Companion graph and DAG publishing tools
  • Extra dependencies for each tool can be found in the corresponding directory’s requirements.txt
  • Cross-device synchronization requires rclone configuration
  • Hugo blog related functions require Hugo, as well as image/video compression tools pngquant, HandBrakeCLI
  • Translation defaults to using a local inference engine via Ollama; Linux can use vLLM, Windows can use transformers fallback

It is recommended to enter the conda environment first:

conda activate AI

Installation#

Install the shared package:

pip install -e .

Install extras such as common, summarize, research, benchmark, website, etc.:

pip install -e ".[all]"

Note: The README explicitly states that all does not include translator. The translator needs to be installed separately:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

If only installing website-related dependencies:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Configuration#

Tool configurations are located in config.json at the repository root, which is gitignored; the README instructs to copy from config.example.json. The configuration file path can be overridden using GADGET_CONFIG.

Unified support for API / LLM backends:

  • ollama: Default, local Ollama, no key required
  • claude_cli: Reuses Claude Code CLI login status, no API key required
  • anthropic
  • openai

You can switch via the --api parameter of each tool, or set it via the global environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND.

The translation backend is controlled by GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND. The selection order/backends listed in the README include:

  • ollama
  • llamacpp
  • vllm
  • transformers

The translation model can be overridden via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL.

The tokens/ directory is used to save API keys and onboarding sheets; it is gitignored, and the README specifically emphasizes not to commit its contents.

Summarize: AI Conversation Daily / Weekly / Monthly Reports#

The typical workflow is: first export conversation logs from various devices, then synchronize and merge them, and finally generate daily, weekly, and monthly reports.

Export all unexported dates:

python -m summarize daily export

Synchronize all dates and merge them day by day:

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Generate a weekly report for a specific week and deploy:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

Generate a monthly report for a specific month and deploy:

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

One-click full pipeline: Export, merge, generate weekly report, generate monthly report, and deploy:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

The README also mentions that old entry points are still compatible, such as python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ..., weekly_summary.py, monthly_summary.py, but the new python -m summarize format is recommended.

Research: Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis#

Unified entry point:

python tools/research/research_scout.py

Full paper discovery pipeline: Search, three-stage evaluation, and report generation:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

Natural language search with automatic data source routing:

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

Generate researcher profiles:

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

Perform citation graph analysis by arXiv ID / DOI:

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Deploy research reports to Hugo:

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

The README states that Research’s LLM functionality also supports switching via --api: ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, openai.

Benchmark: CPU/GPU Performance Testing#

The README explicitly states: all benchmark commands require entering tools/benchmark/ first.

cd tools/benchmark

Run all benchmarks and append results to CSV:

python -m benchmark.cli

Test CPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Test GPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

Run benchmarks and generate an HTML report:

python -m benchmark.cli --report

The /benchmark/ for generating reports and publishing to Hugo:

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

The README states that the GPU will automatically detect CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU; OpenCL may only appear in --info detection.

Website: Hugo Blog#

Install website dependencies:

pip install -e ".[website]"

Incremental compression, Hugo build, and push to Pages under macOS / Linux:

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

Run update script under Windows:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

Local preview, including drafts:

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

Translator: Gradio Document Translator#

Create an Ollama variant optimized for summarize and print the environment:

The README description for new machine onboarding is: after filling in tokens/onboard.yaml, run scripts/onboard.py once; it will handle SSH, Claude/Codex CLI installation/authentication, pip extras, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.

outputs/

Part One: Project Chinese Summary#

1. Project Introduction (What it is)gadget is a collection of practical tools accumulated from daily development practices, covering five major domains: AI Daily Report Generation, Academic Paper Discovery, Performance Benchmarking, Blog Automated Maintenance, and Local Document Translation.#

tools/research/ Research

Part 2: Detailed Usage Tutorial#

1. Environment Preparation#

  • Python Version: Python 3.10+ (recommended to create and activate conda environment AI): 
    conda activate AI
  • Node.js: Node.js 18+ (only for optional Companion graph and DAG publishing tools).
  • External System Tools (for corresponding tools):
    • website media compression requires system-level tools pngquant and HandBrakeCLI, as well as the static site builder hugo.
    • Data synchronization functions require installing and configuring rclone.

2. Installation Guide#

The project supports installing different extras on demand via pip’s editable mode (-e):

# 方式 A：一次性安装 common 基础包及 summarize / research / benchmark / website 工具依赖
pip install -e ".[all]"

# 方式 B：单独安装 Translator 工具依赖（注意：.[all] 不包含 translator，需单独安装）
pip install -e ".[translator]"

# 方式 C：仅安装 Website 工具所需依赖（包含用于本地翻译的 torch + transformers）
pip install -e ".[website]"

# 方式 D：仅安装根目录 common 基础依赖包
pip install -e .

Note: pip install -e . will generate build/ and gadget.egg-info/ directories in the root directory, which have been excluded in .gitignore.

3. Configuration Instructions#

  1. Configuration File config.json:
    • Configurations for all tools in the repository are uniformly saved in config.json at the repository root (already gitignored).
    • For first-time use, you can copy and create it from config.example.json.
    • To customize the configuration file path, you can set the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.
  2. Credentials and Keys Directory tokens/:
    • The tokens/ directory stores API keys and one-click setup configurations; it has been gitignored and is strictly forbidden from being committed to Git.
  3. New Server/New Machine One-click Configuration (Onboarding):
    • After filling out the tokens/onboard.yaml configuration, run the script to complete SSH, Claude/Codex CLI authentication, pip dependencies, and rclone initialization: 
      python scripts/onboard.py
    • To perform a system-level one-click installation on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, refer to the sibling repository script help: 
      bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help
  4. Switching LLM Backends:
    • Tools support switching backends uniformly via the --api parameter, options include:
      • ollama (default, uses local Ollama, no API Key required, model Gemma4-26B)
      • claude_cli (reuses Claude Code CLI login status, no API Key required)
      • anthropic
      • openai
    • Can also be set via the global environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND.
    • Start a tuned local Ollama and export environment variables: 
      eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"
  5. Local Translation Engine Configuration:
    • Switch via the environment variable GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama (default, reuses gemma4:26b) → llamacpp / vllm / transformers (runs tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B model, automatically downloads on first run).
    • The default translation model can be overridden via the environment variable GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL.

4. Typical Usage and Commands for Each Tool#

Tool 1: Summarize (AI Conversation Summary)#

# 阶段 1：导出所有未导出的对话记录
python -m summarize daily export

# 阶段 2：同步所有日期的记录并逐日合并生成日报
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

# 生成指定周的周报并部署
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

# 生成指定月份的月报并部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

# 一键全自动流程：export -> merge -> weekly -> monthly 并且发布部署
python -m summarize auto --deploy

Tool 2: Research (Academic Paper and Researcher Analysis)#

# 完整流程：论文检索 -> 三阶段评估 -> 生成项目报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

# 自然语言搜索论文（自动路由数据源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

# 分析指定研究者画像（轨迹、Tier 分数、合作网络）
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

# 分析指定论文的引用图谱（通过 arXiv ID 或 DOI）
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

# 将研究报告部署到 Hugo
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

Tool 3: Benchmark (Computing Power Benchmarking)#

Note: Before running Benchmark, you must cd into the tools/benchmark directory!

# 进入目录
cd tools/benchmark

# 运行全部基准测试（结果自动以追加模式写入 CSV）
python -m benchmark.cli

# 仅测试 CPU
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

# 仅测试 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

# 运行测试并生成 Plotly 交互式 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report

# 运行测试、生成报告并发布到 Hugo 博客的 /benchmark/ 路径
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

Tool 4: Website (Hugo Blog)#

# 安装博客构建及本地翻译依赖
pip install -e ".[website]"

# macOS / Linux：执行增量媒体压缩 + Hugo 构建 + 推送到 GitHub Pages
cd tools/website && bash update.sh

# Windows：执行更新与发布脚本（PowerShell，脚本会自动进入自身目录）
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

# 本地启动 Hugo 预览服务器（包含草稿）
cd tools/website && hugo server -D

Tool 5: Translator (Document Translation Web Interface)#

# 安装翻译器依赖（包含 Gradio 与 GGUF 依赖栈）
pip install -e ".[translator]"

# 启动 Gradio Web 界面（执行后在浏览器中打开）
python -m translator

Operations, Testing, and Data Synchronization Scripts#

# 运行全仓库各工具的只读冒烟测试（检查 --help / --info / 导入，无网络和写入）
bash scripts/smoke.sh

# 跨设备 rclone 数据推送与拉取（配置位于 config.json 的 sync 部分）
python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

5. Output Artifacts and Precautions#

  • Unified Output Directory: All task outputs are concentrated under outputs/, which has been added to .gitignore and supports rebuilding at any time:
    • outputs/logs/: Intermediate process logs
    • [[[HYMTPH_4697 الطيب]]: Final output reports (Markdown, JSON, HTML)
    • [[[HYMTPH_4698 الطيب]]: LLM cache and search cache
    • [[[HYMTPH_4699 الطيب]]: Structured data (CSV performance data, researcher profile JSON, etc.)
    • [[[HYMTPH_4700 الطيب]]: Generated charts and images
    • [[[HYMTPH_4701 الطيب]]: Backup files
  • Git Commit Workflow Standards:
    • Strictly forbidden to commit git add automatically generated content (contents of the outputs/ directory).
    • Strictly forbidden to commit rclone synchronized data or the build-generated build/ and gadget.egg-info/ directories.
    • Strictly forbidden to perform manual Git commits directly to the deployment repository (tools/website/public/) under tools/website/ or its theme sub-repository.

Gadget Project Interpretation and Usage Tutorial> The following content is based solely on the README.md you provided; no commands/parameters outside of the README have been fabricated. For detailed steps, the README explicitly states to refer to TUTORIAL.md, the Chinese version docs/README.zh.md, and the respective source docs of each tool.#

1. Project Summary#

1.1 What it is#

gadget is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development, covering:

  • AI conversation daily report generation
  • Paper discovery
  • Performance benchmarking
  • Blog automation
  • Document translation

Design Principle: Under tools/, each directory is an independently usable tool; general capabilities are sunk into the common/ package at the repository root (installed via pip install -e .), providing LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation, Hugo deployment, etc.

Additionally: Optional Companion graph/planning tools run explicitly locally without agent hooks; ../ai-companion/ is a sibling independent repository providing DAG publishing; the Coding agent follows AGENTS.md and is not intercepted by Companion.

1.2 Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 5个独立工具产品，改工具逻辑去这里
│   ├── summarize/      # AI对话 日报/周报/月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现 + 学者画像 + 引用图
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo博客（增量媒体压缩+自动构建发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包（LLM/cache/IO/翻译/Hugo）
├── scripts/            # 运维脚本（sync.py、onboard.py、language.py等）
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL计划（docs/ecl/）、审计报告、历史归档
├── outputs/            # 所有生成物（gitignored，可重建）
├── AGENTS.md           # 所有AI agent工作流协议，先读
├── CLAUDE.md           # 给Claude Code的仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # common+各工具的打包配置（pip install -e .）

The “Where to go to change things” lookup table provided in the README:

What you want to do Where to go
Change tool logic tools/<tool>/
Change shared capabilities (LLM/cache/translation/Hugo deployment) common/
Change data synchronization scripts/sync.py
One-time setup for a new machine scripts/onboard.py
Change dev workflow/skill ai-companion repository (sibling ../ai-companion/)
View plan/design documents docs/ecl/、docs/

Other notes:

  • build/ and gadget.egg-info/ are generated by pip install -e ., are gitignored, and are all at the repository root.
  • Data synchronization: python scripts/sync.py
  • outputs/ uniformly holds artifacts and is gitignored: intermediate products in logs/, final reports in reports/, LLM/search cache in cache/, structured data in data/, charts in images/, and forced overwrite backups in backups/.
  • Hugo site content is written directly to tools/website/content|static without passing through outputs/site.
  • tokens/ holds API keys and onboarding tables; it is gitignored and must never be committed.
  • Tool configurations are at the repository root config.json (gitignored, copied from config.example.json), and paths can be overridden using GADGET_CONFIG.

1.3 What each tool does#

Directory Function Key Technologies
tools/summarize/ AI conversation Daily/Weekly/Monthly reports, multi-device two-stage architecture Claude/OpenAI API, ccusage 20.x, matplotlib
tools/research/ Paper discovery + Scholar profiling + Citation graphs arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed, Semantic Scholar, LLM
tools/benchmark/ Cross-platform CPU/GPU performance benchmarks PyTorch, NumPy, Plotly
tools/website/ Hugo blog (incremental media compression + auto build & publish) Hugo, pngquant, HandBrakeCLI
tools/translator/ Gradio document translator (based on common translation engine) Gradio, GGUF/transformers
common/ Shared package (LLM, cache, IO, translation, Hugo deployment) pip install -e .
scripts/ Operations (rclone sync for sync.py, machine configuration for onboard.py, etc.) rclone, Python
../ai-companion/ (Independent Repo) AI change tracking + planning execution skill pipeline + all skills Node.js, TypeScript

Breakdown:

1. Summarize: AI conversation Daily/Weekly/Monthly reports

Automatically reads daily AI conversation logs (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON) and calls LLMs to generate structured daily, weekly, and monthly summaries. Multi-device workflow: export conversation logs from each device, aggregate them via cloud drive sync or manual copy, and then generate the final daily report; once enough daily reports are accumulated, weekly and monthly trend summaries are generated. Automatically discovers and statistics token usage and costs for various agent CLIs via ccusage 20.x source-based namespace commands (ccusage claude, ccusage codex, ccusage gemini…). There are 4 AI summary backends, switched uniformly via --api: ollama (default, local Ollama, no key required, Gemma4-26B), claude_cli (reuses Claude Code CLI login state, no key required), anthropic, and openai.

2. Research: Paper discovery and scholar analysis

A unified academic tool where a single entry point tools/research/research_scout.py provides 4 major capabilities:

  • Paper discovery: Search for papers from arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed through a three-stage LLM pipeline (fast screening → deep evaluation → citation impact) to generate research weekly reports and deploy them to Hugo. Supports conference paper search and author search.
  • Deep paper insights (--insight): Download full texts, let the LLM analyze writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable core knowledge; automatically match OpenReview to retrieve peer reviews and analyze consensus and controversy; synthesize cross-paper writing guides.
  • Scholar profiling: Extract paper citation data from ArXiv + Semantic Scholar, let the LLM generate academic trajectory analyses, calculate tier scores, and automatically discover mentor-student relationships via homepage extraction + co-authorship patterns. Supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup.
  • Citation graph analysis: Forward citation/backward reference analysis based on Semantic Scholar API, with LLM-powered impact interpretation.

LLM functions all support switching via --api: ollama (default, local Ollama, no key required, Gemma4-26B), claude_cli (no key required), anthropic, and openai.

3. Benchmark: Performance benchmark suite

Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarks, unifying measurements across different vendors and precisions. Actual GPU execution supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU) (OpenCL may only appear in --info detection); precision coverage includes FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental). Measurements use warm-up + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR for outlier removal), with explicit GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy. Results are accumulated in CSV in append mode (never overwritten, naturally supporting multi-hardware cumulative leaderboards), and can generate Plotly interactive HTML reports and leaderboards, supporting deployment to Hugo websites and submission to public leaderboards.

4. Website: Hugo blog

Hugo static blog (“TzJ’s Net”, PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages (https://tzj2006.github.io/). Includes a built-in incremental image/video compression pipeline (only compresses media changed since .last_build: images via pngquant, videos via HandBrakeCLI) and local model bilingual translation (default Ollama; vLLM under Linux / transformers under Windows as fallback; model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded on first run without using cloud LLM APIs). Automatically generated content (daily/weekly/monthly reports, research reports, benchmark pages, images) is written directly by each deployment pipeline to tools/website/content|static (the unique Hugo content root, files are marked with gadget_generated; unmarked handwritten files are never overwritten), then translated, compressed, built, and pushed. tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), where build scripts automatically commit and push; do not commit directly.

5. Translator: Gradio document translator

A Google Translate-style local translation web page based on the common translation engine, translating text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images) while preserving Markdown formatting (code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc., are protected). Runs local inference without calling cloud APIs: reuses common.engine.create_engine() to automatically select the backend (prioritizes ollama if the model tag has been pulled; transformers is the Windows fallback, vllm is prioritized on Linux, and llamacpp is the low-VRAM GGUF option); models stay in memory (warm), with on-demand lazy loading when switching models. Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF), automatically downloaded on first use, and can be overridden via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or the GUI’s model management. Source language can be set to auto (detected by text CJK ratio); when the target is auto, it flips between zh↔en.

6. common/ scripts/ ai-companion* common/：Shared layer that all tools depend on, installed as a Python package via pip install -e .: unified two-layer LLM API (4 backends: ollama default / claude_cli / anthropic / openai), JSON parsing fixes, SHA-256 disk cache (namespace + TTL), atomic writes and content hashing, local inference translation engine (Ollama / vLLM / transformers / GGUF) and bilingual content generation, cross-platform Hugo deployment.

  • scripts/：sync.py centralized rclone data synchronization (push / pull / status / bootstrap / config, covering categories like summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups; plus special dag category generation + DAG site deployment); onboard.py repository-level one-time configuration for new machines (fill one YAML table tokens/onboard.yaml, run once to automate SSH, Claude/Codex CLI installation/authentication, pip extras installation, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap); smoke.sh all-tool read-only smoke tests (--help / --info / import, no LLM, no network, no write); serve_local_llm.sh create summarize-tuned Ollama variants and print env; other language.py (Hugo bilingual audit + summarize report renaming), profile_translation.py (translation engine GPU profiler).
  • AI Companion: Brother ../ai-companion/ repository provides the DAG publishing tool used by scripts/sync.py --category dag; existing local idea maps, manual map commands, and skills are still available. This repository has no Companion interception hooks; onboarding does not install Companion, and install.ai_companion settings in old onboarding tables are ignored.

Note the README emphasis: all commands must first cd into tools/benchmark/.

cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --report
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy
  • Without parameters: Run all benchmarks, append results to CSV.
  • --cpu-only runs only CPU, --gpu-only runs only GPU.
  • --report runs benchmarks + generates HTML reports; add --deploy to generate reports + deploy to Hugo /benchmark/.

2.7 Typical Usage of Website#

pip install -e ".[website]"
cd tools/website && bash update.sh
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1
cd tools/website && hugo server -D
  • First line: Install dependencies (including torch + transformers for translation).
  • Second line macOS/Linux: Incremental compression + Hugo build + push to Pages.
  • Third line Windows (the script will cd to its own directory automatically).
  • Fourth line local preview (dev server, including drafts).
  • Before local preview/build, auto-generated content has been written to tools/website/content|static by various deployment pipelines; do not manually commit to tools/website/public/.

2.8 Typical Usage of Translator#

pip install -e ".[translator]"
python -m translator
  • First line: Install dependencies (gradio + GGUF translation stack).
  • Second line: Start Gradio GUI (open in browser). For UI wiring, see tools/translator/app.py; for translation and file logic, see tools/translator/core.py; for the shared engine, see common/engine.py and common/translation.py.

If you want to dive deeper into step-by-step operations, configuration items, data formats, or FAQs for a specific tool, the README points to: TUTORIAL.md + each tool’s own source doc (summarize see tools/summarize/tutorial.md, research see tools/research/TUTORIAL.md, benchmark see tools/benchmark/tutorial.md, website see tools/website/CLAUDE.md).

gpt-5.6-terra-high — 6,552 chars · 15/16 facts

1. Project Overview#

Gadgets is a set of independently usable development tools covering:- Generation of daily, weekly, and monthly reports for AI conversation logs

  • Academic paper discovery, researcher profiling, and citation graph analysis
  • CPU/GPU performance benchmarking
  • Building, translating, media compression, and publishing of Hugo blogs
  • Local Gradio documentation translation

The repository concentrates general capabilities in the common/ package in the root directory, including LLM calls, caching, JSON parsing, atomic writes, local translation, and Hugo deployment. Each tool is located under tools/ and can be run independently.

Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/
│   ├── summarize/   # AI 对话日报 / 周报 / 月报
│   ├── research/    # 论文检索、研究者分析、引用图
│   ├── benchmark/   # CPU/GPU 性能测试
│   ├── website/     # Hugo 博客
│   └── translator/  # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/          # 所有工具共享的基础设施
├── scripts/         # 同步、初始化、检查等运维脚本
├── docs/            # 设计文档、计划、审计报告和归档
├── outputs/         # 生成产物，已被 Git 忽略，可重建
├── AGENTS.md        # AI Agent 工作流程协议
├── CLAUDE.md        # Claude Code 仓库说明
└── pyproject.toml   # Python 打包及依赖配置

What the five tools do respectively#

Tool Purpose
summarize Reads conversation logs from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, or general JSON; uses LLMs to generate daily, weekly, and monthly reports, and summarizes token usage and costs across various Agent CLIs.
research Searches for papers from arXiv, bioRxiv, and PubMed; generates research weekly reports; analyzes full paper texts, OpenReview reviews, researcher career trajectories, mentor-student relationships, and citation networks.
benchmark Tests cross-platform CPU/GPU floating-point performance, supporting NVIDIA CUDA, Apple MPS, and Intel XPU; records results and generates Plotly HTML reports and leaderboards.
website Hugo static blog, supporting incremental compression of images/videos, automatic translation, building, and pushing to GitHub Pages.
translator Locally running Gradio translation web page, capable of translating text, .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, and images, while preserving formats like Markdown, code blocks, URLs, and Hugo shortcodes as much as possible.

Additionally:

  • scripts/sync.py: Cross-device data synchronization based on rclone.
  • scripts/onboard.py: One-time initialization for new machines.
  • common/: Shared LLM, cache, IO, translation, and Hugo deployment capabilities.
  • ../ai-companion/: An independent sibling repository providing optional DAG publishing and planning tools; this repository does not intercept Agent workflows.

2. First-time Use Tutorial#

The following content is strictly based on the README; the README also points to TUTORIAL.md and the documentation of each tool for more detailed configuration, data formats, and FAQs.

2.1 Environment Preparation#

Requirements:

  • Python 3.10+
  • Recommended Conda environment AI
  • Node.js 18+: Only required when using optional Companion graph tools or DAG publishing
  • For using websites and translation features, a local inference engine is required: Ollama by default; vLLM is available on Linux; Windows can fall back to transformers

The README recommends entering the Conda environment first:

conda activate AI

The base package shared by all tools can be installed in editable mode:

pip install -e .

To install all extra dependencies for summarize, research, benchmark, and website:

pip install -e ".[all]"

Note: all does not include the translator; the translator needs to be installed separately:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

The website tool itself also provides installation commands:

pip install -e ".[website]"

2.2 Basic Configuration#

Project configuration is placed in config.json in the repository root, which is ignored by Git. The README specifies that it should be created from config.example.json; if the configuration file is located elsewhere, the default path can be overridden via the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.

Notes:

  • tokens/ stores API Keys and new machine initialization forms; it is ignored by Git and should not be committed.
  • Generated files are located in outputs/, which also should not be committed.
  • Cross-device synchronization requires configuring rclone first.
  • LLM backends can be uniformly selected via --api:
    • ollama: Default, runs locally, no API Key required
    • claude_cli: Reuses Claude Code CLI login status, no API Key required
    • anthropic
    • openai
  • The LLM backend can also be globally specified via GADGET_LLM_BACKEND.
  • The translation engine is selected via GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND, defaulting to ollama; the README also lists local backends such as llamacpp, vllm, and transformers.

3. Typical Usage for Each Tool#

3.1 Summarize: AI Conversation Daily, Weekly, and Monthly Reports#

Use Case: You use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, ChatGPT, etc., on multiple devices and want to centrally export conversations to generate structured work summaries.

The workflow consists of two stages:

  1. Export unexported dates from each device.
  2. Synchronize or manually copy the summarized records via cloud drives, then merge them by day and generate reports.

Export all dates that have not yet been exported:

python -m summarize daily export

Synchronize all dates and merge them day by day:

python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

Generate a weekly report for a specific week and deploy:

python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

Generate a monthly report for a specific month and deploy:

python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

Execute export, merge, weekly report, monthly report, and deployment in one click:

python -m summarize auto --deploy

The README recommends using the python -m summarize format mentioned above. Old entry points remain compatible:

python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ...
python tools/summarize/weekly_summary.py ...
python tools/summarize/monthly_summary.py ...

Its LLM backend can be switched via --api, defaulting to local Ollama.

3.2 Research: Paper Discovery, Researcher Analysis, Citation Graphs#

The unified entry point is:

python tools/research/research_scout.py

Full paper retrieval and reporting process: Search, three-stage evaluation, and report generation.

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

Retrieve papers using natural language; the tool will automatically select data sources:

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

Generate researcher profiles:

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

Analyze citation graphs based on arXiv ID or DOI:

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

Deploy generated reports to Hugo:

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

This tool involves:

  • Paper searching in arXiv, bioRxiv, and PubMed
  • Three-stage LLM filtering: rapid screening, deep evaluation, and citation impact
  • Full paper insights and OpenReview comment analysis
  • Researcher analysis based on ArXiv and Semantic Scholar
  • Forward citation and backward reference graph analysis

The README states that its LLM backend can also be switched via --api.

3.3 Benchmark: CPU/GPU Performance Testing#

This tool requires entering its own directory first:

cd tools/benchmark

Run all benchmarks; results will be appended to the CSV and will not overwrite existing records:

python -m benchmark.cli

Test CPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

Test GPU only:

python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

Run tests and generate an HTML report:

python -m benchmark.cli --report

Generate reports and publish to Hugo’s /benchmark/:

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

The README states that this tool:

  • Automatically detects CUDA, Apple MPS, and Intel XPU.
  • Supports FP64, FP32, FP16, BF16, and experimental FP8.
  • Employs warmup, formal measurement, median, and IQR outlier removal, and explicitly synchronizes the GPU to ensure timing accuracy.
  • OpenCL may appear in --info detection but is not used for actual GPU testing.

3.4 Website: Hugo Blog Building and Publishing#

This blog uses Hugo and the PaperMod theme. Automatically generated daily reports, research reports, benchmark pages, etc., will be written directly to:

tools/website/content
tools/website/static

Generated content carries the gadget_generated tag; handwritten files without this tag will not be automatically overwritten.

Install website dependencies:

pip install -e ".[website]"

On macOS/Linux, execute incremental media compression, Hugo build, and GitHub Pages push:

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

On Windows, execute the corresponding script:

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

Preview the website locally, including drafts:

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

The README states:

  • Incremental image compression uses pngquant.
  • Incremental video compression uses HandBrakeCLI.
  • Local translation defaults to Ollama; Linux can use vLLM; Windows can fall back to transformers.
  • tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B will be automatically downloaded upon first use.
  • tools/website/public/ is an independently deployed repository, automatically committed and pushed by build scripts; content should not be committed directly to it.

3.5 Translator: Gradio Documentation Translator#

Install translator dependencies:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

Start the local Gradio web page:

python -m translator

An interface will open in the browser after starting. It can translate text and the following files:

.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / 图片

The README specifies the default model as:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B

The GGUF variant is:

tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF

The model is automatically downloaded upon first use. You can rewrite the default model using GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or manage models via the GUI.

Regarding translation direction:

  • The source language can be set to auto, identified through the CJK ratio in the text.
  • When the target language is set to auto, it will automatically switch between Chinese and English.
  • The translation process protects fragments such as Markdown code blocks, URLs, and Hugo shortcodes.

4. Operations and Auxiliary Scripts#

Execute cross-device data synchronization:

python scripts/sync.py

The README states that this script supports push, pull, status, bootstrap, and config, and requires rclone to be configured. A common form of cross-device synchronization is:

python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull

New machine initialization: Fill out tokens/onboard.yaml first, then run:

python scripts/onboard.py

It will handle SSH, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap.

Run a read-only smoke test, which will not call LLMs, the network, or write files:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

Create an Ollama variant for summarize and output environment variables:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

Finally, do not add automatically generated content, rclone sync data, build/, gadget.egg-info/, or the deployment/theme repositories under tools/website/ to Git.

Project Summarygadget is a “toolbox-style” repository that collects a set of practical tools accumulated during daily development, covering 5 types of scenarios:#

  • AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly report generation
  • Paper discovery and researcher analysis
  • CPU/GPU performance benchmarking
  • Hugo blog automation
  • Document translation

Its design follows “independent tools, shared core capabilities”:

  • Each subdirectory under tools/ is a standalone tool
  • The common/ in the repository root is the shared infrastructure package, installed via pip install -e ., providing unified capabilities to all tools, such as:
    • LLM calls
    • JSON parsing and repair
    • Disk caching
    • Atomic writes
    • Translation
    • Hugo deployment

Additionally, there are:

  • scripts/: Operations and maintenance scripts
  • docs/: Design documents, plans, audit reports, and historical archives
  • outputs/: All generated artifacts, which are gitignored but can be rebuilt
  • ../ai-companion/: A separate repository providing optional Companion/DAG related capabilities

Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报 / 周报 / 月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现 + 研究者分析 + 引文图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包
├── scripts/            # 运维和维护脚本
├── docs/               # 文档、计划、审计、归档
├── outputs/            # 生成产物
├── AGENTS.md
├── CLAUDE.md
└── pyproject.toml

What each tool does#

1. tools/summarize/#

Used to automatically organize your AI conversation records into daily, weekly, and monthly reports.

The README explicitly mentions that it supports reading conversation records from these sources:

  • Claude Code
  • Codex
  • Cursor Agent
  • ChatGPT
  • General JSON

The workflow is “two-stage, multi-device”:

  1. Export session logs from each device first
  2. Synchronize via cloud drives or manual copying for aggregation
  3. Generate daily reports
  4. Accumulate enough daily reports to generate weekly and monthly reports

It can also leverage ccusage 20.x to statistics token usage and costs for various agent CLIs.
The LLM backend supports unified switching:

  • ollama (default)
  • claude_cli
  • anthropic
  • openai

2. tools/research/#

This is a unified academic research CLI tool, with the core entry point being tools/research/research_scout.py. It has four major capabilities:

  • Paper Discovery: Search for papers from arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed, evaluate them through a three-stage LLM process, generate research weekly reports, and deploy them to Hugo.
  • Deep Paper Insights (--insight): Download full texts, analyze writing structures, submission strategies, and reusable knowledge, and automatically match OpenReview reviews.
  • Researcher Profiling: Perform research trajectory analysis, hierarchical scoring, and mentorship relationship discovery based on ArXiv + Semantic Scholar data.
  • Citation Graph Analysis: Perform forward citation / backward reference analysis based on the Semantic Scholar API, and use LLM to interpret impact.

The LLM backend also supports:

  • ollama (default)
  • claude_cli
  • anthropic
  • openai

3. tools/benchmark/#

This is a cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarking tool used to unify testing of floating-point performance under different hardware and precisions.

The README states it supports:

  • NVIDIA CUDA
  • Apple Silicon MPS
  • Intel XPU

And covers these precision levels:

  • FP64
  • FP32
  • FP16
  • BF16
  • FP8 (experimental)

Features include:

  • Warm-up + formal measurement + statistical analysis
  • Explicit GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy
  • Results are appended to a CSV file without overwriting old results
  • Can generate interactive HTML reports and leaderboards
  • Supports deployment to Hugo sites and submission to public leaderboards

4. tools/website/#

This is a Hugo static blog site, referred to in the README as “TzJ’s Net”, deployed to GitHub Pages.

It is not just a blog directory, but includes a complete automation workflow:

  • Incremental image/video compression
  • Bilingual translation
  • Build
  • Push deployment

Key features:

  • Images use pngquant
  • Videos use HandBrakeCLI
  • Translation defaults to local model inference instead of cloud LLM APIs
  • Automatically generated content is written directly to tools/website/content|static
  • tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository, which is automatically committed and pushed by scripts; it should not be manually committed directly.

5. tools/translator/#

This is a local document translator based on Gradio, reusing the translation engine from common.

It supports translating:

  • Text
  • .md
  • .txt
  • .pdf
  • .docx
  • Images

Features include:

  • Attempts to preserve Markdown formatting as much as possible
  • Protects code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc.
  • Local inference, no reliance on cloud APIs
  • Automatic backend selection:
    • ollama priority
    • transformers is the Windows fallback
    • vllm is Linux priority
    • llamacpp is suitable for low VRAM GGUF
  • The default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B
  • Source language can be set to auto
  • If the target language is set to auto, it will automatically switch between Chinese and English

What are common/, scripts/, and ../ai-companion/ respectively#

common/#

The shared base package for all tools, mainly providing:

  • Unified LLM calls
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • SHA-256 disk caching
  • Atomic writes and content hashing
  • Local translation engine
  • Cross-platform Hugo deployment

scripts/#

A collection of repository-level scripts; the README highlights these:

  • sync.py: Centralized rclone data synchronization
  • onboard.py: One-time initialization for new machines
  • smoke.sh: Read-only smoke tests
  • serve_local_llm.sh: Create Ollama variants optimized for summarize and print environment
  • language.py: Hugo bilingual audit and report renaming
  • profile_translation.py: Translation engine GPU profiler

../ai-companion/#

This is a sibling repository, not part of this repository. The README mentions it provides:

  • DAG publishing tools
  • Code change tracking
  • Planning/execution skill pipelines
  • Server-level installation scripts

Detailed Chinese Usage Tutorial#

The following tutorial is based only on the README. I. First, understand how to use this repository#

This repository is not a single application, but a collection of tools. The most common way to use it is:

  1. Prepare the Python environment first
  2. Install the shared package in the root directory and the dependencies for the tools you want to use
  3. Configure the repository root config.json
  4. Enter only the tool you need and use its corresponding commands
  5. Generated results are uniformly written to outputs/ or connected to tools/website/

The principles given in the README are very clear:

  • Each tools/<tool>/ is an independent tool
  • Shared capabilities are placed in common/
  • Tool configurations are in the repository root config.json
  • Sensitive information is placed in tokens/ and must not be committed
  • All generated results are placed in outputs/

The environment requirements mentioned in the README are:

conda activate AI

The command provided by the README is:

pip install -e ".[website]"

The README explains this will include website-related dependencies, including:

  • torch
  • transformers

Typical Commands#

1. macOS/Linux: Update, compress, build, and push Pages#

cd tools/website && bash update.sh

The README explains this will perform:

  • incremental compress
  • Hugo build
  • push Pages

2. Windows: Run PowerShell update script#

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

The README explains that this script will automatically switch to its own directory.

3. Preview Hugo site locally#

cd tools/website && hugo server -D

The README explains:

  • This is a local dev server
  • It includes drafts

Important Website Rules in the README#

  • Automatically generated content is written to tools/website/content|static
  • These automatically generated files will carry the gadget_generated tag
  • Handwritten files without this tag will not be overwritten
  • tools/website/public/ is a separately deployed repository
  • It will be automatically committed and pushed by the build script
  • Do not commit directly to this directory

For further details#

The README points to:

  • The Website section in TUTORIAL.md
  • tools/website/CLAUDE.md

XI. translator Usage Tutorial#

What this tool does#

It is a Gradio-based local document translator, suitable for translating text or files into another language while attempting to keep the Markdown structure intact.

Install Dependencies#

The command provided by the README is:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

The README explains that the following will be installed:

  • Gradio
  • GGUF translation stack

How to Start#

python -m translator

The README explains it will:

  • Start the Gradio GUI
  • Open in the browser

Supported Content#

The scope of support listed in the README:

  • Text
  • .md
  • .txt
  • .pdf
  • .docx
  • Images

Models and Backends#

The README explains:

  • Default model: tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B
  • GGUF variants: tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF
  • Automatically downloaded upon first use
  • Can be overridden via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL
  • Model management can also be done within the GUI

The automatic backend selection logic is written in the README as:

  • ollama auto priority
  • Windows fallback: transformers
  • Linux priority: vllm
  • Low VRAM GGUF: llamacpp

Automatic Language Detection#

The README explains:

  • Source language can be set to auto
  • It will automatically judge based on the text’s CJK ratio
  • If the target language is set to auto, it will automatically flip between zh ↔ en

For further details#

The README points to:

  • The Translator section in TUTORIAL.md

It also provides the code entry point locations for further investigation:

  • tools/translator/app.py
  • tools/translator/core.py
  • common/engine.py
  • common/translation.py

XII. How to use the Operations Scripts#

These scripts are not among the five main tools, but the README explicitly lists them as important components of the repository.

1. Data Synchronization: scripts/sync.py#

The README says it is used for centralized rclone data synchronization and can be used for:

  • push
  • pull
  • status
  • bootstrap
  • config

The entry point for running is:

The README also explains:- Covers categories such as summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups, etc.

  • Configuration path can be overridden via GADGET_CONFIG

2. New Machine Initialization: scripts/onboard.py#

After filling in tokens/onboard.yaml, execute:

The README says it will automatically handle:

  • SSH
  • Claude/Codex login
  • pip extras
  • per-tool config
  • rclone bootstrap

3. Read-only smoke check: scripts/smoke.sh#

bash scripts/smoke.sh

The README explains this is:

  • Will test --help / --info / imports
  • Does not involve LLM, network, or writing

The command provided in the README is:

The README describes it as:

The README does not provide specific command examples for these two scripts, so only their purposes are explained here without adding commands.

XIII. How to view the output directory#

The README explains that all generated results are concentrated in outputs/:

outputs/
├── logs/         # 中间产物

Part I: Open Source Project Gadgets Summary#

1. Project Introduction#

Gadgets is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development, licensed under GPL-3. The project covers the following 5 core domains:

  • AI Conversation Daily/Weekly/Monthly Report Generation (Summarize)
  • Paper Retrieval and Researcher Analysis (Research)
  • CPU/GPU Performance Benchmarking (Benchmark)
  • Hugo Blog Automation and Media Incremental Compression (Website)
  • Gradio Document and File Translator (Translator)

Each tool under the tools/ directory can be used independently; the common/ package in the root directory provides unified shared basic capabilities (including LLM calls, JSON parsing fixes, disk caching, atomic writes, translation engines, and Hugo deployment, etc.), installed via pip install -e .. All generated intermediate and final products are uniformly saved in the outputs/ directory.

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 5 个独立的工具产品（修改具体工具逻辑去这里）
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日/周/月报生成
│   ├── research/       # 论文检索 + 研究者分析 + 引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 跨平台性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客（增量媒体压缩 + 自动化构建与发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础架构包（LLM / 缓存 / IO / 翻译 / Hugo 部署）— 被所有工具依赖
├── scripts/            # 运维与维护脚本（sync.py, onboard.py, language.py, profile_translation.py 等）
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划 (docs/ecl/)、审计报告与历史归档 (docs/archive/)
├── outputs/            # 所有生成的产物目录（已 gitignore，可自动重建）
│   ├── logs/           # 中间日志（导出日志、运行日志）
│   ├── reports/        # 最终报告（Markdown, JSON, HTML）
│   ├── cache/          # LLM 缓存、搜索缓存
│   ├── data/           # 结构化数据（CSV, JSON profiles）
│   ├── images/         # 图表与生成的图片
│   └── backups/        # 强制覆盖备份（website-force 等）
├── AGENTS.md           # 所有 AI agent 的工作流协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # common/ 及各工具的打包配置 (pip install -e .)

3. Introduction to Tool Functions#

  • Summarize (AI Conversation Report Generation): Automatically reads daily AI conversation logs (supporting Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON), calls LLM APIs to generate structured daily, weekly, and monthly reports. It uses a multi-device two-stage architecture (Device Export → Cloud Drive Sync/Manual Merge → Daily Merge Export → Generate Weekly/Monthly Reports). Integrates ccusage 20.x to automatically count Agent CLI Token usage and costs. Supports switching between 4 backends (ollama default, claude_cli, anthropic, openai).
  • Research (Paper Retrieval and Researcher Analysis): Provides four major capabilities through the unified CLI entry tools/research/research_scout.py:
    1. Paper Retrieval: Performs three-stage LLM screening, evaluation, and impact analysis via arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed, generating research weekly reports and deploying them to Hugo;
    2. Deep Paper Insights (--insight): Downloads full texts to analyze structure and publication strategies, automatically matching OpenReview reviewer comments;
    3. Researcher Profiling: Combines arXiv + Semantic Scholar to analyze research trajectories, calculate tier scores, and extract mentor-student relationships;
    4. Citation Graph Analysis: Analyzes forward and backward citations and interprets LLM impact based on the Semantic Scholar API.
  • Benchmark (Performance Benchmarking): A cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS floating-point performance testing tool. Actual GPU execution supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU), covering FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental) precisions. It employs warm-up, formal measurement, median/IQR outlier removal, and explicit GPU synchronization. Results are appended to CSV files (supporting multi-hardware accumulation), and it can generate Plotly interactive HTML reports and leaderboards.
  • Website (Hugo Blog): A blog based on Hugo (PaperMod theme) (“TzJ’s Net”), deployed to GitHub Pages. It features built-in incremental media compression (pngquant for images, HandBrakeCLI for videos) and local model bilingual translation (defaulting to Ollama; Linux uses vLLM / Windows uses transformers, automatically downloading tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B). Generated content is written directly to tools/website/content|static (handwritten files marked with gadget_generated will not be overwritten).
  • Translator (Gradio Document Translator): A local Google Translate-like web interface built on the common translation engine. Supports text and file translation (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images) while maintaining Markdown formatting (protecting code blocks, URLs, and Hugo shortcodes). It performs pure local inference with automatic model selection (prioritizing ollama, choosing transformers for Windows, vllm for Linux, and llamacpp for low VRAM), with the default model being tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF). It automatically switches between Chinese and English (zh↔en) based on CJK ratio detection.

Part II: Detailed Usage Tutorial#

1. Environment Preparation and Configuration#

  • Python Version: Requires Python 3.10+ (recommended to use the conda environment AI, i.e., conda activate AI).
  • Node.js Version: Node.js 18+ (only required when using optional Companion graphs and DAG publishing tools).
  • Configuration Files and Keys:
    • API Keys and machine initialization forms are stored in the tokens/ directory (gitignored).
    • Project configuration is stored in the root directory config.json (can be copied from config.example.json), and the configuration file path can be specified using the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.
  • LLM and Translation Backend Settings:
    • LLM backends can be specified via the command line --api parameter or the environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai.
    • Translation backends are specified by the environment variable GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama (default) / llamacpp / vllm / transformers.

2. Installation#

4. Typical Usage and Commands for Each Tool#

gemini-3.1-pro — 4,422 chars · 13/16 facts

This is a Chinese summary and detailed usage tutorial based on the provided README content.

Part 1: Project Summary#

1. Project Introduction (What is it)#

Gadgets is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development. It mainly covers five functional areas: AI daily conversation report generation, academic paper discovery and analysis, cross-platform hardware performance benchmarking, automated blog deployment, and document translation. The project adopts a “modular” design: all tools can be used independently, while their shared core capabilities (such as LLM invocation, disk caching, translation engines, etc.) are unified and extracted into a common package (common).

2. Repository Structure (Repository Structure)#

The directory structure of the entire repository clearly divides tools, common components, scripts, and output directories:

  • tools/: Core directory, containing 5 independent tool products.
  • common/: Shared infrastructure package (handling LLM, cache, file IO, translation, Hugo deployment, etc.), which all tools depend on.
  • scripts/: O&M and management scripts directory, containing scripts such as data synchronization (sync.py) and new machine onboarding (onboard.py).
  • docs/: Documentation directory, containing design documents, plans, audit reports, and historical archives.
  • outputs/: All products automatically generated by all tools (such as logs, reports, cache, data, charts, etc.) are output here (configured with gitignore).
  • Others: AGENTS.md (AI Agent workflow protocol), CLAUDE.md (Claude Code repository guide), pyproject.toml (packaging configuration files).

3. What Each Tool Does (Tools at a Glance)#

In the tools/ directory, the five tools are responsible for the following functions:

  1. summarize (AI Report Summarization): Automatically reads your AI conversation records across various devices (such as Claude, ChatGPT, etc.), calculates Token consumption and costs, and generates structured daily, weekly, and monthly summary reports via LLMs.
  2. research (Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis): An academic research toolkit. It supports retrieving papers from major preprint and literature databases and performing three-stage deep LLM evaluations; it can also analyze researchers’ academic trajectories, generate relationship graphs, and perform paper citation graph analysis.
  3. benchmark (Performance Benchmarking): A cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS performance testing tool. It supports unified measurement of performance across different hardware vendors (NVIDIA, Apple, Intel) and different precisions, generating HTML reports with charts and leaderboards.
  4. website (Hugo Blog Automated Deployment): Used for building and publishing Hugo static blogs. It features a built-in incremental media compression pipeline (only compressing changed images and videos), supports bilingual translation using local models, and can automatically build and push generated reports and articles to GitHub Pages.
  5. translator (Gradio Document Translator): A Gradio-based local document translation web interface. It supports the translation of text as well as .md, .txt, .pdf, and .docx files, perfectly preserving Markdown formatting during the translation process. It uses entirely local model inference without requiring cloud APIs.

Part 2: Detailed Beginner’s Tutorial#

For users encountering this project for the first time, please follow these steps for environment preparation, installation, configuration, and usage.

I. Environment Preparation#

  1. Python Environment: Requires Python 3.10 or higher (it is recommended to use Conda to create an independent environment, such as conda activate AI).
  2. Node.js (Optional): Node.js 18+ (only required if you need to use the optional Companion graph and DAG publishing features).

II. Installation and Configuration#

1. Dependency Installation Run the following commands in the repository root to install the base package and most tools (summarize, research, benchmark, website):

pip install -e ".[all]"

Note: [all] does not include translator. If you need to use the translation tool, you must execute extra steps:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

2. Configuration File Initialization

  • General Configuration: The project’s runtime configuration is located in config.json in the repository root. You need to copy the example file config.example.json to config.json (this file will be ignored by Git). You can also specify other paths by setting the GADGET_CONFIG environment variable.
  • One-click Onboarding for New Machines (Optional): If you are configuring on a new server, you can fill in information in tokens/onboard.yaml and then run the following script to automatically complete SSH, CLI authentication, dependency installation, and other configurations: 
    python scripts/onboard.py

III. Typical Usage of Each Tool#

The following are the most commonly used, ready-to-copy running commands for each tool.

1. Summarize (AI Report Generation)#

Supports automatic collection of your AI chat records and generating summaries. The LLM backend defaults to the local ollama, but can be switched to claude_cli, anthropic, or openai via the --api parameter.

# 步骤 1：导出所有未导出的历史日期数据
python -m summarize daily export

# 步骤 2：同步并按天合并每日数据
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

# 步骤 3：生成指定周的周报并部署
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

# 步骤 4：生成指定月的月报并部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

# 🌟 懒人一键命令：全流程自动执行（导出 → 合并 → 周报 → 月报 → 部署）
python -m summarize auto --deploy
2. Research (Scientific Research and Paper Analysis)#

Called uniformly through the research_scout.py entry point, which also supports switching different LLM backends via the --api parameter.

# 全流程：搜索论文 → 三阶段评估 → 生成报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

# 自然语言快速搜索（自动路由来源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

# 生成指定研究人员的分析画像（学术轨迹、关系网等）
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

# 根据 arXiv ID 或 DOI 生成引用图谱
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

# 将生成的报告部署到 Hugo 博客
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy
3. Benchmark (Performance Testing)#

Used to test CPU/GPU floating-point operation performance. Note: You must enter the benchmark directory before executing these commands.

cd tools/benchmark

# 运行所有基准测试（结果会自动追加到 CSV 文件中）
python -m benchmark.cli

# 仅测试 CPU
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only

# 仅测试 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

# 运行测试并生成包含图表的 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report

# 生成报告并将其发布到 Hugo 博客的 /benchmark/ 路径下
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy
4. Website (Hugo Blog)#

Used for automated building of static blogs. It includes built-in scripts for incremental compression and automatic pushing to GitHub Pages.

# 确保你已安装对应的 website 依赖包
pip install -e ".[website]"

# 【macOS / Linux 系统】执行增量压缩、Hugo 构建并推送
cd tools/website && bash update.sh

# 【Windows 系统】执行增量压缩、构建并推送
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

# 本地预览你的博客网站（包含草稿）
cd tools/website && hugo server -D

Tip: All automatically generated content will be written directly to tools/website/content|static. The built public website is deployed in a separate tools/website/public/ repository; the script will automatically commit and push, so please do not manually commit code to the public directory.

5. Translator (Document Translator)#

Starts a web-based UI that supports document translation, capable of safely protecting code blocks and formatting when translating long Markdown files and other documents.

# 确保已安装翻译组件所需依赖
pip install -e ".[translator]"

# 启动 Gradio 网页界面（会自动在浏览器中打开）
python -m translator

Tip: This tool will automatically download the default translation model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B upon its first run. The translation engine runs entirely locally. You can switch models via the UI or by setting the GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL environment variable.
