  • outputs/ stores all generated results; it is reconstructible and ignored by Git.
  • There is also an optional adjacent repository ../ai-companion/ used for capabilities like DAG publishing.

In short: This is a tool repository built around five types of tasks: AI reports, paper research, performance benchmarking, blog automation, and document translation.

Repository Structure#

The structure provided in the README can be understood as follows:- tools/summarize/：AI Conversation Daily / Weekly / Monthly Reports

  • tools/research/：Paper Discovery + Researcher Analysis + Citation Graphs
  • tools/benchmark/：CPU / GPU Performance Benchmarking
  • tools/website/：Hugo blog site, with automatic compression, build, and publish
  • tools/translator/：Gradio Document Translator
  • common/：Shared Base Library
  • scripts/：Maintenance scripts for sync, onboarding configuration, smoke tests, etc.
  • docs/：Design docs, ECL plans, audit reports, historical archives
  • outputs/：All generated artifacts
  • AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md：Workflow and repository guides
  • pyproject.toml：Packaging configuration

What each tool does#

summarize#

Automatically reads your daily AI conversation logs to generate structured daily, weekly, and monthly reports. It supports multi-device workflows: first export conversation logs from various devices, then sync and merge them to generate the final report. The README also explains that it can automatically calculate tokens and costs for various Agent CLI via ccusage 20.x.

There are four supported backends, switchable via --api:

  • ollama, default
  • claude_cli
  • anthropic
  • openai

research#

This is a unified academic research tool, with the entry point being tools/research/research_scout.py. It mainly includes four types of capabilities:

  • Paper Discovery: Search for papers from arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed and generate research weekly reports, which can also be deployed to Hugo.
  • Deep Paper Insights: Download full texts, let LLM analyze paper writing structures, publication strategies, and reusable knowledge, and combine with OpenReview to analyze review comments.
  • Researcher Profiling: Analyze research trajectories, hierarchical scoring, mentor-student relationships, etc., based on ArXiv + Semantic Scholar.
  • Citation Graph Analysis: Perform forward citation and backward reference analysis, interpreted by LLM for impact.

It also supports switching LLM backends via --api.

benchmark#

This is a cross-platform CPU/GPU floating-point performance testing tool that measures FLOPS performance on different hardware. The README states it supports:

  • NVIDIA CUDA
  • Apple Silicon MPS
  • Intel XPU

It performs warm-up, formal measurement, and statistical analysis, appends results to a CSV, and can generate HTML reports and leaderboards.

website#

This is a Hugo blog site named TzJ’s Net, using the PaperMod theme. Its focus is on:

  • Incremental image / video compression
  • Automatic build and publish
  • Automatic content translation
  • Writing generated content directly to tools/website/content|static
  • tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository for automatic commit + push

translator#

This is a Gradio document translator based on the common translation engine, functioning like a local version of a Google Translate-style webpage:

  • Supports text and file translation
  • Supports .md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images
  • Preserves Markdown structure, such as code blocks, URLs, and Hugo shortcodes
  • Uses local inference by default, without calling cloud APIs
  • Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B or its GGUF variants

2. Detailed Chinese Usage Tutorial#

Step 1: Prepare the Environment#

The minimum environment requirements provided in the README are:

  • Python 3.10+
  • conda activate AI is recommended
  • Node.js 18+ only for optional Companion graphs and DAG publishing capabilities

If you want to use all the tools mentioned in the repository, there are several dependency installation methods provided in the README:

pip install -e .
pip install -e ".[all]"
pip install -e ".[translator]"
pip install -e ".[website]"

The README instructions are:

  • pip install -e .: Install the shared package at the repository root
  • pip install -e ".[all]": Install common package + extra dependencies like summarize / research / benchmark / website
  • pip install -e ".[translator]": Install translator dependencies separately
  • pip install -e ".[website]": Install website-related dependencies, including torch and transformers required for translation

If this is your first time encountering this project, the README also suggests running a read-only self-check first:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

It will perform --help / --info / import checks; it will not use LLM, will not connect to the internet, and will not write files.

Step 2: Configure the Project#

The main configuration points explicitly mentioned in the README are:

1. config.json#

Tool settings are located in config.json at the repository root, which is gitignored. The README suggests:

  • Copy a version from config.example.json as a starting point
  • If you need to change the configuration file location, you can use GADGET_CONFIG

2. tokens/#

This directory stores API keys and onboarding forms; do not commit this to Git.

3. LLM Backend Switching#

The README explains that all LLM-related functions can be switched uniformly through these backends:

  • ollama, default
  • claude_cli
  • anthropic
  • openai

The corresponding global environment variable is GADGET_LLM_BACKEND.

4. Translation Backend Switching#

The README explains that the translation path also has unified local inference backend choices; the environment variable is GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND, with options including:

  • ollama
  • llamacpp
  • vllm
  • transformers

The translation model can also be overridden using GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL.

5. First-time Machine Configuration#

If you are using this repository on a new machine, the README recommends using:

python scripts/onboard.py

It requires filling out tokens/onboard.yaml first, then it will automatically complete:

  • SSH configuration
  • Claude / Codex CLI installation and authentication
  • pip extras installation
  • Configuration for each tool
  • rclone bootstrap

Step 3: Usage by Tool#

Below are the most commonly used commands categorized by tool.

1) Typical usage of summarize#

The new entry point recommended by the README is python -m summarize.

python -m summarize daily export
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy
python -m summarize auto --deploy

These correspond to:

  • daily export: Export all dates that haven’t been exported yet
  • daily merge --sync-all: Sync all dates and merge them by day
  • weekly generate: Generate weekly reports and deploy
  • monthly generate: Generate monthly reports and deploy
  • auto --deploy: One-click execution of export, merge, weekly report, monthly report, and deployment

The README also states that the old entry point is still available, but the new form python -m summarize is recommended.

2) Typical usage of research#

The entry point for the research tool is:

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

Representing:

  • report: Search papers, perform three-stage evaluation, and generate reports
  • ask: Natural language questioning with automatic routing of retrieval sources
  • profile: Generate researcher profiles
  • citations: Perform citation graph analysis; input arXiv ID / DOI is supported
  • deploy: Deploy reports to Hugo

3) Typical usage of benchmark#

The README explicitly states: All benchmark commands must first enter tools/benchmark/.

cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --report
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

Meaning:

  • Run all benchmarks by default, appending results to CSV
  • --cpu-only: Run CPU only
  • --gpu-only: Run GPU only
  • --report: Run tests and generate HTML reports
  • --report --deploy: Generate reports and publish to Hugo’s /benchmark/

4) Typical usage of website#

The website tools mainly have three common commands. The build scripts for Windows and macOS/Linux are different:

pip install -e ".[website]"
cd tools/website && bash update.sh
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1
cd tools/website && hugo server -D

Purposes are:

  • pip install -e ".[website]": Install website-related dependencies
  • bash update.sh：Perform incremental compression, Hugo build, and push on macOS/Linux
  • update.ps1：Execute the same process on Windows
  • hugo server -D：Local preview, including drafts

The README also emphasizes:

  • Automatically generated content will be written into tools/website/content|static
  • tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository
  • Do not manually commit directly to public/

5) Typical usage of translator#

The simplest way to start the translator is:

pip install -e ".[translator]"
python -m translator

It will start the Gradio interface and open it in your browser.

The README also explains several usage points:

  • Supports text, Markdown, PDF, DOCX, and images
  • Preserves Markdown structure
  • Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B
  • Also supports switching via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or model management within the interface
  • Source language can be set to auto
  • When target language is set to auto, it will switch between Chinese and English

Step 4: Understanding Output and Sync#

The README explains that all generated artifacts are concentrated in the outputs/ directory, which includes:

  • logs/
  • reports/
  • cache/
  • data/
  • images/
  • backups/

If you need to sync data across devices, the README provides:

python scripts/sync.py
python scripts/sync.py push/pull

sync.py also covers patterns like status, bootstrap, config, etc., and is used for syncing categories such as summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups.

Step 5: Recommended Order for Your First Use#

If you are encountering this project for the very first time, the most stable path is:1. Set up Python 3.10+, conda activate AI is recommended. 2. First, install the base environment:

pip install -e .
  1. If you want to use most tools, install the extras: 
    pip install -e ".[all]"
  2. If you want to use the translator, install it separately: 
    pip install -e ".[translator]"
  3. Copy and fill in config.example.json, and set GADGET_CONFIG if necessary.
  4. If you have API keys, put them into tokens/.
  5. Run this first: 
    bash scripts/smoke.sh
  6. Then run the corresponding command for the tool you want to use.

If you wish, in my next message I can reorganize this content into a “step-by-step getting started checklist” more suitable for beginners, compressed into the easiest version to follow.

gpt-5.4-nano-high — 9,295 chars · 15/16 facts

1. Project Overview (What it is, repository structure, and what each tool does)#

Gadgets is a “collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development.” It covers the following areas: AI daily/weekly/monthly report generation, paper discovery and research analysis, CPU/GPU performance benchmarking, Hugo blog automation, and document translation.

The core design of the repository root is:

  • Each subdirectory under tools/ is an independent tool that can be used separately;
  • Shared capabilities are centralized in the common/ package in the root directory (installed via pip install -e .), providing common capabilities such as LLM invocation, JSON parsing/repair, disk caching, atomic writes, translation, Hugo deployment, etc., to each tool;
  • Optional Companion/planning tools come from the sibling repository ../ai-companion/ (local tools in this repository will not be “intercepted” by Companion);
  • The AI agent coding workflow follows the AGENTS.md in the root directory.

Repository Structure (Directory division provided in README)#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具产品
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报/周报/月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现 + 研究者分析 + 引文图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客（增量媒体压缩 + 自动构建与发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包（LLM / cache / IO / translation / Hugo）
├── scripts/           # 运维与维护脚本（sync.py, onboard.py 等）
├── docs/              # 设计文档、ECL 计划、审计报告、历史归档等
├── outputs/           # 生成的所有产物（gitignored，可重建）
├── AGENTS.md          # AI agent 工作协议（读后再行动）
├── CLAUDE.md          # 给 Claude Code 的仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml    # packaging 配置：common/ 与各工具（pip install -e .）

What each tool does#

  1. tools/summarize/ — Summarize (AI conversation daily / weekly / monthly reports)
  • Automatically reads AI conversation records exported from different devices (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON), and calls LLMs to generate structured daily/weekly/monthly summaries.
  • The multi-device workflow is: first export the unexported dates from each device, then aggregate/merge them, then generate weekly and monthly reports, which can then be deployed.
  • Uses the per-source command of ccusage 20.x to automatically discover and calculate token usage and costs.
  • The LLM backend can be switched via a unified --api: ollama (default, local Ollama, no key required; Gemma4-26B), claude_cli, anthropic, or openai.
  1. tools/research/ — Research (Paper discovery and researcher analysis)
    Provided by a single CLI entry point tools/research/research_scout.py, offering four types of capabilities:
  • Paper discovery: Performs three-stage LLM pipeline screening and evaluation from arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed, generates research weekly reports, and deploys them to Hugo; supports conference paper search and author search.
  • Deep paper insight（--insight）: Downloads full paper texts, allowing LLMs to analyze writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable core knowledge; automatically matches OpenReview comments and analyzes consensus and divergence; synthesizes cross-paper writing guides.
  • Researcher profiling: Retrieves paper and citation data from ArXiv + Semantic Scholar to perform research trajectory analysis and layered scoring, and discovers mentor-student relationships through homepage extraction and co-authorship patterns (supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup).
  • Citation graph analysis: Performs forward citation/backward reference based on the Semantic Scholar API, with explanations provided by LLMs.
    Similarly supports switching LLM backends via --api: ollama (default) / claude_cli / anthropic / openai.
  1. tools/benchmark/ — Benchmark (CPU/GPU performance benchmark suite)
  • Measures floating-point performance (FLOPS) on different hardware using a unified standard, supporting NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel XPU for actual GPU runs; OpenCL may only appear in --info detection.
  • Precision coverage includes FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (FP8 experimental).
  • Uses warm-up + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR outlier removal), and explicitly uses GPU synchronization to ensure timing accuracy.
  • Results are written to CSV in an append mode (not overwritten), and can generate Plotly interactive HTML reports and leaderboards; can also be deployed to Hugo and submitted to public leaderboards.
  1. tools/website/ — Website (Hugo blog)
  • Deployed to GitHub Pages (the site provided in README: https://tzj2006.github.io/), using the PaperMod theme.
  • Built-in incremental media compression: uses .last_build to compress only changed media; images go through pngquant, and videos go through HandBrakeCLI.
  • Local model bilingual translation: defaults to Ollama (and reuses the chat tag gemma4:26b); uses vLLM for translation under Linux and transformers under Windows; the model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded upon first run (does not use cloud LLM APIs).
  • Automatically generated content (daily/weekly/monthly reports, research reports, benchmark pages, images, etc.) will be written to tools/website/content|static (a single Hugo content root directory), and files will be marked with gadget_generated; handwritten files without marks will not be overwritten.
  • tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), which will be automatically committed and pushed by build scripts; do not commit to it directly.
  1. tools/translator/ — Translate (Gradio document translator)
  • A Gradio local translation web page based on the common translation engine: supports translating text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images, etc.), and attempts to preserve Markdown/structure (protecting fragments like code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc.).
  • Uses local inference (no cloud APIs): the backend is automatically selected via common.engine.create_engine():
    • ollama (prioritizes when the corresponding model tag is pulled, defaults to local Ollama);
    • Windows fallback uses transformers; Linux prefers vLLM;
    • Also provides a low-VRAM GGUF solution llamacpp.
  • Default model: tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant: tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF); automatically downloads upon first use.
  • Can be overridden via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or model management in the GUI; source language supports auto (detected by CJK ratio), and if the target is auto, it switches between zh↔en.

  • You can override the configuration file path using the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.

  • The tokens/ directory stores API keys and the onboarding sheet; this directory is gitignored, and the README explicitly states “never commit its contents.”

    • Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS testing, providing unified evaluation for GPUs from different vendors (NVIDIA CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU).
    • Supports precisions such as FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8.
    • Includes warmup + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR for outlier removal), with results appended to CSV.
    • Can generate Plotly interactive HTML reports and supports deployment to Hugo sites or public leaderboards.

  • tools/website/ – Hugo Blog Site

    • Blog site “TzJ’s Net” (PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages.
    • Built-in incremental media compression (only compresses images/videos changed since .last_build):
      • Images via pngquant
      • Videos via HandBrakeCLI
    • Local bilingual translation (default Ollama; vLLM available on Linux, transformers on Windows), automatically downloads tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B models on first use.
    • All auto-generated content (summary reports, research reports, benchmark pages, images) is written directly to tools/website/content|static with gadget_generated tags, and will not overwrite handwritten content.
    • tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository (automatic commit + push; manual modification is not recommended).

  • tools/translator/ – Gradio Document Translator

    • A Web interface implemented based on the common translation engine, similar to Google Translate.
    • Supports translating text and various file types (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images), preserving Markdown format, code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc.
    • Fully utilizes local inference (default tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, GGUF variant); models are automatically downloaded upon first call.
    • Supports automatic detection of source and target languages for Chinese-English mutual translation; the backend can be selected via GUI or environment variables.

  • common/ – Shared Infrastructure

    • Unified LLM calling interface (ollama / claude_cli / anthropic / openai).
    • JSON repair, disk caching, atomic writes, translation engine, and Hugo deployment encapsulation.

  • scripts/ – Operations & Maintenance Scripts

    • sync.py: Unified rclone data synchronization (push/pull/status/config/backup, including DAG sites).
    • onboard.py: One-click completion after filling in tokens/onboard.yaml: SSH, Claude/Codex CLI, pip extras, tool configurations, and rclone startup.
    • smoke.sh: Smoke tests that do not modify any data (--help / --info / import).
    • serve_local_llm.sh : Creates Ollama models adapted for summarize and outputs environment variable settings.
    • Others such as language.py (Hugo language audit), profile_translation.py (translation GPU profiler).

  • ../ai-companion/ (Independent Repository)

    • Provides DAG publishing tools, idea graph, and skill pipeline, but this repository itself does not enable Companion intercept hooks.

II. Detailed Tutorial (For first-time users)#

Note: All example commands below are taken directly from the README; no new commands or parameters have been added. You can copy and run them directly, but please replace paths, project names, timestamps, etc., according to your own environment.

1. Environment Preparation#

  • Base Environment
    • Python 3.10+ (A separate virtual environment or conda environment is recommended, such as the AI environment, then conda activate AI).
    • Node.js 18+ (Only required when using optional Companion graph / DAG publishing tools).
  • Hardware
    • If you need to use benchmark or high-performance translation, it is recommended to have a corresponding GPU (NVIDIA CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU); the project will detect it automatically.
  • Data & API keys
    • There is a tokens/ directory in the repository root (already gitignored) used for storing sensitive information like API keys and onboard configurations; do not commit it to git.

2. Project Installation & Public Dependencies#

Assuming you have placed the repository code in a local directory, execute the following commands from the repository root.

  • Install base packages + dependencies required for summarize / research / benchmark / website
pip install -e ".[all]"
  • If you want to use the translator tool (Gradio document translation), you also need to install its extras separately:
pip install -e ".[translator]"

Note: pip install -e ".[all]" does not include dependencies related to translator; you must explicitly add the command above.

3. Configuration Files & Environment Variables#

  • Global Configuration Files
    • config.json in the root directory (gitignored) saves configurations for various tools. The README mentions you can copy one from config.example.json and modify it as needed.
    • If you need to use a custom path, you can override the default path via the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.
  • LLM Backend Selection
    • All features using LLM (summarize / research / common) support selecting the backend via the --api parameter:
      • ollama (default, local Ollama, gemma4:26b)
      • claude_cli
      • anthropic
      • openai
    • You can also use the environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND for global default settings.
  • Translation Backend & Models
    • The translation path uses the environment variable GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND to specify the backend:
      • Default is ollama (local service, reuses gemma4:26b tag).
      • When falling back to llamacpp / vllm / transformers, it will use tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, which is automatically downloaded on first use.
    • The default model for the Translator tool is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant), which can be overridden via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or the GUI.

4. One-click Initialization for New Machines (Optional)#

  • Repository-level machine configuration: scripts/onboard.py

    1. Fill in information such as SSH, various tokens, and tools you wish to enable in tokens/onboard.yaml.

    2. Run the following in the repository root:

      python scripts/onboard.py

    3. The script will automatically:

      • Configure SSH
      • Install/login to Claude/Codex CLI
      • Install required pip extras for each tool
      • Configure each tool
      • Start rclone synchronization

  • Server-level installation (within the ai-companion repository)

    • If you are performing a full-site installation (SSH key, Claude Code, Superpowers, Ponytail, AI Companion, etc.) on an Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 server, you need to run this in the sibling repository ../ai-companion/:

      bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help

5. Data Synchronization & Output Directories#

  • Data Synchronization (Multi-device scenarios)
    • The README indicates:

      • The top-level synchronization entry point is:

        python scripts/sync.py
```- More granular cross-device synchronization examples are provided in the form of `python scripts/sync.py push/pull` (choose push or pull based on your scenario).

      • The script uses the sync configuration section of the root directory config.json (the path can be overridden using GADGET_CONFIG).

      • DAG site publishing uses scripts/sync.py --category dag.

  • Output Location
    • All content generated by running the tools is placed under outputs/, with a structure roughly as follows:
      • outputs/logs/: Run logs, export logs
      • outputs/reports/: Final reports (Markdown / JSON / HTML)
      • outputs/cache/: LLM and search cache
      • outputs/data/: Structured data (CSV / JSON)
      • outputs/images/: Charts and generated images
      • outputs/backups/: Backups during forced overrides
    • Hugo site content is written directly to tools/website/content|static.

6. Quick Self-Check Before Running (Optional)#

  • Smoke Test Script: scripts/smoke.sh

    • Confirm that the --help / --info and imports for each tool are correct (without triggering LLM, network, or writes):

      bash scripts/smoke.sh

  • Local LLM Service Helper Script: scripts/serve_local_llm.sh

    • Creates an Ollama tag optimized for summarize, and prints a set of environment variables (applied via eval):

      eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

    • Persistent configuration items are written in the summarize section of the root directory config.json.

III. Typical Usage for Each Tool (Commands Ready to Copy)#

1. Summarize: AI Session Daily / Weekly / Monthly Reports#

Goal: Automatically organize AI conversations scattered across multiple devices and tools into structured daily/weekly/monthly reports, with optional automatic deployment to the Hugo site.

  1. Daily Workflow Overview

    • Export the day’s AI conversation records from each device.
    • Sync the exported data from all devices to the same location (cloud drive or python scripts/sync.py).
    • Run the summarize daily/weekly/monthly commands to generate reports, with an option to --deploy automatically publish to Hugo.

  2. Typical Commands

python -m summarize daily export
  • Meaning: Phase 1, export conversation records for all dates that are “not yet exported.”
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all
  • Meaning: Phase 2, sync all dates and merge them by day to generate daily summaries.
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy
  • Meaning: Generate the weekly report for Week 12 of 2026 and deploy it.
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy
  • Meaning: Generate the monthly report for February 2026 and deploy it.
python -m summarize auto --deploy
  • Meaning: One-click full pipeline: export → merge → weekly → monthly and deploy.

Switching LLM Backends: --api can be added after any of the above commands, such as --api ollama / --api claude_cli / --api anthropic / --api openai.

Legacy Entry Compatibility: python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ... / weekly_summary.py / monthly_summary.py are still available, but the new python -m summarize format is recommended.

2. Research: Paper Discovery and Scientific Figure Analysis#

Unified Entry Script: tools/research/research_scout.py.

  1. Full Paper Search + Weekly Report Generation
python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project
  • Meaning: Using my-project as the project name, execute:
    • Multi-source paper search (arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed)
    • Three-stage LLM evaluation
    • Generate research weekly reports and deploy to Hugo (based on internal tool configuration).
  1. Natural Language Retrieval
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"
  • Meaning: Use natural language queries to automatically route to appropriate data sources for paper searching.
  1. Researcher Profiling
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"
  • Meaning: Based on ArXiv + Semantic Scholar, construct a research trajectory analysis and tier rating for “Sergey Levine.”
  1. Citation Graph Analysis
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597
  • Meaning: Construct a citation/cited-by graph using an arXiv ID (or DOI) and use LLM to interpret the impact.
  1. Deploy Reports to Hugo
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy
  • Meaning: Deploy the generated research reports to the Hugo site.

Similarly, all commands involving LLM can add --api to switch backends, for example, appending --api claude_cli after the report command.

3. Benchmark: CPU/GPU Performance Benchmarking#

Important: The README explicitly requires that all benchmark commands must first cd tools/benchmark.

  1. Enter Tool Directory
cd tools/benchmark
  1. Run All Benchmarks (Results appended to CSV)
python -m benchmark.cli
  1. Run CPU Benchmarks Only
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only
  1. Run GPU Benchmarks Only
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only
  1. Run Benchmarks and Generate HTML Report
python -m benchmark.cli --report
  1. Generate Report and Deploy to Hugo
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

4. Website: Hugo Blog Automated Construction and Publishing#

  1. Install website-related dependencies
pip install -e ".[website]"
  1. macOS / Linux: Media Compression + Hugo Build + Push to GitHub Pages
cd tools/website && bash update.sh
  1. Windows: Media Compression + Build + Push
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1
  • The script will automatically switch to its own directory internally before execution.
  1. Local Site Preview (Development mode, including drafts)
cd tools/website && hugo server -D
  • This allows you to open the Hugo dev server on your local machine to preview blog content in real-time.

Note:

  • Automatically generated content is written to tools/website/content|static and marked with gadget_generated; manually written content will not be overwritten.
  • tools/website/public/ is an independent Git repository used for deployment; the build script will automatically commit + push.

5. Translator: Gradio Document Translation Web App#

  1. Install translator dependencies
pip install -e ".[translator]"
  1. Start Gradio GUI
python -m translator
  • After starting, a browser page will open where you can:
    • Input or paste text
    • Upload .md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images, etc.
    • Select source language (can be set to auto) and target language (can be set to auto to achieve Chinese-English mutual translation)
    • Select or switch models (default is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, automatically downloaded on first use)

This tool uses common.engine.create_engine() to select the backend: prioritizing ollama, preferring vllm on Linux, using transformers on Windows, and using llamacpp GGUF for low VRAM scenarios.

IV. Typical Usage of Scripts and Helper Tools#

1. Data Synchronization Script scripts/sync.py#

  • Basic Call:
python scripts/sync.py
  • Purpose (according to README description):
    • Centralized management of rclone data synchronization (push / pull / status / bootstrap / config).
    • Covers categories such as summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups, etc.
    • The special dag category is used via scripts/sync.py --category dag to generate + deploy DAG sites.
    • Also used for cross-device synchronization (explained in the README in the form of python scripts/sync.py push/pull).

2. One-click Onboarding (Re-emphasized)#

  • Repository-level:
python scripts/onboard.py
  • Run once after filling out tokens/onboard.yaml.

3. Smoke Test and Local LLM Service#

  • Smoke Test:
bash scripts/smoke.sh
  • Local LLM Environment Variable Output:
eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

The above is an overview and tutorial organized entirely based on the README, without adding any commands or parameters outside of the README. If you later wish to create more in-depth Chinese steps for a specific tool (for example, using only summarize or only benchmark), I can help you break it down into a more detailed operation checklist following that tool’s README / TUTORIAL structure.

Based on the README.md content of the open-source project gadget you provided, I have organized a project summary and a detailed Chinese usage tutorial for beginners.

Part 1: Open Source Project gadget Summary#

1. Project Introduction#

Gadgets is a collection of practical tools accumulated during daily development. It covers scenarios such as AI daily report generation, academic paper discovery and analysis, hardware performance benchmarking, Hugo blog automated building and publishing, and local document translation. The core philosophy of the project is high modularity, where each tool can be used independently while sharing the underlying infrastructure located in the root directory.

2. Repository Structure#

The project directory structure is clearly divided, mainly containing the following parts:

  • tools/ (Tool Product Directory): Contains five completely independent sub-toolkits, serving as the location for specific tool logic.
  • common/ (Shared Infrastructure): General underlying code providing cross-tool basic capabilities such as LLM invocation, JSON parsing and repair, SHA-256 disk caching, atomic writing, translation engines, and Hugo deployment.
  • scripts/ (Ops & Maintenance Scripts): Contains scripts for machine setup, multi-device synchronization, smoke testing, and local LLM startup.
  • docs/ (Documentation): Stores design documents, ECL plans, audit reports, and historical archives.
  • outputs/ (Output Directory): A unified location for all generated artifacts (such as logs, reports, caches, data, charts, backups, etc.). This directory is ignored by Git and can be automatically rebuilt.
  • Protocol/Guide Files:
    • AGENTS.md: AI Agent workflow protocol (must read before modifying code).
    • CLAUDE.md: Repository guide specifically for Claude Code.
    • pyproject.toml: Bundled configuration files used for installing common packages and various tool dependencies.

3. Functional Overview of Each Tool#

  • summarize (AI Conversation Reports): Reads AI conversation logs from multiple devices (such as Claude Code / Cursor, etc.), calls LLMs to automatically generate structured daily, weekly, and monthly reports, and uses ccusage to automatically calculate Token consumption and costs for each Agent CLI.
  • research (Academic Research Toolkit): Integrates multiple data sources like arXiv and Semantic Scholar, providing automatic paper discovery with three-stage LLM filtering, deep paper insights (structural analysis, OpenReview evaluation synthesis), researcher trajectory profiling, and citation graph analysis.
  • benchmark (Performance Benchmarking): A cross-platform CPU/GPU floating-point performance measurement tool. It uniformly supports multi-precision testing (FP64 to FP8) for CUDA, Apple MPS, and Intel XPU. Results are written in append mode to CSV and can generate Plotly interactive chart leaderboards.
  • website (Hugo Blog): A static blog website based on Hugo. It features built-in incremental media compression (pngquant, HandBrakeCLI) and a bilingual translation pipeline using local models (Hy-MT2-1.8B) without needing an internet connection, achieving fully automated building and publishing.
  • translator (Gradio Document Translator): A local Web-based translation interface built on the common translation engine. It supports translating text while preserving Markdown formatting and various document types (.pdf, .docx, etc.), and can automatically identify languages based on CJK ratios for Chinese-English mutual translation.

Part 2: gadget Detailed Chinese Usage Tutorial#

This tutorial is intended for users encountering the project for the first time, guiding you through the entire process from environment preparation, installation, and configuration to the actual running of each tool.

1. Environment Preparation#

3. Initialization and Machine Configuration#

3.1 One-click Onboarding Script#

For the first environment configuration on a new machine, the project provides an onboarding script. It automatically configures SSH, installs and authenticates Claude/Codex CLI, installs dependency packages, and configures rclone:

  1. Copy and fill in tokens/onboard.yaml (this directory is ignored by Git for safe storage of sensitive Tokens).
  2. Run the onboarding script in the project root directory:

3.2 Configuration Files#

  • Please copy config.example.json and rename it to config.json for modification.

The project supports flexible switching of underlying engines via environment variables and command-line parameters:

5.3 Benchmark — Performance Benchmarking#

5.4 Website — Hugo Blog Automated Build#

  • Update, compress media, and publish on macOS / Linux systems

6. Common Operations and Auxiliary Commands#

    • Others: AGENTS.md (proxy workflows), pyproject.toml (packaging configuration)

  • What each tool does (Summary)

    • summarize: Reads AI session logs from multiple devices (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON), uses LLMs to generate structured daily/weekly/monthly summaries, and can track token/cost (via ccusage 20.x); supports multiple LLM backends (--api).
    • research: A unified academic research tool featuring paper discovery (arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed), three-stage LLM review, deep insight downloading and analysis, researcher profiling (ArXiv + Semantic Scholar), citation graph analysis, and the ability to deploy reports to Hugo.
    • benchmark: Cross-platform FLOPS benchmark supporting NVIDIA CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU, covering various precisions (FP64/FP32/FP16/BF16/FP8 (experimental)), measuring including warmup and statistical analysis, appending results to CSV, generating interactive HTML reports, and deploying to Hugo.
    • website: A Hugo-based static blog pipeline with built-in incremental media compression (pngquant, HandBrakeCLI) and local model bilingual translation (defaulting to Ollama / local model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B automatic download), automatically writing generated content to tools/website/content|static and building/pushing to Pages via scripts (tools/website/public/ is a separate deployment repository and should not be manually committed).
    • translator: A document translator with Gradio Web UI, supporting .md/.txt/.pdf/.docx/图片, etc., protecting code blocks/URLs/Hugo shortcodes, using the local inference translation engine from common (automatically selecting ollama / vllm / transformers / llamacpp), with default model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (automatically downloaded on first run).

  • Shared Base and Script Key Points

    • common/ implements unified LLM backend access (ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, openai), disk cache, translation engine, Hugo deployment, etc.
    • scripts/ includes data synchronization (sync.py, based on rclone), machine onboarding (onboard.py), local LLM startup scripts, read-only smoke test scripts, etc.
    • Outputs are uniformly written to outputs/ (logs/reports/cache/data/images/backups).- Key points to note (Reminders in README)
    • Python 3.10+, Node.js 18+ (only required when using Companion/DAG tools)
    • tokens/ stores API keys and onboarding forms; it is gitignored; do not commit
    • All generated files are under outputs/ and are gitignored
    • LLM backend is switched globally via the --api parameter, or via the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable
    • Translation backend is controlled via GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND, and models via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL
    • Do not commit auto-generated content, rclone sync data, build/, gadget.egg-info/, or deployment theme repository content to git
    • License: GPL-3
  1. Detailed Chinese Usage Tutorial (For first-timers, covering environment preparation, installation, configuration, and typical usage of each tool; commands can be copied directly; all sourced solely from README)

Prerequisites: The following steps and commands are based strictly on the instructions and descriptions listed in the README, without adding extra parameters or commands not appearing in the README.

A. Environment Preparation (Minimum Requirements)

  • Python: 3.10+

    • conda environment (README suggests): Create and activate first (README only suggests activate):
      • conda create -n AI python=3.10
      • conda activate AI (Note: README recommends using conda activate AI, but does not provide the specific creation command; the above is just a common practice)
  • Node.js: 18+ (only when Companion / DAG functionality is required)

  • In the repository root, install the common editable package (minimal):
pip install -e .

(Note: all does not include translator; translator must be installed separately, see below)

C. Configuration (Must Read)

  • The config.example.json at the repository root is an example; tools actually read config.json (repo root), and this file is gitignored. README suggests: Copy the example to config.json and modify as needed.

cp config.example.json config.json
# Windows PowerShell 可用复制命令：Copy-Item config.example.json config.json
  • The tokens/ directory saves API keys and onboarding forms (tokens/onboard.yaml); this directory is gitignored. Do not commit its contents.
  • Available environment variables (mentioned in README):
    • GADGET_CONFIG —— Overrides the configuration file path (tools read the repo-root config.json; set this variable if an override is needed)
    • GADGET_LLM_BACKEND —— Globally switches the LLM backend (equivalent to command line --api)
    • GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND / GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL —— Controls the translation backend and model (used for translator / website translation)

D. General Operations Scripts

  • Data synchronization (rclone required):
python scripts/sync.py
# cross-device push/pull（README 指出可用 push/pull，例如）
python scripts/sync.py push
python scripts/sync.py pull
  • One-time machine configuration (onboarding):
python scripts/onboard.py

(README: Fill in tokens/onboard.yaml and run the script once to complete configuration)

  • Read-only smoke check (no LLM/network/write operations):
bash scripts/smoke.sh
  • Local LLM service (generates an Ollama variant optimized for summarize and prints env), README provides:
eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

(This command is used in Unix-like/bash environments; README contains this example)

E. outputs/ Directory Description (Where to find and what it’s for)

  • All generated artifacts are written to outputs/ under the repository root:
    • outputs/logs/ — Intermediate products (export logs, runtime logs)
    • outputs/reports/ — Final reports (Markdown, JSON, HTML)
    • outputs/cache/ — LLM / Search cache
    • outputs/data/ — Structured data (CSV/JSON)
    • outputs/images/ — Charts and generated images
    • outputs/backups/ — Forced overwrite backups
  • Note: Hugo content is written directly to tools/website/content|static (not outputs/site)

F. Typical Usage of Each Tool (Commands that can be copied and run directly; all from README)

  1. Summarize (AI session daily/weekly/monthly summaries)
  • Recommended entry point (new format, README recommends using python -m summarize):
python -m summarize daily export
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy
python -m summarize auto --deploy
  • Key points (all from README):
    • Phase 1: daily export exports unexported dates
    • Phase 2: daily merge merge (--sync-all can sync all dates)
    • weekly generate and monthly generate support separate generation and can be published via --deploy
    • auto --deploy is the “one-click” full pipeline: export → merge → weekly → monthly + deploy
    • LLM backend is switched via --api (ollama is default; also claude_cli / anthropic / openai)
    • README notes that the old entry point is still available (backward compatible): python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ... (but -m summarize is recommended)
  1. Research (Paper discovery and researcher analysis)
  • Unified CLI (README specifies script path and example commands):
python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy
  • Key points:
    • report: Full pipeline (search → three-stage evaluation → report generation)
    • ask: Natural language search (automatically routes to appropriate sources)
    • profile: Researcher profiling
    • citations: Citation graph (can use arXiv ID / DOI)
    • LLM backend is switched via --api (same as summarize)
  1. Benchmark (Performance benchmarks)
  • First switch to the benchmark directory (explicitly required by README):
cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --report
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy
  • Key points:
    • python -m benchmark.cli runs all benchmarks (results appended to CSV)
    • --cpu-only / --gpu-only restrict the execution range respectively
    • --report generates HTML reports (can be added to --deploy for Hugo publication)
    • README mentions automatic detection of CUDA / MPS / Intel XPU, etc. (no extra commands)
  1. Website (Hugo blog)
  • Install website-related dependencies:
pip install -e ".[website]"
  • Execute update and build on macOS / Linux (provided by README):
cd tools/website && bash update.sh
  • Execute PowerShell script on Windows (noted by README):
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1
  • Local preview (Hugo dev server):
cd tools/website && hugo server -D
  • Key points:
    • update.sh implements incremental compression (only processes media changed since .last_build), builds, and pushes tools/website/public/ (this is a separate deployment repo)
    • tools/website/public/ should not be committed manually; the script will automatically commit + push
    • Local translation and model: Defaults to Ollama; the local model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B will be automatically downloaded on the first run (as explained in README)
  1. Translator (Gradio document translation)
  • Install translator dependencies (separate installation):

  • Start Gradio GUI:

  • Key points (README):

    • Default model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF), automatically downloaded on first run
    • Supports file types .md/.txt/.pdf/.docx/图片 and protects code blocks / URLs / Hugo shortcodes
    • Default model can be overridden via the GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL environment variable (README mentions the variable name but does not provide example syntax)

  • Global LLM backend switch: command line --api or environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND (optional values: ollama (default) / claude_cli / anthropic / openai))

I. Project Summary#

What is this#

Gadget is a collection of daily tools for an individual developer, written in Python. The author has accumulated practical tools used repeatedly in daily development into a single repository, covering five major scenarios: AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly report generation, academic paper discovery and analysis, hardware performance benchmarking, Hugo blog automation, and document translation.

Core design philosophy:

  • Each directory under tools/ is an independent tool that can be used separately;
  • All tools share the common/ infrastructure package in the root directory (LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation engine, Hugo deployment), installed via pip install -e .;
  • LLM backends are unified and switched via the --api parameter, with four choices: ollama (default, local, no key required), claude_cli (reuses Claude Code login state), anthropic, and openai;
  • All outputs are unified into outputs/ (gitignored), and configurations are unified in the root directory config.json.

Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报/周报/月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现 + 研究者分析 + 引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客（增量压缩 + 自动构建发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包（LLM/缓存/IO/翻译/Hugo）
├── scripts/            # 运维脚本（sync.py、onboard.py 等）
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划、审计报告
├── outputs/            # 所有生成产物（gitignored）
├── AGENTS.md           # AI agent 工作协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # common/ + 各工具的打包配置

What each tool does#

Tool Function
summarize Reads AI conversation logs from Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / ChatGPT, etc., and calls LLMs to generate structured daily, weekly, and monthly reports. Multi-device two-stage architecture: export from each device → sync and aggregate via cloud drive → merge and generate. Uses ccusage 20.x to statistics token usage and costs for various agent CLIs
research A unified academic research tool. A single entry point research_scout.py provides four capabilities: ① Paper discovery (arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed, three-stage LLM pipeline: rapid screening → deep evaluation → citation impact); ② Deep paper insights (--insight, full-text download + writing structure analysis + OpenReview comment matching); ③ Researcher profiling (paper/citation data + research trajectory analysis + teacher-student relationship discovery); ④ Citation graph analysis (Semantic Scholar API)
benchmark Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarking, supporting NVIDIA CUDA, Apple MPS, and Intel XPU, covering FP64/FP32/FP16/BF16/FP8 (experimental) precision. Statistical method: warmup + formal measurement + median/IQR outlier removal + explicit GPU synchronization. Results are appended to CSV, and Plotly interactive HTML reports and leaderboards can be generated
website Hugo static blog (“TzJ’s Net”, PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages. Built-in incremental media compression (pngquant for images, HandBrakeCLI for video, only processing files changed after .last_build) and local model bilingual translation. Each tool’s deployment pipeline writes directly to `tools/website/content
translator A Gradio-based document translation web app, providing a Google Translate-like experience. Supports text and .md/.txt/.pdf/.docx/images, while protecting Markdown formatting (code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes). Pure local inference, default model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, with the model residing in memory

II. Beginner’s Tutorial#

1. Environment Preparation#

Required basic environment (from the “Environment Requirements” section of the README):

  • Python 3.10+, recommended to use conda environment AI:
conda activate AI
  • Node.js 18+ (only required if you want to use the optional Companion graph / DAG publishing tools)
  • rclone (only if cross-device data synchronization is needed)
  • Specific dependencies for each tool can be found in their respective requirements.txt directories

2. Installation#

After cloning the repository, execute in the root directory:

# 安装 common 包 + summarize / research / benchmark / website 全部 extras
pip install -e ".[all]"

Note: all does not include translator; the translator must be installed separately:

pip install -e ".[translator]"

If you only use a single tool, you can install just the corresponding extra, for example, only website:

pip install -e ".[website]"

After installation, you can use a read-only smoke test to verify each tool’s availability (no LLM calls, no internet access, no file writing):

bash scripts/smoke.sh

3. Configuration#

  • Configuration Files: Copy the template to generate root directory configurations (gitignored):
cp config.example.json config.json

You can use the GADGET_CONFIG environment variable to specify other paths.

  • API Keys: Place them in the tokens/ directory (gitignored, never commit).
  • One-click Initialization for New Machines: Fill out one form in tokens/onboard.yaml, then run once:
python scripts/onboard.py

It will automatically complete SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras installation, tool configurations, and rclone guidance.

  • LLM Backend Selection: All tools use --api to switch LLM functions: ollama (default, local Ollama, no key required, Gemma4-26B), claude_cli (no API key required), anthropic, and openai; you can also use the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable for global specification.

4. Typical Usage for Each Tool#

4.1 Summarize — AI Conversation Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

python -m summarize daily export                                   # 阶段 1：导出所有未导出的日期
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all                         # 阶段 2：同步所有日期并逐日合并
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy       # 周报 + 部署
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy      # 月报 + 部署
python -m summarize auto --deploy                                  # 一键全流程：导出 → 合并 → 周报 → 月报 + 部署

Old entry points like python tools/summarize/daily_summary.py ... are still available (backward compatible), but the python -m summarize format above is recommended.

Optional: Start a local Ollama variant optimized for summarize:

eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"

4.2 Research — Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis#

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project        # 完整流水线：搜索 → 三阶段评估 → 报告
python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"  # 自然语言搜索（自动路由来源）
python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"             # 研究者画像
python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597               # 引用图谱（支持 arXiv ID / DOI）
python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy                              # 部署报告到 Hugo

All LLM functions can use --api to switch backends (ollama / claude_cli / anthropic / openai).

4.3 Benchmark — Performance Benchmarking#

Note: All commands must first be cd to tools/benchmark/:

cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli                # 跑全部基准测试（结果追加到 CSV）
python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only     # 只测 CPU
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only     # 只测 GPU
python -m benchmark.cli --report       # 测试 + 生成 HTML 报告
python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy  # 生成报告 + 发布到 Hugo /benchmark/

GPU will automatically detect CUDA / Apple MPS / Intel XPU.

4.4 Website — Hugo Blog#

pip install -e ".[website]"                          # 安装依赖（含翻译用的 torch + transformers）
cd tools/website && bash update.sh                   # macOS/Linux：增量压缩 + Hugo 构建 + 推送 Pages
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1  # Windows（脚本会自己 cd）
cd tools/website && hugo server -D                   # 本地预览（开发服务器，含草稿）

The translation model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B will be automatically downloaded upon the first run. tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository, which is automatically committed and pushed by build scripts; do not commit to it manually.

4.5 Translator — Document Translator#

pip install -e ".[translator]"   # 安装依赖（gradio + GGUF 翻译栈）
python -m translator             # 启动 Gradio 界面（自动在浏览器打开）
  • Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B, downloaded automatically on first use; you can switch via the GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL environment variable or within the GUI.
  • Source language can be set to auto (detected by CJK ratio), and when the target language is auto, it will automatically flip between Chinese and English.
  • Translation backend is specified by GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND: ollama (default) → llamacpp/vllm/transformers.

5. Data Synchronization and Output Locations#

Cross-device data synchronization (requires rclone configuration, configured in the sync section of the root directory config.json):

python scripts/sync.py            # 查看用法
python scripts/sync.py push       # 推送
python scripts/sync.py pull       # 拉取

All generated items (logs, reports, cache, structured data, charts, backups) are under outputs/, all of which are gitignored and can be automatically rebuilt if deleted.

6. Common Precautions#

  • Never git add auto-generated content, rclone synchronized data, build artifacts (build/, gadget.egg-info/), or the deployment/theme repositories under tools/website/.
  • The tokens/ directory stores keys; never commit them.
  • License: GPL-3.

For more detailed step-by-step operations, data formats, and FAQs, the README points to TUTORIAL.md as well as the source documentation in each tool’s directory (such as tools/summarize/tutorial.md, tools/research/TUTORIAL.md, etc.). This tutorial only covers content appearing in the README.

I. Project Summary#

1. What is it#

Gadgets is a collection of practical tools accumulated by a developer during daily work, covering five major scenarios:

  • AI conversation daily/weekly/monthly report generation (Summarize)
  • Paper discovery and researcher analysis (Research)
  • CPU/GPU performance benchmarking (Benchmark)
  • Hugo blog automation (Website)
  • Document translation (Translator)

There are several key design features:- Each subdirectory under tools/ is a standalone tool

  • common/ is the shared infrastructure package for all tools (LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation, Hugo deployment), installed via pip install -e .
  • All LLM functions are unified through the --api parameter to switch between four backends: ollama (default, local without key), claude_cli (reuses Claude Code CLI login state), anthropic, openai
  • All generated outputs are unified to outputs/ (already gitignored)
  • Configurations are unified in config.json at the repository root (gitignored, copied from config.example.json), with paths that can be overridden using GADGET_CONFIG
  • License: GPL-3

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立工具产品（改工具就改这里）
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日/周/月报
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现 + 研究者分析 + 引用图
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客（增量媒体压缩 + 自动构建发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包（LLM/缓存/IO/翻译/Hugo）
├── scripts/            # 运维与维护脚本（sync.py, onboard.py 等）
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL 计划、审计报告、历史归档
├── outputs/            # 所有生成产物（gitignored）
├── AGENTS.md           # AI agent 工作流协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # common + 各工具的打包配置

Sub-classifications within the output directory outputs/:

outputs/
├── logs/      # 中间日志
├── reports/   # 最终报告（Markdown/JSON/HTML）
├── cache/     # LLM 缓存、搜索缓存
├── data/      # 结构化数据（CSV、JSON profile）
├── images/    # 图表与生成图片
└── backups/   # 强制覆盖备份

Note: Hugo site content is written directly to tools/website/content|static; no outputs/site staging directory exists.

3. What Each Tool Does#

Summarize — AI Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

Automatically reads daily AI conversation logs (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor Agent / ChatGPT / general JSON) and calls LLMs to generate structured daily/weekly/monthly summaries.

  • Multi-device Two-stage Architecture: Export conversation logs from various devices → aggregate via cloud drive sync or manual copy → generate daily reports → accumulate to generate weekly reports and monthly trends
  • Automatically discovers and statistics token usage and costs for each agent CLI via the namespace-by-source command in ccusage 20.x (ccusage claude, ccusage codex, ccusage gemini…)
  • Four LLM backends are switched via --api: ollama (default, local Gemma4-26B), claude_cli, anthropic, openai

Research — Paper Discovery and Researcher Analysis#

Provides four major capabilities through a single CLI entry point tools/research/research_scout.py:

  • Paper Discovery: Searches arXiv / bioRxiv / PubMed, generates research weekly reports deployed to Hugo via a three-stage LLM pipeline (fast screening → deep evaluation → citation impact); supports conference paper and author searches
  • Deep Paper Insights (--insight): Downloads full papers, lets LLMs analyze writing structure, publication strategies, and reusable core knowledge; automatically matches OpenReview to obtain reviews and analyze consensus vs. controversy; synthesizes cross-paper scientific writing guides
  • Researcher Profiling: Scrapes paper and citation data from arXiv + Semantic Scholar, uses LLM to generate research trajectory analysis, calculates tier scores, and automatically discovers mentor–student relationships via homepage extraction + co-authorship patterns; supports name disambiguation and reverse lookup
  • Citation Graph Analysis: Forward citation / backward reference analysis based on Semantic Scholar API, paired with LLM-driven impact interpretation

Benchmark — Performance Benchmark Suite#

A cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS benchmarking tool that uniformly measures floating-point performance across different hardware vendors and precision levels.

  • Supports real runs on NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU) (OpenCL only appears in --info detection)
  • Precision coverage: FP64 / FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 (experimental)
  • Measurement process: Warmup + formal measurement + statistical analysis (median, IQR outlier removal) + explicit GPU synchronization
  • Results are accumulated in CSV in append mode (never overwritten, naturally supporting multi-hardware cumulative leaderboards)
  • Can generate Plotly interactive HTML reports and leaderboards, supporting deployment to Hugo sites / submission to public leaderboards

Website — Hugo Blog#

A Hugo static blog site (“TzJ’s Net”, PaperMod theme), deployed to GitHub Pages (https://tzj2006.github.io/).

  • Built-in incremental image/video compression pipeline (only compresses media changed since .last_build; images use pngquant, videos use HandBrakeCLI)
  • Local model bilingual translation (default Ollama; uses vLLM for Linux / transformers as fallback for Windows; model tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is automatically downloaded on first run, no cloud LLM API used)
  • Automatically generated content (daily/weekly/monthly reports, research reports, benchmark pages, images) is written directly by the deployment pipeline to tools/website/content|static (single Hugo content root, files marked with gadget_generated; unmarked handwritten files are never overwritten)
  • tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository (tzj2006/tzj2006.github.io), automatically committed and pushed by build scripts; do not commit it directly

Translator — Gradio Document Translator#

A Gradio document translator built on the common translation engine: a Google-Translate style local translation web interface.

  • Translates text and files (.md / .txt / .pdf / .docx / images), preserving Markdown format (code blocks, URLs, Hugo shortcodes, etc., are protected)
  • Local inference without cloud APIs: reuses common.engine.create_engine() to automatically select backends (ollama preferred; transformers as Windows fallback; vllm as Linux preference; llamacpp as low-VRAM GGUF option)
  • Models stay in memory (warm), with on-demand lazy loading when switching models
  • Default model is tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B (GGUF variant tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF), automatically downloaded on first use; can be overridden via GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL or the GUI’s model management
  • Source language can be set to auto (detected by CJK ratio); when target is auto, it flips between zh↔en

common/ — Shared Infrastructure Package#

The shared layer that all tools depend on, installed as a Python package via pip install -e .:

  • LLM calls (unified two-layer API, supporting four backends: ollama (default) / claude_cli / anthropic / openai)
  • JSON parsing and repair
  • SHA-256 disk caching (namespace + TTL)
  • Atomic writes and content hashing
  • Local inference translation engine (Ollama / vLLM / transformers / GGUF) and bilingual content generation
  • Cross-platform Hugo deployment

scripts/ — Operations and Maintenance Scripts#

  • sync.py — Centralized rclone data synchronization (push / pull / status / bootstrap / config, covering summarize / website / research / benchmark / backups categories; also includes a special dag category for generating + deploying DAG sites). Configuration is in the sync section of the repository root’s config.json
  • onboard.py — Repository-level one-time machine configuration: fill out a tokens/onboard.yaml, run the script once, and it automatically completes SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, pip extras installation, tool configurations, and rclone bootstrap
  • smoke.sh — A read-only smoke test spanning all tools (--help / --info / imports; no LLM calls, no internet, no file writing)
  • serve_local_llm.sh — Creates an Ollama variant optimized for summarize and prints env (eval "$(bash scripts/serve_local_llm.sh env)"); persistence knobs are in the summarize section of config.json
  • Others: language.py (Hugo bilingual audit + summarize report renaming), profile_translation.py (translation engine GPU profiler)

AI Companion — Optional Tool#

The sibling repository ../ai-companion/ provides DAG publishing tools, used by scripts/sync.py --category dag. This repository does not have Companion interception hooks; onboarding will not install Companion. Old install.ai_companion settings are ignored.

Tool configurations are unified in config.json at the repository root (already gitignored). Copy from example files:

To specify other paths, set environment variables:

# Windows PowerShell
$env:GADGET_CONFIG = "C:\path\to\your\config.json"

Globally specify the backend via the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable. Optional values: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai.

export GADGET_LLM_BACKEND=ollama

1.5 Global Translation Backend Configuration (Optional)#

Specified via GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND, default is ollama, options include llamacpp / vllm / transformers.

1. Project Summary#

Gadgets is a practical toolkit accumulated through daily development, designed to automate repetitive tasks in development, research, and content publishing using AI capabilities. It not only contains multiple independent tools but also builds a complete automated workflow through a core shared package (common).

Repository Structure#

  • tools/: Core tools directory, containing five independent tool products. Each tool can run independently.
  • common/: Shared infrastructure package. Provides unified underlying capabilities for all tools, such as LLM calls, JSON parsing, disk caching, atomic writes, translation engines, and Hugo deployment functionality.
  • scripts/: Operations and maintenance scripts used for data synchronization, new machine initialization configuration, etc.

Repository Structure#

    cd tools/website && hugo server -D

4. Other Common Operations#

  • Data Synchronization: If you operate on multiple devices, you can use the sync scripts: 
    python scripts/sync.py push
# or
python scripts/sync.py pull
  • Switch Model Backend: All tools supporting LLM (Summarize, Research) can switch backends via the --api parameter: ollama (default), claude_cli, anthropic, openai.

  • Configuration Files: Core project configuration is located in config.json in the root directory (please copy config.example.json for first-time use).
