1. Project Summary: What is Gadget?Gadget is an open-source developer toolkit repository designed to solve daily development pain points through automated scripts and integrated workflows. It is more than just a codebase; it is a complete ecosystem covering AI report generation, academic research assistance, performance benchmarking, blog automation/O&M, and document translation.#

The project adopts a “shared infrastructure + independent tools” architectural design, where all tools rely on the common package in the root directory to handle common tasks such as LLM calls, caching, and atomic writes.

Repository Structure Overview#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 核心工具目录（每个子目录是一个独立应用）
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报/周报/月报生成器
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析、引用图谱工具
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 跨平台性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # 基于 Hugo 的个人博客站点（含自动压缩与部署）
│   └── translator/     # 基于 Gradio 的本地文档翻译 Web 应用
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包（LLM API、缓存、翻译引擎、Hugo 部署）
├── scripts/            # 运维脚本（数据同步、新机器初始化、冒烟测试）
├── docs/               # 设计文档、计划、审计报告
├── outputs/            # 所有生成产物的存放地（已 gitignore，可重建）
├── AGENTS.md           # AI 代理工作协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 指引
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 打包配置（支持 pip install -e .）

Note: Development workflows and Skills are located in a separate sibling repository ../ai-companion/.

Detailed Tool Functions#

Tool Name Core Function Key Features
Summarize AI Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports Automatically reads conversation logs from Claude Code/Codex/ChatGPT, etc., and uses LLMs to generate structured reports. Supports multi-device data aggregation and automatic statistics for Token usage and costs.
Research Research Assistant 1. Paper Discovery: Retrieves papers from sources like arXiv/PubMed and generates weekly reports via a three-stage LLM evaluation.
2. Deep Insights: Analyzes paper writing structures and publication strategies, matching OpenReview comments.
3. Researcher Profiling: Analyzes scholar trajectories, calculates scores, and discovers mentor-student relationships.
4. Citation Mapping: Performs forward/backward citation analysis based on Semantic Scholar.
Benchmark Performance Benchmarking Measures CPU/GPU floating-point performance across platforms (CUDA/MPS/XPU). Supports multiple precisions from FP64 to FP8. Results are accumulated in CSV files, supporting the generation of Plotly interactive HTML reports and deployment to blogs.
Website Hugo Blog Automation Personal blog site. Core features include incremental media compression (only compressing newly changed images/videos) and bilingual translation. Automatically writes reports and charts generated by the above tools into the blog and deploys them to GitHub Pages.
Translator Local Document Translation A Gradio-based Web interface. Supports formats such as .md/.pdf/.docx/images, etc. Uses local models (Ollama/Transformers, etc.) to protect Markdown formatting (code blocks and URLs are not translated).
Common Shared Base Library Provides a unified LLM interface (supporting Ollama/Claude CLI/Anthropic/OpenAI), SHA-256 disk caching, atomic writes, local translation engines, etc.

2. Detailed Gadget Usage Tutorial#

This tutorial is intended for developers using Gadget for the first time. We will proceed in the order of Environment Preparation -> Installation & Configuration -> Tool Usage.

Phase 1: Environment Preparation and Installation#

1.1 Environment Requirements#

  • Python: 3.10+ (Recommended in a Conda environment named AI)
  • Node.js: 18+ (Only required if using features from the ai-companion repository)
  • Dependency Tools:
    • rclone: Used for data synchronization (optional, mandatory for multi-device users)
    • Hugo: Static site generator (for the Website tool)
    • pngquant & HandBrakeCLI: Used for media compression (for the Website tool, optional but recommended)
    • Ollama: Local LLM runtime environment (recommended, used for default LLM backend and translation)

1.2 Clone the Repository#

# 克隆主仓库
git clone git@github.com:TzJ2006/gadget.git
cd gadget

# 克隆 AI 伴侣仓库（同级目录，用于开发工作流和技能）
git clone git@github.com:TzJ2006/ai-companion.git ../ai-companion

1.3 Install Python Dependencies#

Gadget uses pyproject.toml to manage dependencies.

Option A: Install all core tool dependencies except Translator (Recommended for most users)

# 激活 Python 环境
conda activate AI  # 或者你的虚拟环境

# 安装 common 包及 summarize, research, benchmark, website 的依赖
pip install -e ".[all]"

Option B: If document translation functionality is required [all] does not include translator because its dependencies are large (involving the GPU inference stack).

# 单独安装 Translator 依赖
pip install -e ".[translator]"

Note: translator dependencies include the gradio, gguf translation stack, etc.

1.4 Configure Configuration Files#

Tool configurations are located in config.json in the repository root (this file is gitignored and must be created manually).

  1. Copy the example configuration: 
    cp config.example.json config.json
  2. Edit config.json to fill in necessary API keys (if using Claude/Anthropic/OpenAI backends) or adjust other settings.
    • LLM 后端切换: Globally controlled via the --api parameter or the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable.
    • 翻译模型: Uses tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B by default; automatically downloaded upon first run.

1.5 One-click Initialization for New Machines (Optional)#

If you are configuring a new server, you can use the built-in Onboard script to automatically configure SSH, CLI authentication, Pip dependencies, etc.

# 1. 填写 tokens/onboard.yaml (包含 SSH 密钥、API Keys 等敏感信息，请勿提交)
# 2. 运行初始化脚本
python scripts/onboard.py

This script will automatically complete: SSH configuration, Claude/Codex CLI installation and authentication, Pip Extras installation, and Rclone basic configuration.

Phase 2: Typical Usage of Each Tool#

2.1 Summarize: AI Daily/Weekly/Monthly Reports#

This tool automatically aggregates your AI conversation logs from different devices (Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, etc.) to generate statistical reports.

Prerequisites: Ensure the log export function of each AI tool is enabled, or manually export logs to the specified directory.

Typical Workflow:

  1. Stage 1: Export Conversation Logs Extract conversation logs for all unexported dates.

    python -m summarize daily export

  2. Stage 2: Sync and Merge If you have multiple devices, first sync data via scripts/sync.py, then merge daily data.

    # Sync data for all dates and merge day by day
python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

  3. Generate Reports

    # Generate a weekly report for a specific week and deploy to the blog
python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy

# Generate a monthly report for a specific month and deploy to the blog
python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

  4. One-click Full Process (Recommended) Automatically executes: Export -> Merge -> Generate Weekly Report -> Generate Monthly Report -> Deploy.

    python -m summarize auto --deploy

Tip: Uses ollama backend (local Qwen3.8-27B) by default, no API Key required. To switch, use --api claude_cli or --api anthropic.

2.2 Research: Research Assistant#

This is a powerful academic tool supporting natural language queries, deep paper analysis, researcher profiling, and citation mapping.

1. Natural Language Paper Search Automatically routes to appropriate data sources (arXiv, PubMed, etc.).

python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "找 Pieter Abbeel 最近的机器人操作论文"

2. Generate Complete Research Weekly Reports Executes the full process: Search -> Three-stage LLM evaluation (Fast screening -> Deep evaluation -> Citation impact) -> Report generation.

python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project

3. Researcher Profiling Obtains a scholar’s papers and citation data to generate trajectory analysis, scores, and mentor-student relationships.

python tools/research/research_scout.py profile "Sergey Levine"

4. Citation Mapping Analysis Based on arXiv ID or DOI, analyzes forward citations and backward references.

python tools/research/research_scout.py citations 2301.12597

5. Deploy Reports to Blog

python tools/research/research_scout.py deploy

2.3 Benchmark: Performance Benchmarking#

Measures CPU/GPU FLOPS performance, supporting NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU).

Note: The Benchmark command must be executed in the tools/benchmark/ directory.

1. Run All Benchmarks Results will be appended to a CSV file (supports multi-hardware accumulation).

cd tools/benchmark
python -m benchmark.cli

2. Test CPU or GPU Only

python -m benchmark.cli --cpu-only
python -m benchmark.cli --gpu-only

3. Generate HTML Report

python -m benchmark.cli --report

4. Generate Report and Deploy to Blog Publishes benchmark results to the /benchmark/ path of the Hugo website.

python -m benchmark.cli --report --deploy

View report: Visit https://tzj2006.github.io/benchmark/

2.4 Website: Hugo Blog Automation#

This tool is responsible for integrating content generated by other tools (daily reports, weekly reports, charts) into the blog, and handling media compression and bilingual translation.

1. Update Blog (Compress + Build + Deploy) This is the core command; it performs incremental compression (only processing new files), Hugo build, and pushes to GitHub Pages.

# macOS / Linux
cd tools/website && bash update.sh

# Windows
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

2. Local Preview Starts the Hugo development server locally to view drafts and recent changes.

cd tools/website
hugo server -D

Note: -D indicates including Drafts.

3. Translation Mechanism The Website tool has a built-in translation engine. During the build process, it automatically detects bilingual content and calls a local model (default tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B) for translation.

  • Default backend: ollama
  • Alternative backends: vllm (Linux), transformers (Windows)
  • Models are downloaded automatically; no manual configuration required.

2.5 Translator: Local Document Translation#

Provides a Web interface for translating local files (.md, .pdf, .docx, images, etc.) while preserving Markdown formatting.

1. Start Translation Service

# 确保已安装 translator 依赖: pip install -e ".[translator]"
python -m translator

The Gradio interface will automatically open in your browser after starting.

2. How to Use

  1. Open the local address in your browser (usually http://127.0.0.1:7860).
  2. Upload a file or input text.
  3. Select the source language and target language (supports auto auto-detection).
  4. Click Translate.
  5. Copy the result or download the translated file.Advanced Configuration:
  • Model Switching: tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B is used by default. You can switch models via the model management interface in the GUI, or by setting the environment variable GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL.
  • Backend Switching: ollama is prioritized by default. If Ollama is not installed, it will automatically fall back to transformers (Windows) or vllm (Linux). You can also force a specific backend via GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND.

Phase 3: Operations and Data Synchronization#

3.1 Data Synchronization (Rclone)#

If you are developing across multiple devices, you can use the built-in synchronization scripts.

# 查看同步状态
python scripts/sync.py status

# 推送本地更改到云端
python scripts/sync.py push

# 从云端拉取最新数据
python scripts/sync.py pull

Configuration is located in the sync section of config.json.

3.2 Smoke Test#

Before running the full workflow, you can quickly check if the environment is configured correctly (read-only operation, does not consume LLM Tokens).

bash scripts/smoke.sh

3.3 Output Directory Management#

All generated artifacts (logs, reports, charts, cache) are stored in the outputs/ directory.

  • This directory is ignored by .gitignore.
  • If outputs/ is deleted, all reports can be reconstructed by re-running the corresponding tool’s generate command.

FAQ#

Q: How do I use different LLM backends? A: Most tools support the --api parameter.

  • ollama (Default): Runs locally, no Key required, Qwen3.8-27B is recommended.
  • claude_cli: Reuses the Claude Code login state, no additional API Key required.
  • anthropic: Uses Anthropic API Key.
  • openai: Uses OpenAI API Key. Global default values can be set via the environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND.

Q: Why is translation so slow/failing? A: Translation uses local inference.

  1. Ensure Ollama is running and the model has been pulled (ollama pull tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B).
  2. If Ollama is unavailable, the program will fall back to transformers (high CPU/memory consumption) or vllm (GPU).
  3. Check if the GADGET_TRANSLATION_BACKEND environment variable correctly points to your installed backend.

Q: Blog deployment failed? A:

  1. Check the Hugo path and Git configuration in config.json.
  2. Ensure the tools/website/public/ directory is an independent Git repository (usually managed automatically by scripts; do not manually git add files under this directory to the main repository).
  3. View the build logs in outputs/logs/.

Q: How do I back up? A: Your source code is in Git. For your data (conversation logs, CSV benchmark data, generated reports), it is recommended to keep them outside the outputs/ directory or sync them to the cloud via scripts/sync.py. The tokens/ directory contains sensitive information; please back it up yourself and never commit it to Git.

End of tutorial. Happy using! If you have more questions, please refer to TUTORIAL.md and the documentation under each tool’s directory.

Below is the Project Summary and Detailed Usage Tutorial organized based on the provided README content.

Part 1: Project Summary#

1. What is it?#

Gadget is a practical toolkit for developers, primarily serving daily development workflows. Its core functions include:

  • AI Report Generation: Automatically summarizes AI conversation logs and generates daily/weekly/monthly reports.
  • Academic Research Assistance: Paper discovery, researcher profiling, and citation network construction.
  • Performance Benchmarking: Cross-platform (CPU/GPU) performance benchmarking tools.
  • Blog Automation: A blog building and auto-publishing system based on Hugo, supporting media compression and local translation.
  • Document Translation: A local document translation web application based on Gradio.

The project adopts a modular design where each tool runs independently, shares underlying infrastructure (common), and relies on an independent external repository ai-companion to provide development workflows and code change tracking.

2. Repository Structure#

gadget/
├── tools/              # 五个独立的工具模块（核心功能）
│   ├── summarize/      # AI 对话日报/周报/月报生成
│   ├── research/       # 论文发现、研究者分析与引用图谱
│   ├── benchmark/      # CPU/GPU 性能基准测试
│   ├── website/        # Hugo 博客系统（含自动化构建与发布）
│   └── translator/     # Gradio 文档翻译器
├── common/             # 共享基础设施包 (LLM调用、缓存、IO、翻译、Hugo部署等)
├── scripts/            # 运维与维护脚本 (同步、新机配置、烟雾测试等)
├── docs/               # 设计文档、ECL计划、审计报告及历史归档
├── outputs/            #所有生成的产物（报告、日志、缓存），已被 gitignore
├── AGENTS.md           # AI Agent 工作流协议
├── CLAUDE.md           # Claude Code 仓库指南
└── pyproject.toml      # Python 打包配置

Key Dependencies:

  • ai-companion: Located in the parent directory ../ai-companion/, providing code change tracking, planning/execution workflows, and skills, integrated into this project via hooks.

3. What does each tool do?#

Tool Directory Core Function Key Technologies/Stack
tools/summarize/ AI Conversation Report Generation:
Reads AI conversation logs from multiple devices to generate structured daily/weekly/monthly reports. Uses ccusage to track token usage. Supports local Ollama, Claude CLI, Anthropic, and OpenAI backends.		 Claude/OpenAI API, ccusage 20.x, matplotlib
tools/research/ Academic Research Assistant:
1. Paper Discovery: Searches arXiv/PubMed, etc., and generates weekly reports.
2. Deep Insights: Analyzes article structure, writing strategies, and core knowledge.
3. Researcher Profiling: Analyzes researcher trajectories and mentor-student relationships.
4. Citation Mapping: Analyzes forward/backward citations.		 arXiv/bioRxiv/PubMed, Semantic Scholar, LLM
tools/benchmark/ Performance Benchmarking:
Cross-platform CPU/GPU FLOPS testing. Supports NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (MPS), and Intel (XPU). Outputs CSV results and interactive HTML leaderboards that can be deployed to the blog.		 PyTorch, NumPy, Plotly
tools/website/ Hugo Blog Automation:
A blog based on the PaperMod theme. Automatically performs incremental compression of images/videos, local model translation, and one-click builds/publishes to GitHub Pages. Automatically generates tool report pages.		 Hugo, pngquant, HandBrakeCLI, Python (translation)
tools/translator/ Document Translator:
Gradio Web UI. Supports Markdown format preservation for text and files (.md/.txt/.pdf/.docx/images). Uses local model inference without relying on cloud APIs.		 Gradio, GGUF/transformers/vLLm/Ollama

Part 2: Detailed Chinese Usage Tutorial#

This tutorial is intended for users encountering this project for the first time. Please operate strictly according to the information provided in the README.

1. Environment Preparation#

Before installation, please ensure the following basic environment requirements are met:

  • Python: Version 3.10+. Using a conda environment AI (conda activate AI) is recommended.
  • Node.js: Version 18+ (only for the standalone ai-companion repository; the core tools in this repo primarily depend on Python).
  • Git: Used for cloning code.

Pre-check (Smoke Test): During the configuration process, you can run the following command to perform a read-only smoke test to ensure there are no errors:

bash scripts/smoke.sh

2. Installation and Initialization#

Step 1: Clone the Repository and Prepare Dependencies#

Assuming the ai-companion repository already exists in your working directory.

  1. Clone the Gadget repository (if not already cloned):

    git clone <gadget_repo_url>
cd gadget

  2. Install the shared infrastructure package (common) and all core tool dependencies: The README indicates that common is the foundation, while each tool is installed as an extra. To cover summarize, research, benchmark, and website, it is recommended to install the all extra package.

    Note: translator is not included in all and must be installed separately.

    # Install common and dependencies for summarize/research/benchmark/website
pip install -e ".[all]"

# If you need to use the Translator tool, execute additionally:
pip install -e ".[translator]"

  3. Configure AI Companion (Workflow Engine): The Gadget development workflow depends on the parent directory ../ai-companion/. Please ensure this directory exists and has been correctly initialized. Refer to ../ai-companion/scripts/install.ts for specific installation steps.

Step 2: Configuration Files and Keys#

  1. Create Configuration Files: All tool settings are located in config.json in the root directory (this file is gitignored).

    # Copy example configuration and modify it
cp config.example.json config.json
    • The configuration file path can be specified via the environment variable GADGET_CONFIG.

  2. Manage Keys (Tokens): API keys and onboarding information are stored in the tokens/ directory (which is gitignored; never commit this to Git).

    • API Keys: Place them in the corresponding locations under tokens/.
    • Onboarding Sheet: Fill out tokens/onboard.yaml for one-click machine configuration.

  3. Set LLM Backend: By default, ollama is used (local, no Key required, uses Qwen3.8-27B). Global switching can be done via the environment variable GADGET_LLM_BACKEND or by setting it in config.json. Supported values: ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, openai.

3. Detailed Tool Usage#

A. Summarize: AI Conversation Report Generation#

Scenario: Automatically summarize AI conversations from multiple devices to generate daily/weekly reports. Architecture: Two-stage (Export -> Merge/Generate).1. Phase 1: Export unexported date data bash python -m summarize daily export

  1. Phase 2: Sync all dates and merge daily data

    python -m summarize daily merge --sync-all

  2. Generate weekly reports

    • Specify a specific week (e.g., Week 12 of 2026): 
      python -m summarize weekly generate --week 2026-W12 --deploy
    • The --deploy parameter will publish the report to the Hugo blog.

  3. Generate monthly reports

    • Specify a specific month (e.g., February 2026): 
      python -m summarize monthly generate --month 2026-02 --deploy

  4. One-click full process Execute the complete pipeline: Export -> Merge -> Weekly/Monthly report generation -> Deployment.

    python -m summarize auto --deploy

Tip: Backend switching uses the --api parameter (such as --api openai), specifically supporting ollama, claude_cli, anthropic, openai.

B. Research: Academic Research Assistant#

Entry Command: python tools/research/research_scout.py

  1. Full Pipeline: Paper Search and Report Generation

    python tools/research/research_scout.py report --project my-project
# Workflow: Search -> Three-stage evaluation (Fast screening -> Deep evaluation -> Citation impact) -> Generate report

  2. Natural Language Paper Search

    python tools/research/research_scout.py ask "Find recent robot manipulation papers by Pieter Abbeel"
# Automatically routes to appropriate data sources (arXiv/PubMed, etc.)

C. Benchmark: Performance Benchmarking#

Note: All commands must be executed in the tools/benchmark/ directory.

cd tools/benchmark

  1. Run all tests (CPU + GPU) Results are appended to a CSV and will not overwrite old data.

D. Website: Hugo Blog Management#

Directory: tools/website/

  1. Local Preview (Development Mode)

    cd tools/website
hugo server -D

  2. Build and deploy to GitHub Pages (macOS/Linux) This script performs incremental media compression, Hugo build, and push.

    bash update.sh

  3. Build and deploy to GitHub Pages (Windows)

    powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/website/update.ps1

Important Warning: tools/website/public/ is an independent deployment repository. Do not perform git commit directly on this directory; it is managed automatically by scripts.

E. Translator: Document Translator#

Scenario: Translate Markdown, PDF, and other files via Web UI while preserving formatting.

  1. Start Gradio Interface

    python -m translator
# The browser will open automatically (or visit localhost:7860)

  2. Configure Default Model Uses tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B by default; it will be downloaded automatically on the first run. Can be overridden via the GADGET_TRANSLATION_MODEL environment variable.

  3. Backend Switching Ollama is prioritized by default. On Windows, it falls back to transformers; on Linux, vLLm or GGUF can be configured.

4. Operations and Maintenance (Scripts)#

Data Sync (Sync)#

Used for synchronizing data generated by summarize/website/research, etc., across multiple devices.

# 推送数据
python scripts/sync.py push

# 拉取数据
python scripts/sync.py pull

# 查看状态

Onboarding (New Machine Setup)#

For new machines, fill out tokens/onboard.yaml and then run:

python scripts/onboard.py

This will automatically complete SSH, CLI authentication, pip dependency installation, and rclone bootstrap.

Server-level One-click Deployment#

System-level installation (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) for Ubuntu servers is located in the ai-companion repository:

bash ../ai-companion/scripts/onboard-server.sh --help
# 示例用法 (需传入 ai-companion 路径)

5. Outputs and Precautions#

  • All generated files are located in the outputs/ directory (logs, reports, cache, etc.), which has been added to .gitignore.
  • Do not commit:
    • Any content under outputs/.
    • Keys under tokens/.
    • tools/website/public/ (it is an independent repository).
    • build/ and gadget.egg-info/.
    • Data synchronized via rclone.
  • LLM Backend Switching: Can be set globally via the GADGET_LLM_BACKEND environment variable, or by using the --api parameter in various tool commands.

By following these steps, you can fully run all core tools in the Gadget project. For detailed advanced configurations (such as specific tool JSON formats or more CLI parameters), please refer to the TUTORIAL.md or README.md under each tool’s directory.
